clean_body: Add your name: No president is above the law = On day one as Attorney General, Todd Blanche’s Justice Department released a memo attempting to shield the President’s actions from future and retroactive investigations. It's illegal and unconstitutional. The memo argues that executive privilege can cover confidential presidential communications with private advisers. In practice, that could give Trump and his allies a new excuse to resist congressional subpoenas and obstruct future investigations. This is not an abstract legal debate. Congress has a constitutional duty to investigate corruption, expose abuses of power, and hold the executive branch accountable. A president cannot be allowed to create a blanket shield against scrutiny — especially one designed to reach backward and forward at the same time. As the top Democrat on the House Oversight Committee, I know exactly what is at stake when an administration tries to place itself beyond accountability. House Democrats will fight this in the courts. We will defend Congress’s oversight authority, the separation of powers, and the basic principle that the law applies to everyone. you for standing up for accountability. Robert Garcia = P.S. As the top Democrat on the House Oversight Committee, I’ll have subpoena power to finally hold the Trump Administration accountable — but only if we win back Congress this November. = = * Paid for by Robert Garcia for Congress Robert Garcia for Congress 65 Pine Ave #348 Long Beach, CA 90802 United States This email was sent to . **Last night, tens of thousands of Alaskans sent a clear message: We are ready for change.**

I’m so grateful for every Alaska voter who made their voice heard yesterday and cast their ballot for our movement. And I’m committed, over the next 76 days, to bringing as many Alaskans as we can into this fight with us.

From day one, this campaign has been about all Alaskans, regardless of where they live or who they vote for. That’s just as true today as ever.

Alongside our unique open primary system, Alaska also has ranked choice voting in the general. That means in November, voters will be able to rank up to four Senate candidates – myself, incumbent Republican Senator Dan Sullivan, and two others who will be determined in the coming days – in their order of preference.

**[This system rewards bipartisanship. Ted Stevens often said, to hell with politics, put Alaska first. Ranked choice voting encourages that mindset, and that’s exactly why I’m running. And I’m committed, over the next 76 days, to bringing as many Alaskans as we can into this fight with us. From day one, this campaign has been about all Alaskans, regardless of where they live or who they vote for. That’s just as true today as ever. Alongside our unique open primary system, Alaska also has ranked choice voting in the general. That means in November, voters will be able to rank up to four Senate candidates – myself, incumbent Republican Senator Dan Sullivan, and two others who will be determined in the coming days – in their order of preference. = = We are in a moral moment that needs real leadership. But instead, incumbent Senator Dan Sullivan has repeatedly taken votes that are injurious to Alaskans. He voted more than ten times for the Iran war, which is driving up our costs. He supported gutting healthcare, public radio, disaster relief, and veterans’ benefits. And he was revealed as the top recipient of corporate trawling industry donations in the Senate. He exemplifies what’s wrong in DC – a rigged system that puts corporate greed and self-serving politicians before the people. That’s why I’m running: Because Alaskans need an independent voice in the Senate who will stand up to anyone to put Alaska first, not DC special interests or billionaire donors. Last night’s result was a product of months of traveling to every corner of the state, and while I wouldn’t do anything differently, that means we’re heading into the general election with a huge cash-on-hand disadvantage. = = With all of you, we can win this November. Thank you! \- Mary | | | | | | | Resist Reclaim Rebuild is an organization committed to helping Democrats win up and down the ballot, nationwide. body:
170 Texas public schools have closed under Abbott.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
Here's a number that should keep every Texan up at night: **170.**
**That's how many public schools have closed in Texas over the last three years alone — under Greg Abbott's leadership.**
**170 schools.** Gone. Not because they weren't needed, not because communities didn't want them — but because Greg Abbott and his administration have failed our students, our teachers, and our families.
Every closed school represents kids who lost their classrooms. Teachers who lost their jobs. Communities that lost their future. **And Abbott's plan will be more of the same if reelected.**
Texas public schools simply cannot afford another four years of Greg Abbott.
That's why I'm running for governor — to fight for our schools, our students, and the future of this state. To fully fund public education, respect our teachers, and make sure every child in Texas has access to a quality education.
But I can't do it alone._I need you with me._
**[Will you chip in $5 or whatever you can today to help us defeat Greg Abbott and give Texas public schools the leadership they deserve?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260820_3_schools.2FWnMq&refcode=em20260820-1886&amount=5&t=1&akid=1886%2E299639%2EIJJTQg)**

This is not a dry legal history. It is the story of a man born into crushing poverty in segregated Georgia. A man who was raised by a grandfather who worked him from dawn to dark and taught him that no one was coming to save him. A man who flirted with radical Left-wing politics as a young man and walked away from it. A man who studied to be a priest and ended up on the highest Court in the land. And a man who has spent thirty years insisting on one simple, radical idea: To celebrate the launch, I'm offering an opportunity to receive your copy while supporting this work: that **the Constitution -- not the personal views of nine justices -- is the highest law in this country.** For that, the Left has never forgiven him. I spent hours and hours interviewing Justice Thomas one-on-one for this book. It is wide-ranging. Very personal. Completely unguarded. He talks about the confirmation hearings. He talks about the years in the wilderness when even Conservatives kept their distance. He talks about what it cost to be right when everyone in the room is telling you that you are wrong. Team, Donald Trump has vowed to “nationalize” our elections by targeting mail-in voting... _And yet, he utilizes mail-in voting for his own gain._ | [ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137627744/641429507/1071238059?refcode=em-8.20.26-all-a-2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS84OTkxNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3MDg1ZjMwOC1mZTljLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=EsWtSQta73H62XiVGGlsskZWAujBTvn3R7pvBKEx5ho=) **Trump votes by mail again in his home state of Florida**
---
The White House is trying to spin this by calling Trump’s vote “a non-story.” But let’s lay out the facts:
When he spoke to millions last month, Trump called vote by mail _“inherently corrupt.”_
He’s repeatedly called on his Justice Department to _rig the system and force Federal control_ over who can and can’t receive a ballot in the mail – _despite the Constitution prohibiting the President from controlling our elections._
And in spite of all of this, Trump has voted by mail in Florida’s elections _twice this year._
It’s more than a “non-story,” team. This is about an administration who will rig the game in their favor at our expense – whether it’s weaponizing our federal government or having Trump’s allies run to be Secretaries of State across the country.

subject: AITKEN: ICE Was There to Protect Taunton. No One Let Them.
body:
| | | | |
---
| | [](https://qgzxgy5ab.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001cJzyMYV4G2bWmFvv6cMTkRepSg0065kRtM7NlzErHt_O8Qe30aQzXc9daR-S1pOzUeoXH67KyXS1Jk837EQOQ_As3lQP9QDO-TpAU5vtRxWvblQ-tDnsKSsH0IM5nAqL2XV_rJTBu69vzMzjyDoVQQ==&c=oR2r5mW1Xq_PSLEbvO_HnQLbYx9sYIO2Bj67R_HSiAKAwJGyBuAMnw==&ch=nRGt-kk2bKRkSI7f8isv27rszs4xP0CvHntXlTWdYzPWDrFP7nNuxA==)
---
---
| NOTE: The following Op-Ed is being distributed for Seth Aitken for Bristol County District Attorney
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE CONTACT: Vincent Errichetti 617 922 1824
ICE Was There to Protect Taunton. No One Let Them
If Massachusetts agencies had simply notified ICE before releasing Heriton Da Silva Aredes after any of his prior arrests, he would have been in federal custody instead of behind the wheel on Court Street; cooperation that costs nothing would have prevented the crosswalk killing.
Here is the story.
Heriton DaSilva Aredes is a Brazilian national with a substantial record of criminal convictions who previously entered into the United States illegally and was removed by Immigration in 2008.
From 2023, when he was arrested for driving without a license, until recently, Heriton DaSilva Aredes was apparently living in Taunton.
On the morning of November 20, 2024, Mr. Aredes was driving a borrowed motor vehicle, accelerated in front of a school bus on Court Street by the Taunton Green and killed a pedestrian in a cross walk. He was charged with Motor Vehicle Homicide in August 2025 and scheduled to be arraigned in Taunton District Court in November 2025.
Mr. Aredes did not show up for his arraignment. He was arrested on a default warrant more than a month later and, following that arraignment, was held on $2,500 cash bail. For the next seven+ months, unable to make bail, Mr. Aredes was held at the Bristol County House of Correction while his case progressed in the Taunton District Court. Mr. Aredes was transported to court in custody on July 23, 2026 and two days later, somehow posted bail and was released from the House of Correction. Despite a federal immigration detainer having been filed with the Bristol County Sheriff, the Sheriff elected not to notify immigration officials that Mr. Aredes had posted bail and released him back into society.
He was taken into custody by ICE on August 6, 2026.
Recently, Bristol County Sheriff Paul Heorux has claimed that Massachusetts law prevents his office from complying with Immigration detainers. While politically convenient, this is untrue. The Sheriff cites the 2017 court case of Lunn v. Commonwealth as cover for his decision to ignore ICE. The Lunn case stands for the proposition that law enforcement, including court officers, are prohibited from holding an individual solely on the basis of a federal civil immigration detainer.
An immigration detainer requests two things from any law enforcement agency holding someone in custody: 1) 48 hours of additional detention to give immigration officials time to arrive and take the person into custody or 2) advance notice before a person is scheduled to be released. While the Lunn case prohibits compliance with the first request - extended detention, nothing prohibits a sheriff's department from giving courtesy notice to ICE before an alien subject to removal is released back into the public.
The Bristol Sheriff's Office could have easily and lawfully given Immigration officials notice that Mr. Aredes was arranging to make bail. Instead, the Sheriff chose to take a progressive political stand by ignoring the immigration detainer and putting the public at risk. Mr. Aredes' criminal record was available to the Sheriff. The Sheriff knew Mr. Aredes had killed someone with a car and he knew that when given the opportunity, Mr. Aredes would very likely disappear and not show up to court. Most importantly, the Sheriff would have known that Mr. Aredes had been previously removed from the United States and had re-entered, a felony under federal law.
Perhaps, most important of all, the Sheriff was very likely aware that in the years preceding Mr. Aredes' motor vehicle homicide charge, he had been arrested several times by different Massachusetts law enforcement agencies and each time, either in defiance or ignorance of an immigration detainer, was released before ICE could respond. Had any of those agencies honored the detainer, if only to give ICE sufficient notice of Mr. Aredes' imminent release, the man who Mr. Aredes killed in that Taunton crosswalk might still be alive.
Here, knowing all that - fully aware of the harm that could have previously been avoided with a modicum of cooperation and communication - the Bristol County sheriff still followed through on his promise to ignore ICE efforts and released Heriton DaSilva Aredes to an unsuspecting public.
Whether motivated by politics or arrogance, the Sheriff's choice only served to make Bristol County less safe and serves as a startling example of what can happen when progressive politicians care more about indulging their hatred of conservative ideals than they care about their sworn duty to protect the innocent.

---

body:
August 8th, 2008, the worst day of my life, changed how I see everything: from family to the importance of our rural communities and it is a key part of why I am running for office.
| | | | | [](https://eub669hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001JQ2hd8tZhGYX7W7MNFban8-tak0D8oiybanQDwai8CHYdvvDlYtDcF_tkXWBITaR4yKA1V4hRcVHCd29LKf2YZeJZRUNHJZmUvHwXSjjysM4guPtIc44Tpzc5rrQA1Ijt9zPLsd7FegkFFnc_xjkjvWRxMHxQNC1dobPbfT6ffln1TL3U-24IN-9h7dojzrs2hPI4baC1oNm6sIzr2oyZtyk9TWNzy6S&c=nYSahziFzaQ6eIGn1zqz7AYVoWRCw_9UVg07bbxd8h8o97STElxA6w==&ch=L5d132k9QWUTJLvlgfZz_4AjYuh0cmIbFw-qUdBNlX7-L9dYyMUgug==)
---
| Peter,
August 8, 2009, is a date I will never forget.
Just days before his 19th birthday, my son Justin was out in the fields with us, doing what this family has done for over three generations--farming the Louisiana delta. A breakdown in our combine left corn spilled across the ground, and as we worked to recover it, Justin got too close. In an instant, his pant leg was caught, and the thresher pulled him in.
I can still hear his voice: "Dad, get me out."
And there was nothing I could do.
---
| [](https://eub669hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001JQ2hd8tZhGYX7W7MNFban8-tak0D8oiybanQDwai8CHYdvvDlYtDcF_tkXWBITaR4yKA1V4hRcVHCd29LKf2YZeJZRUNHJZmUvHwXSjjysM4guPtIc44Tpzc5rrQA1Ijt9zPLsd7FegkFFnc_xjkjvWRxMHxQNC1dobPbfT6ffln1TL3U-24IN-9h7dojzrs2hPI4baC1oPPlfbu5RCdsmHSdDDO-_rc&c=nYSahziFzaQ6eIGn1zqz7AYVoWRCw_9UVg07bbxd8h8o97STElxA6w==&ch=L5d132k9QWUTJLvlgfZz_4AjYuh0cmIbFw-qUdBNlX7-L9dYyMUgug==)
---
My son and I on the farm in 2021.
Multiple miracles occurred that day: When it initially happened he wasn't in pain because his nerves were pinched so tightly in the machine. Nor was he bleeding because he was caught so tight in there.
It took the jaws of life to tear apart that machine and when the metal finally gave way he let out a scream that I will never forget for the rest of my life.
The paramedics quickly sprang into action and he was airlifted to Jackson, Mississippi, where Doctors fought to save his leg, but the injury and infection from all the dirt and debris were too severe. Justin lost his leg from below the knee.
That day could have broken us. Instead, it showed me what makes Louisiana strong.
Neighbors, first responders from two parishes (what we call counties in Louisiana), and a doctor who wasn't even on duty, Dr. Ron Gregg, a farmer himself and longtime family friend -- showed up because that's what rural communities do. They take care of each other. They don't ask if it's their job or jurisdiction. They just show up.
Today, Justin is 35. He runs our farm. He's built a life, with a fiancee and a family of his own. He still hunts, fishes, and works the land -- just with a prosthetic leg and the same determination that carried him through that day.
But the truth is, the kind of community that saved Justin is disappearing. Rural hospitals are closing. Doctors like Dr. Gregg--who live in our communities, who know our families--are harder to find. Too many of our kids feel like they have to leave home to build a future.
And my family, who first worked this Louisiana delta soil as sharecroppers, and now as farmers who own this land, have put too much blood into this soil for us to leave and go somewhere else.
I have to take a stand and fight for our way of life and it's why I am proud to be the Democrat running for Senate in Louisiana.
If you believe in that fight, I'm asking you to stand with me today. A Democratic win here is the first step in taking our state back from the far-right whose policies of atomization and vicious corporatism are tearing our communities apart.
And mark my words, a win is possible, Democrats just won a deep red special election here by a landslide. [The blue wave will wash over Louisiana and we will flip this seat but only if we fight for it. Will you please make a contribution of $25, $10, or even just $5 to help us in our fight to restore the Louisiana that we love so dearly.](https://eub669hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001JQ2hd8tZhGYX7W7MNFban8-tak0D8oiybanQDwai8CHYdvvDlYtDcF_tkXWBITaRmVUwZ085GEnjwaY-kpa1wr0QG5G3iB9h_LvDR6nURrDNyTlePLu2k5VkHdjpPFKT4WcfY59lhXqi3tloTkaQcxy34jE1NY1L7SU3ceJqVIrZJFz_oRR6nljbwBgC2kT5w-9t6T-DosADFIzhg2EKPxJhErBfrG-GmeRjKyec-C8=&c=nYSahziFzaQ6eIGn1zqz7AYVoWRCw_9UVg07bbxd8h8o97STElxA6w==&ch=L5d132k9QWUTJLvlgfZz_4AjYuh0cmIbFw-qUdBNlX7-L9dYyMUgug==)

| | Friends,
As I traveled through the UP last weekend, I couldn't help but think about the wonderful place it is. Unfortunately, it has found itself in our current Attorney General's crosshairs over exactly what I will eliminate from the office when I'm elected: Politics.
For years, the need to build a tunnel to house the new pipeline has been held up with litigation and political lawsuits by our Attorney General. Despite there being an environmental review process to decide whether a project like Line 5 poses too much of a risk to our habitat to be built, Dana Nessel has sued to stop just to appease her political base.
This is a dangerous game for the Attorney General to play. Line 5 doesn't just move oil through a pipe -- it supplies roughly half the propane used to heat homes across the Upper Peninsula, along with the crude that keeps regional refineries running and gas prices in check.
We are already dealing with an affordability crisis as energy costs skyrocket and these lawsuits put Michiganders at risk of paying even more for energy needed to live.
The most frustrating part of this effort to stop Line 5 is that the opponents aren't saying what we should do instead.
Filing a lawsuit to stop something as critical as supplying energy to Michiganders without offering alternative supply solutions does not serve the citizens. It serves your political ambition. We should embrace projects like Line 5 that will provide Northern Michigan and the Upper Peninsula with reliable, affordable energy instead of scoring political points by obstructing them.
That is why when I am Attorney General, I will withdraw the lawsuits and allow the process to ensure citizen safety and to protect our environment can proceed. And if the project passes all its reviews and construction begins, I will work with local communities and Enbridge to ensure all laws are being followed. If an issue comes up during construction, I will work with all involved to try and solve them without costly lawsuits.
This represents one of the starkest differences between me and my opponent. Eli Savit will no doubt play politics and fight Line 5, spend taxpayer money on countless lawsuits, and continue to put Michiganders at risk. His guiding light as a prosecutor has been politics, not the law.
I believe Michigan has had enough of that after 8 years of Dana Nessel. I hope you'll share my vision of a politics-free Attorney General office with your family and friends.
This weekend I will be at the Michigan Republican Party's state convention in Mt. Pleasant where we will officially nominate our statewide candidates. We have a great ticket who will be facing off against the most dangerous slate of candidates Michigan has ever seen.
It is as important as ever that we come out our convention united and focused on protecting Michigan in November.
I will be hosting a breakfast on Saturday morning before the convention for all the delegates. clean_body: We are already dealing with an affordability crisis as energy costs skyrocket and these lawsuits put Michiganders at risk of paying even more for energy needed to live. | | | | | == | | | == | | Friends, As I traveled through the UP last weekend, I couldn't help but think about the wonderful place it is. Unfortunately, it has found itself in our current Attorney General's crosshairs over exactly what I will eliminate from the office when I'm elected: Politics. For years, the need to build a tunnel to house the new pipeline has been held up with litigation and political lawsuits by our Attorney General. Despite there being an environmental review process to decide whether a project like Line 5 poses too much of a risk to our habitat to be built, Dana Nessel has sued to stop just to appease her political base. This is a dangerous game for the Attorney General to play. Line 5 doesn't just move oil through a pipe -- it supplies roughly half the propane used to heat homes across the Upper Peninsula, along with the crude that keeps regional refineries running and gas prices in check. We are already dealing with an affordability crisis as energy costs skyrocket and these lawsuits put Michiganders at risk of paying even more for energy needed to live. The most frustrating part of this effort to stop Line 5 is that the opponents aren't saying what we should do instead. Filing a lawsuit to stop something as critical as supplying energy to Michiganders without offering alternative supply solutions does not serve the citizens. It serves your political ambition. We should embrace projects like Line 5 that will provide Northern Michigan and the Upper Peninsula with reliable, affordable energy instead of scoring political points by obstructing them. That is why when I am Attorney General, I will withdraw the lawsuits and allow the process to ensure citizen safety and to protect our environment can proceed. And if the project passes all its reviews and construction begins, I will work with local communities and Enbridge to ensure all laws are being followed. If an issue comes up during construction, I will work with all involved to try and solve them without costly lawsuits. This represents one of the starkest differences between me and my opponent. Eli Savit will no doubt play politics and fight Line 5, spend taxpayer money on countless lawsuits, and continue to put Michiganders at risk. His guiding light as a prosecutor has been politics, not the law. I believe Michigan has had enough of that after 8 years of Dana Nessel. I hope you'll share my vision of a politics-free Attorney General office with your family and friends. This weekend I will be at the Michigan Republican Party's state convention in Mt. Pleasant where we will officially nominate our statewide candidates. We have a great ticket who will be facing off against the most dangerous slate of candidates Michigan has ever seen. It is as important as ever that we come out our convention united and focused on protecting Michigan in November. I will be hosting a breakfast on Saturday morning before the convention for all the delegates. You can get more ==. I hope to see you there. Folks are tired of hearing our leaders talk about making it even harder for them to cast their vote by mail.

## Army Resumes Apache Flights after Crash
The Army resumed [Apache helicopter training flights](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL3OozAQAJ8GOiP_EMNXuLgm3XftlWix13gVg5G9F5K3P-Ve4etHo9H8-V6-gTId22_Y0fErluXAq2VkxrqcwJX8g6FuyG2rcCbyaymPRUtthZyFVgt4picuI_TBrTJ8qR6dmubJKKmU7ZNbg0d7Q_M1otJyhFsI2vh1jABGYZx6ch-dnLVSSqqbGVAqb22YlUHrvZm7UWIgLnXghIwvaDG_yxPr4MveZ5eYz9aZX52-d_p-XdewUyaG-v4Anb5D3d-iYvu7YxOQhB0FnOATiphpSyy4Ah10bAIiYxURGLKIpbJIpQThK7TUVxfOi3KmZqdulNsOlP8X8E_PPZ3-FwAA__9XN4av) on Wednesday, a week after a crash near Salado killed two Fort Hood pilots. Army leaders [grounded the training flights Aug. 14](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDGupDAQRE8DmUduA8YEBJuQ_U03RG27AWuMjeze4f_br2ausFEFT1XSqz9f6xeGGNL-G0-a-XvLa6K7RmKmsl7IJbgnY9mJ617wOoKzOT9XJZUW0ggFKzoOL1p7bP1spZ-gpRlGM3YgAXR7zKBp8JuySk2dARxt74zvjd4mbSf0Yxvm95w0CgAkDN2DJDitvYGOtHOdaXpJPnAuDz6I6RvrFn_yi8rD5bON88F81ab71ailUct934-no8SvN27UgoWDi9So5e32DuSQE8YPO39Eofr3pCrwQneQ2GLYDxZcMKSQdpEvKp9GFZUxeeHznUQunkqjlkFKMeqx9-BAbAAg-qGfhJWDEsYr46TdhmGybZn9dYcYQ9Vj08v9xBA_Avy_x79m9S8AAP__WP6YJg), and then lifted the stand-down "after a thorough review of safety procedures and flight operations." The Combat Readiness Center at Fort Rucker, Alabama, is still investigating the cause. Chief Warrant Officer 2 Deontre Huey, 34, of Killeen, and Warrant Officer Seth Olmstead, 25, of Belton, were [the only two aboard](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDuOqzAUhlcDnSM_iE0KF7ehy22i0ZTI2MdwFIORfSaP3Y_IFqb9P-l_fV_Hq8OE2_zfrWDpFfO4wbMmIIIy7o4K-ju5MgPVubh9QT_lfB8ll5rxnkkxOk_4gLFzbbATDxfRghWmN0pwIXS7WIiqC1MEMYXYGWO86YNTOp5F6KKJukV72PFeCiG4OKsTcOG1Dr1QoL1XfdNxCEi5nGgBgperMb3zA8rJ57VNdiHaa6P-NXJo5OAmf2w4WCOHr1sjhycWuFEu7wOX9c0K1J8VKnO78wuwBRL6vBMURsXhhtvMVqwV81aZix_9iGVCnc2FK8nbYsP-xJSwatN0fF4dpk8d-uuNDyt_AwAA___yAIpR) when the helicopter went down Aug. 12 during a maintenance test flight. The crash sparked a fire that burned 155 acres in Bell County. Huey entered the Army in 2014 and Olmstead in 2023; both flew with the 1st Air Cavalry Brigade. [Huey's sister, Chassidy](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOhCAUheGnwQ7DRQexoNjGbrbd0iBchYiDgZtx5u03s6-w9Um-nPw_9_luY4qP7dseaOi15vmBV01IhGU-LZXodrJlQ6pbsWeIbsl5n6WQigvNJczWUXzi3NvGm0X4ERo0MOihAwGgmmDEqN1t1aMC6ITv-37Uo9W9GrRUYOXSRPPhhJYAIODWtSjAKeU1dKic6zTrBfpIubQUkPBl65re-YmldflokglEZ2XdF5MTk9N1Xe1-0eszMjl9bCYnoZmcYGRyWu0R05sXPPBYsFS-5kI85Ox5zclHLHyPKaHn9rQuIA-YossnYeGu2BqYnJpi_HnFlGJVA-vFdtiY_t7Qfys-jfwNAAD__yANhtI), said he was "extremely funny, incredibly creative, and simply unforgettable," and asked that he be remembered for how he lived, not how he died.
## Border Wall Fight Reaches Parks Commission
Hundreds of Texans packed the Texas Parks and Wildlife Commission's [annual hearing in Austin](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGuozAQRb_GdI5sExxSuNiG7m27JRrsAUYxNrIn8N7fr4j2D7a80tHRvffP1_gFFCktv2FDx99zHhOeNSIzlnEHLuRfDGVBrkuBfSU_5fwajTJWql4aPYJnOnC8QxPcpMJTN-j0o3-0Wmltm9XNVj-7WXUWfW8B8d7Pcxcm71sIU_tUDblLp3qjtVa6a2-otLc29LpF633bi7vCQJzLjVdk_IY6x598YLn5vDXRrcx7Fe0vYQZhhvM8bwfEiD8eExeIFyXMcA0TZqgMjPJf-MjkDuVVJaQgT4oh0ozS522jWiknLFVSeqcAjBfAq5xyCVjkCTFKn5PHkqoM70JpkZDSG6LcEJnSIszQFBf2k2Kkah_irpYN6FOp4f89_HDmbwAAAP__fMGcKA) on Wednesday to ask the agency to keep border barriers out of state parks. Ninety-nine people signed up to speak, though barriers weren't on the agenda. Cardboard cutouts of desert animals lined the walkway, reading, "No wall, no wire, no way." Chair Paul Foster told the crowd the commission agrees with most of them and is working with Gov. [Greg Abbott's office](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLHSoyAURp9GOxwuGCQFxTZ22XZL5wpXJSHiwE3Mvv1O9hX-_pvvzDl_btMNY4r7-huf5Piz5GmnsyZipjIdyCX6B2NZieta8Niin3N-TEoqI6QVCib0HN809dgGN8twhZYcDHbQIAFMuzktUQ-LvWjy9ioXXAYA34crDdgHaUMb3fdOWgUAEi66IwnemGBBk_Fe26aXFCLn0vFGTB-sS_qb31Q6n59tchvzURv9q1Fjo8bzPLslf5TZ8qty3r-jRo1fr0aN91dYSWyYuIo5rmKmPYgdOeYdkziwPMScS6AiTkxJHCXfyXNbXDjOmFKsZmh6uT4xpv90_mm1t1P_AgAA__-shITD) and the federal government to "minimize damage to the ecosystem." A federal judge set an Aug. 28 hearing in San Antonio on halting the work. Downriver, [San Ygnacio landowners sued](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGSpCAQxvGnwQyLBsfRgOASs730QquFVqlhwIJe3Xn7q5lX2OyLfvXV_9_X_IUhhrT9xSdZ_lnznOiqkZipzAdyCe7BWDbiuhU89uCWnB-zVrqXapAaZnQcTpo7bLxdlB-hIQv34W5AAfTNbsexV44GbRYDqMAvON5WfyO_YodgdBPsm1ODBgAFN9OSAtf3fgBDvXNmEJ0iHziXlndi-sG6xlc-qbQuP5tod-ajCvNH6Eno6bqu9rGl2vIp9PSmhZ7U8NlCTxWTDFtCF7I8Sj6o8EvmK1Gpsn6TfLtyycVTkRfGKF1Olcu345CT0FNTrD-uEGOo_V10antiiJ8j_NuAp9X_AwAA__8Y3oao), saying crews entered their riverfront property without notice or payment.
## Patrick Targets 'Vulgar' Books in Schools
Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick said Wednesday he'll back legislation [docking public schools a letter grade](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD2u2zAQhE9DdTT4Z0opWKRR57QphRW1lgivRYLcyPbtAwXBu8DrphgM5vt-36YbJEr7-gueGPh9z9OOr0bIjHUqwDXFB0NdkdtaoWwpzjk_JqOMl2qQRk8QOR04OeiWMKvlh-4w6H7orVZa-24LzsHVeBO98-httLPulbLXuAAsDu6uS-GcU4PRWit9tRdUOnq_DNqij9EOwilcEud64Q0Z39Du9MkH1kvMz47CxlyasD-FGYUZG-ywr0iZ0oFnQ5jxhBJmLJkSp3jGLwIlzEgs13zI_7yy1FxywyYL7kCcsMkWt5ypyeMPrVDlKaFJSnOF-ulqWMorEaXme-HU-oRE_67xd5UewfwNAAD__yCojfE) in state performance ratings if they keep graphic books on library shelves. He stood at the Capitol beside easels of [book covers](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0D2OpDAQhuHTmMwtVwEGAoJNyGbTDZF_ymC120amppm5_YrR3mDjkl7V8_35WD9MTDFvv82LZv4KZc10nYmYqa6H4Rrdk03diM-tmmOPzpbyXFGhlmqUCKtxHN-0dqbxs1V-goZmGMahBQWgm332k_JBDRjI2c6rdghaDQFMr3oHow1NnO-cGhEAFPTtgxQ4rf0ILWnn2lF0inzkUh-8E9OXOUP6Lm-qD1deTZp35uMU7S-Bi8Dluq7Hk_LZ31eBi6kcXSKBy00TuJD_dIZjyQKXn5pMLLe7l0uV3mT5Dy59rPwtb_EprcnydHspSYbP7GPeBC449jJM3llHWvbOgOy6CaTV1krVqUkHJEQ_NXX2xxVTiqceRKe2l4np53v-39XfM_4NAAD__-qjl7E) he called "so filthy, so dirty, so vulgar, so pornographic" that he refused to open them. Some, he said, are barred from state prisons. The [bill would require](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2SpSAQhZ9Gs7ZouINMQLCJ2Wy6oYXQKnVRLOjVO2-_5dR9g03756vznT9f45eLKe7Lb7eR5decx52umoiZyng4LtE_2ZWFuC7FHWv0U87PUQqpQRiQODrP8aTx4dpgJxE-sSWLvekVCkTdrlbh1BtnTK_9pNCpD499cMHr2SFR_9lGe-OEkYgo8EN1JNBrHQwq0t4r0zwEhci5dLwS08vVOX3nk0rn89YmuzIftVG_Gjk0criuq3u-3H4vGzncPo0cft7gyCly9PfgokLg8xb3BeZcgFeC261CYljyCW97uNzOFThDoS2fBCEW_n6fziVvcPydUvRQ_ZpzutFtseG4Ykqx6r55iGVzMf1k5f_t-LTyXwAAAP__bluV8Q) the Texas Education Agency to lower a campus's grade over any challenged book still on the shelf. Patrick said most school boards haven't acted under Senate Bill 13, the 2025 law that shifted book removal authority from librarians to boards. "_It's the law and we expect you to follow the law. So we're coming for the books_ ," Patrick said, adding that nothing is banned because anyone can still buy the books. Patrick presides over the Senate and faces state Rep. Vikki Goodwin, D-Austin, in November.

name: Vera Smith
subject: Speak Up: Protect millions of acres of forests by sending your comment today!
body:
Tell the Trump administration not to repeal the Roadless Area Conservation Rule!

Tell the Trump administration not to repeal the Roadless Area Conservation Rule!
                  

(https://support.defenders.org/s/5917598/38SyG9Xl)

(https://support.defenders.org/s/5917599/38SyG9Xl)

Protect America’s Remaining Intact Forests! (https://support.defenders.org/s/5917600/38SyG9Xl)

Defender,

Forty-five million acres of national forest lands – stretching from the Appalachians to the North Cascades and beyond – are protected by the Roadless Area Conservation Rule, or “Roadless Rule.”

Free from roads and clearcuts, these last intact forests are havens for many animals such as wolverines, grizzly bears, salmon, trout, flying squirrels and salamanders, to name just a few.

But these lands and their wildlife are in danger: The Trump administration just published its proposal to repeal those protections, which will open these natural forests to industrial logging.

We need to speak out now: Sign a public comment telling the Trump administration not to repeal the Roadless Rule. We have only 30 days to comment, so don’t delay! (https://support.defenders.org/s/5917601/38SyG9Xl)

Roadless areas in our national forests are critically important to wildlife, including some of our nation’s most imperiled species. These areas contain habitat for over half of all vulnerable land species in the United States.

And it’s not just animals that depend on these forests – these areas also help deliver clean water to fish-bearing streams and eventually into the faucets of many American homes. They’re also places where many Americans go to hike, fish and spend time in nature.

Repealing the Roadless Rule would compromise habitat for countless animals, and it would deprive us of some of the last places we can go to experience the natural wonders of our American forests.

The Trump administration is taking comments from the public on its proposal to repeal these protections. Before the deadline, it’s vital that we speak up to demand our forests remain protected for wildlife and future generations!

Click here to tell the Department of Agriculture to keep our national forests protected! (https://support.defenders.org/s/5917602/38SyG9Xl)

We’re so fortunate to have the incredible landscapes that define our nation. Let’s work together to stop this land grab so that our children and grandchildren can also experience the wonders of these places and the animals that live within them.

Thank you for taking action today in defense of our invaluable forests and wildlife.

Sincerely,

Vera Smith

Director National Forests & Public Lands

Defenders of Wildlife

(http://www.facebook.com/DefendersofWildlife) (http://twitter.com/defenders) (https://www.instagram.com/defendersofwildlife/?hl=en) (http://www.youtube.com/defendersofwildlife) (https://www.tiktok.com/@defendersofwildlife)

Defenders of Wildlife 1130 17th Street NW • Washington, DC 20036 defenders.org (https://defenders.org)

### Connecticut Republican Congressional Nominee Dr. Michael Goldstein sends letter to EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin seeking federal review of 8-30g, Public Act 25-1 and their potential impact on wastewater infrastructure and Long Island Sound
[Pledge your support](https://substack..qW_6w19lfin4Jpik5CC0zx8yu1_pUgtaln-PRheDO9o?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=212130644)
PRESS RELEASE:
Greenwich CT, **August 21, 2026**
Today, **Dr. Michael Goldstein, Republican nominee for Congress in Connecticut 's Fourth Congressional District, sent a letter to EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin** asking the Environmental Protection Agency to examine a problem that has been treated for too long as merely local:
**What happens when Hartford mandates development, but local communities are left with the sewer, stormwater, infrastructure and environmental consequences?**
For Goldstein, the letter represents a central principle of his campaign:
# Federal Solutions to Local Problems.
Connecticut needs housing. But Hartford should not be able to mandate or incentivize additional development without answering whether the infrastructure necessary to support that development can actually handle it.
Goldstein is asking EPA and EPA Region 1 to review Connecticut's **8-30g affordable-housing law and Public Act 25-1, formerly House Bill 8002** , in communities draining into Long Island Sound.
His argument is not that Washington should control local zoning.
It is that **Hartford cannot use state housing policy to escape federal environmental obligations.**
## From Byram Beach to Washington
The problem is visible right here in Fairfield County and Connecticut's Fourth District and in my hometown of Greenwich.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e9fb2346-0fce-4229-8375-edf4f7f8c4fb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Source: [Save the Sound](https://substack.com/redirect/76cb0a27-f261-4e61-83ad-78f6cdbc0357?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Greenwich's Board of Health reported this year that the rainfall threshold for closing Byram Beach was reduced from one-half inch to just **0.3 inches** following review of approximately a decade of testing.
The Town has investigated bacteria in the Tom's Brook watershed and undertaken sewer testing and sewer-line grouting.
Save the Sound gave Byram Beach a **D+** based on 2025 swimming-season data, with samples reportedly failing safe-swimming criteria **36 percent of the time overall** and experiencing substantially greater problems during wet weather.
That may begin as a local problem, But the water doesn't stop at the Greenwich border.
Long Island Sound connects **Greenwich, Stamford, Darien, Norwalk, Westport, Fairfield and Bridgeport** and the rest of Connecticut's coastline.
And once pollution implicates federally protected waters and federal environmental statutes, there is a federal role.
**That is what federal solutions to local problems looks like.**
## Hartford Mandates. Towns Pay.
Hartford's housing policies increasingly affect local land-use decisions. Public Act 25-1 also restricts aspects of municipal authority over off-street parking requirements for residential development.
* Hartford doesn't operate Greenwich's sewer system.
* Hartford doesn't maintain Stamford's pumping stations.
* Hartford doesn't manage stormwater in Norwalk.
* Hartford doesn't close beaches after heavy rain.

**Our municipalities and taxpayers deal with those consequences.**
_**My letter therefore asks an important question: before the state imposes additional density, shouldn 't somebody determine whether the sewer system, stormwater system, pumping stations and receiving waters can actually support it?**_
## You Cannot Measure Capacity on a Sunny Day
A wastewater plant's average daily flow does not tell the entire story.
The real test comes during heavy rain.
Goldstein argues that infrastructure capacity must account for **peak wet-weather flow, infiltration and inflow, pumping-station constraints, collection-system bottlenecks, overflow history and treatment performance**.
* Housing produces additional sanitary flow.
* Development can add impervious surfaces that prevent rainwater dissipation.
* Rain produces stormwater.
* Aging infrastructure may already experience infiltration and inflow.
* Those pressures can converge precisely when the system is under the greatest stress.
* **Infrastructure must come before mandates.**

## Taking Hartford to the EPA
Today's letter does **not** ask EPA to become a Connecticut zoning board.
It asks EPA to examine whether state-directed development in areas with documented wet-weather sewer limitations or recurring bacteria problems can create foreseeable conditions that cause or contribute to violations of the **Clean Water Act or degradation of coastal recreational waters protected under the BEACH Act**.
Goldstein specifically asks EPA to use **Byram Beach and the western Long Island Sound watershed as a case study** , while examining the broader Fourth District shoreline.
_Instead of waiting for a sewer overflow or another beach closure, government should be asking these questions**before additional infrastructure loading occurs**._
## This Is What Congress Should Do
Too often, Washington politicians talk about national issues while residents struggle with problems right outside their doors.
Goldstein's approach is different:
**Find the federal connection to the local problem --and use it.**
* _When federal environmental law can help protect a Greenwich beach or any beach in Connecticut, use it._
* _When federal resources can help modernize wastewater infrastructure, pursue them._
* _When state mandates potentially collide with federal clean-water requirements, ask the federal agency responsible for enforcing those requirements to investigate._

As Goldstein wrote in today's letter:
> **" As a candidate for Congress, I believe federal solutions are required when local problems raise federal questions."**
That is the philosophy behind this campaign.
* We can build housing.
* We can modernize wastewater and stormwater infrastructure.
* We can protect local decision-making.
* We can keep our beaches open.
* And we can restore Long Island Sound.

**Federal Solutions to Local Problems.**

clean_body: Time to Stop Hartford from DC by tackling the problem from the Sound and the Clean Water Act | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more The Goldstein Substack - A Father-Son Publication Dr. Goldstein is Running for Congress and his page can be found Time to Stop Hartford from DC by tackling the problem from the Sound and the Clean Water Act | | | Aug 21 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- Connecticut Republican Congressional Nominee Dr. Michael Goldstein sends letter to EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin seeking federal review of 8-30g, Public Act 25-1 and their potential impact on wastewater infrastructure and Long Island Sound PRESS RELEASE: Greenwich CT, August 21, 2026 Today, Dr. Michael Goldstein, Republican nominee for Congress in Connecticut 's Fourth Congressional District, sent a letter to EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin asking the Environmental Protection Agency to examine a problem that has been treated for too long as merely local: What happens when Hartford mandates development, but local communities are left with the sewer, stormwater, infrastructure and environmental consequences? For Goldstein, the letter represents a central principle of his campaign: Federal Solutions to Local Problems. Connecticut needs housing. But Hartford should not be able to mandate or incentivize additional development without answering whether the infrastructure necessary to support that development can actually handle it. Goldstein is asking EPA and EPA Region 1 to review Connecticut's 8-30g affordable-housing law and Public Act 25-1, formerly House Bill 8002 , in communities draining into Long Island Sound. His argument is not that Washington should control local zoning. It is that Hartford cannot use state housing policy to escape federal environmental obligations. From Byram Beach to Washington The problem is visible right here in Fairfield County and Connecticut's Fourth District and in my hometown of Greenwich. | | ---|---|--- Source: Greenwich's Board of Health reported this year that the rainfall threshold for closing Byram Beach was reduced from one-half inch to just 0.3 inches following review of approximately a decade of testing. The Town has investigated bacteria in the Tom's Brook watershed and undertaken sewer testing and sewer-line grouting. Save the Sound gave Byram Beach a D+ based on 2025 swimming-season data, with samples reportedly failing safe-swimming criteria 36 percent of the time overall and experiencing substantially greater problems during wet weather. That may begin as a local problem, But the water doesn't stop at the Greenwich border. Long Island Sound connects Greenwich, Stamford, Darien, Norwalk, Westport, Fairfield and Bridgeport and the rest of Connecticut's coastline. And once pollution implicates federally protected waters and federal environmental statutes, there is a federal role. That is what federal solutions to local problems looks like. Hartford Mandates. Towns Pay. Hartford's housing policies increasingly affect local land-use decisions. Public Act 25-1 also restricts aspects of municipal authority over off-street parking requirements for residential development. Hartford doesn't operate Greenwich's sewer system. Hartford doesn't maintain Stamford's pumping stations. Hartford doesn't manage stormwater in Norwalk. Hartford doesn't close beaches after heavy rain. Our municipalities and taxpayers deal with those consequences. My letter therefore asks an important question: before the state imposes additional density, shouldn 't somebody determine whether the sewer system, stormwater system, pumping stations and receiving waters can actually support it? You Cannot Measure Capacity on a Sunny Day A wastewater plant's average daily flow does not tell the entire story. The real test comes during heavy rain. Goldstein argues that infrastructure capacity must account for peak wet-weather flow, infiltration and inflow, pumping-station constraints, collection-system bottlenecks, overflow history and treatment performance. Housing produces additional sanitary flow. Development can add impervious surfaces that prevent rainwater dissipation. Rain produces stormwater. Aging infrastructure may already experience infiltration and inflow. Those pressures can converge precisely when the system is under the greatest stress. Infrastructure must come before mandates. Taking Hartford to the EPA Today's letter does not ask EPA to become a Connecticut zoning board. It asks EPA to examine whether state-directed development in areas with documented wet-weather sewer limitations or recurring bacteria problems can create foreseeable conditions that cause or contribute to violations of the Clean Water Act or degradation of coastal recreational waters protected under the BEACH Act. Goldstein specifically asks EPA to use Byram Beach and the western Long Island Sound watershed as a case study , while examining the broader Fourth District shoreline. Instead of waiting for a sewer overflow or another beach closure, government should be asking these questionsbefore additional infrastructure loading occurs. This Is What Congress Should Do Too often, Washington politicians talk about national issues while residents struggle with problems right outside their doors. Goldstein's approach is different: Find the federal connection to the local problem --and use it. When federal environmental law can help protect a Greenwich beach or any beach in Connecticut, use it. When federal resources can help modernize wastewater infrastructure, pursue them. When state mandates potentially collide with federal clean-water requirements, ask the federal agency responsible for enforcing those requirements to investigate. As Goldstein wrote in today's letter: " As a candidate for Congress, I believe federal solutions are required when local problems raise federal questions." That is the philosophy behind this campaign. We can build housing. We can modernize wastewater and stormwater infrastructure. We can protect local decision-making. We can keep our beaches open. And we can restore Long Island Sound. Federal Solutions to Local Problems. Check Out the Campaign and Support Dr. Goldstein Dr. Michael Goldstein is the Republican nominee for Congress in Connecticut 's Fourth Congressional District. Doctor. Lawyer. Father. Fighter. Learn more about Dr. Goldstein, his grassroots campaign and how you can get involved or donate: Support Dr. Michael Goldstein for Congress. Vote November 3.** Put a Doctor in the House. | | **September Rate-Hike Odds Have Fallen to Roughly 42% After Last Week’s CPI — a Near Coin Flip. Warsh’s Jackson Hole Remarks Can Move That Figure Either Way. Here Is Why the Number Is the Cleanest Gauge of How the Market Reads Him.**
---
| | The abstract debate about the Fed’s September decision now has a concrete number: September rate-hike odds have fallen to approximately 42% following last week’s CPI report. **This figure is the market’s real-time barometer of the tension defining the autumn — and Chair Warsh’s Jackson Hole remarks this week have the potential to move it dramatically either way, making the number the cleanest gauge of how the market reads his message.**
---
| | For your portfolio, the 42% is striking because it means the market considers a September hike nearly a coin flip. That the odds are for a hike rather than a cut is itself the story — despite the cooling CPI, the weakening labor market, and the doves’ arguments, the persistent energy shock keeps a rate increase on the table. **The 42% reflects the genuine two-sidedness: cooling inflation pulling the odds down, elevated oil keeping them well above zero.** This is why Warsh’s framing matters so precisely: any signal of a formal shift away from the tightening bias would likely trigger a significant rally in rate-sensitive assets as those hike odds collapse, while maintaining the current posture in the face of contracting employment would extend the uncertainty that has weighed on fixed income and growth equities all summer. For the American investor, the number gives a clear reference: if Warsh pushes the odds meaningfully below 42%, the market reads him dovish (favoring growth, AI, and long bonds); if they hold or rise, hawkish (favoring energy and inflation hedges). Watch where the 42% travels in the hours after he speaks — it is the real-time translation of his message.

He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | Market Commentary Disclaimer We encourage all readers to consult a qualified financial professional — such as a registered investment adviser or licensed broker — before making any investment decision. Minneapolis. Primary day.

I lean in and ask the election judge one question: how many people am I allowed to vouch for?

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5NzV9AAwAAAAAAnr_4FpHg4AgkJOqsjAEXYTSSMtW9DkQJowMKN8gwVKFgdLdMNCnD4x-OPe_GmoTnjx14tAjF-t18k_EmIPp2Pg7Il0AkIe6IDkhOcTqTg

"Eight."

Not one. EIGHT.

So I tell her exactly what she is agreeing to. These people are not registered. They have no ID. No license, no bill, no paperwork of any kind.

She does not blink. She does not hesitate. She says:

"You are the ID."

I said it back to her, just to be sure I had heard it right. I am the ID. She agreed.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5NzV9AAwAAAAAAnr_4FpITskrbeOtzWfeaa5C3u78un7LpzoESc_workBy3y_6zv_ONwOgdZ-R_CsfwGgn_dzxPpUU7IilEY9WY9bZ2VYUzfOU3ypVzkPew
Help me tear this open.

That single sentence is the entire wall standing between a legitimate election and a fraudulent one. Not a database, not a document, not a verification of any kind. One man's word, accepted at the counter.

Now let me show you how deep this particular hole actually goes, because every single thing I am about to tell you makes the thing before it considerably worse.

EIGHT. Minnesota law permits one registered voter to swear an oath that eight other people live in his precinct, and on the strength of that oath alone those eight individuals register on the spot and vote that same day. Not one piece of documentation ever changes hands.

UNLIMITED. Then you read the sentence that comes immediately after it: "This limitation does not apply to an employee of a residential facility." If you happen to work at a nursing home, the eight-person cap disappears entirely. There is no number written anywhere. There is no ceiling at all.

NOBODY WRITES IT DOWN. Scott Pressler's team requested a list of the people who had been vouched in from four different Minnesota cities: Minneapolis, St. Paul, Duluth and St. Cloud. All four came back with nothing whatsoever, because that list does not exist anywhere in the state. An election worker circles a number on a form, and that circled number is the entire permanent record. Pressler describes these voters as nameless, faceless and recordless.

AND YOU CAN NEVER TAKE IT BACK. Those ballots drop straight into the pile alongside everyone else's and are counted immediately. America First Legal put the consequence in writing to Minnesota's Secretary of State back in June: once the ballots have been commingled, pulling them back out again is simply impossible.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5NzV9AAwAAAAAAnr_4FpJR8bSM97fyJJk774IkN9lD4Qo-uwqzDBY91breyPbjd9mWrhBWDQ7LPfKpwI677fMZVKzktXJK8RGE9rrW7_jsQEih4P9L3TXZQ
FUND THE INVESTIGATION — CHIP IN $35 NOW
Sit with that for a moment.

Somebody lies on that oath, and you catch him three weeks later with a recorded confession on video, and none of it matters in the slightest. The votes have already been counted, the winner has already been sworn into office, and there is no undo button, no list to check, and nothing whatsoever to audit, because nothing was ever written down in the first place.

The only lock on that door is a stranger's promise, and nobody bothers checking the promise until long after the door has already swung open.

So on August 11 we went and knocked on it.
https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5NzV9AAwAAAAAAnr_4FpKhxjNr7w2Dm7MsRewiEAvUaOpWGI2PovZpj1CKXkp75c96jve_-RY1VBgjTKyVHN42H3NZy5WHC9_0Jc8LPRg51wKqjyqoOVs-w
Keep us knocking — give $35, $50 or $100.

Polling place after polling place, I said the quiet part out loud every single time. They are not registered. They have no identification. There are eight of them. May I bring them?

Yes.

Yes.

Yes.

One judge was so obliging that she walked me through the entire procedure as though she were signing me up for a library card, and another one assured me that the whole arrangement was a good thing.

Now let me tell you what we did NOT do, because this matters to me more than any footage ever will.

We never brought anyone inside that building. We never registered a single human being. We never cast one ballot. Not one.

We asked the question, we caught the answer on camera, and we walked straight back out the door. That has been the rule for as long as I have been doing this work, and it is not negotiable. We film the hole in the fence. We never climb through it. The day we break that rule is the day every tape we have ever made becomes worthless.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5NzV9AAwAAAAAAnr_4FpLRCMzK-eimezDP2CAiJiOpv0LB7f4xvYPC53bv-WODBTtkMRUERWtJF8_s5S0igPQgUvYVUhfopWVQNGmaEhWwA3z0M1gg8RwDA

Here is the clock.

America starts voting on September 19, which is twenty-nine days from today.

Minnesota is ONE state, and we were on the ground there for ONE afternoon. We uncovered every bit of this simply by walking through a door and asking a question that apparently nobody had ever bothered to ask out loud before.

Now consider every other state in the country with same-day registration on the books. Consider the thousands of polling places this fall that nobody will ever walk into carrying a camera, for the simple reason that there is nobody available to carry one.

That is the entire reason I am writing to you.

sponsor someone who will.

You fund the mission, my team takes the risks, and you and your family watch the results land with your own eyes.

body:
The minute we start assuming we have this in the bag is the moment we set ourselves up to lose.
|

Peter,
_
Time and time again, we’ve seen this pattern play out the same way: Early polls favor Democrats to win battleground Senate races, only for that edge to disappear by Election Day._
So when I saw polls this spring and early summer showing me ahead of my GOP opponent, Michael Whatley, by double digits, I took them with a grain of salt (or, to be honest, about a pound of it).
By July, however, the GOP had started spending nearly $100 million so far to defeat me. As the lies, attacks and dark money heated up, my polling lead shriveled down to just +4.
So if anyone thought that the momentum was on our side enough to coast to victory, then they’re in for a wake-up call in the fall:
**Unless we build the resources right now to fight back, President Trump's hand-picked candidate will win North Carolina, and his allies will keep the Senate until 2029.**
But listen: If there’s a silver lining in my mind, it’s that polls don’t decide elections. People do. Folks just like **you** hold the power to change the outcome of this must-win Senate race – and with it, the future of our country. But only if we have all hands on deck as we enter the final sprint to Election Day.

| | | [](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0c9q3DAQBvCnkW820six5YMPCc5CIWnpH8hRaKVZe0CWjDXesG9ftmyh515nhvnB932823dHkdL81a04Uik25GADFZ-vuPOCZ3QH31wKvB-8WJDQ1dLUoKzzTFe0ravC-ATKXEyFo-pNrxVIgGoZB6NN6wMowKfeyXZQrtX9YAbXXbwaZEXj_Z80oJTSupWNaeEcOn12aOSAuhOtPLbgGBtKhQIWn_O25UhMvjR5n6s4LsxbEfpZwEnAidIlNwvFWIKL2GA4BJwuO2LtSx3xk0rtl50Kk0vEtzpcg9Cn4oWepATQz1JK9aaG6ds0vf4U0B282pKP3aPQ07bnsqFnSvNjtWKgYxV6wtVRfAy9WzdHcxJ68sX-Ue2_qr2rj9OcGBMLPb18eXl7td_7-uPXj_pvLtU-hu2TYqTS9aKV811pfF4r_t-2riP8DgAA__9VsaZI)

Dear Friend,

C.S. Lewis is one of my favorite authors, full stop.

His writings were essential in deepening my faith in God and my understanding of the Bible. Maybe, since you opened my email, he has helped you, too.

Why are Lewis's words so powerful?

It's because he was a master at addressing life's most important questions. His vivid language is delightful and captivating to read.

Lewis's signature ability to communicate the truth about Christianity has inspired so many skeptics to **become** believers and even more Christians to renew and deepen their faith. He is certainly the greatest Christian apologist of the twentieth century.

To help you learn more about Lewis's works related to Christianity, we produced a powerful, free course, "**C.S. Lewis on Christianity** ," which you can now own on DVD absolutely free.

**Claim your FREE DVD set of "C.S. Lewis on Christianity" using this secure link:**

[https://info.hillsdale.edu/free-cs-lewis-christianity-dvd](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0c9q3DAQBvCnkW820six5YMPCc5CIWnpH8hRaKVZe0CWjDXesG9ftmyh515nhvnB932823dHkdL81a04Uik25GADFZ-vuPOCZ3QH31wKvB-8WJDQ1dLUoKzzTFe0ravC-ATKXEyFo-pNrxVIgGoZB6NN6wMowKfeyXZQrtX9YAbXXbwaZEXj_Z80oJTSupWNaeEcOn12aOSAuhOtPLbgGBtKhQIWn_O25UhMvjR5n6s4LsxbEfpZwEnAidIlNwvFWIKL2GA4BJwuO2LtSx3xk0rtl50Kk0vEtzpcg9Cn4oWepATQz1JK9aaG6ds0vf4U0B282pKP3aPQ07bnsqFnSvNjtWKgYxV6wtVRfAy9WzdHcxJ68sX-Ue2_qr2rj9OcGBMLPb18eXl7td_7-uPXj_pvLtU-hu2TYqTS9aKV811pfF4r_t-2riP8DgAA__9VsaZI)

In this course, you will study Lewis's profound insights on the central topics of Christianity, including:
* Good and evil
* Conversion and faith
* Prayer and the Bible
* Suffering and death
* Heaven and Hell

The instructor, Michael Ward, is a distinguished visiting professor at Hillsdale College and a member of the Faculty of Theology and Religion at the University of Oxford. He wrote _Planet Narnia: The Seven Heavens in the Imagination of C.S. Lewis_ and _After Humanity: A Guide to C.S. Lewis 's The Abolition of Man_. He even spent three years living in Lewis's Oxford home as the resident Warden of The Kilns!

You'll find this course especially moving because it examines C.S. Lewis's beautiful writings about faith. You'll even trace Lewis's own journey from skeptic to believer. The combination provides an opportunity for you to grow in your knowledge and understanding of Christianity.

[So please join us in studying Christianity with C.S. Lewis and Michael Ward with this beautiful free DVD set.](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0c9q3DAQBvCnkW820six5YMPCc5CIWnpH8hRaKVZe0CWjDXesG9ftmyh515nhvnB932823dHkdL81a04Uik25GADFZ-vuPOCZ3QH31wKvB-8WJDQ1dLUoKzzTFe0ravC-ATKXEyFo-pNrxVIgGoZB6NN6wMowKfeyXZQrtX9YAbXXbwaZEXj_Z80oJTSupWNaeEcOn12aOSAuhOtPLbgGBtKhQIWn_O25UhMvjR5n6s4LsxbEfpZwEnAidIlNwvFWIKL2GA4BJwuO2LtSx3xk0rtl50Kk0vEtzpcg9Cn4oWepATQz1JK9aaG6ds0vf4U0B282pKP3aPQ07bnsqFnSvNjtWKgYxV6wtVRfAy9WzdHcxJ68sX-Ue2_qr2rj9OcGBMLPb18eXl7td_7-uPXj_pvLtU-hu2TYqTS9aKV811pfF4r_t-2riP8DgAA__9VsaZI)

Warm regards,

Bill Gray '01
Vice President
Institutional Advancement
Hillsdale College

**P.S.** You probably know that C.S. Lewis also wrote the children's series, _The Chronicles of Narnia_. My wife and I read those books to our children so many times! I can't tell you how many dog-eared copies we have of these.

One of the best parts of this course is learning how the Christian faith is woven into these captivating stories. **I hope you 'll take advantage of this great FREE DVD offer today:** [https://info.hillsdale.edu/free-cs-lewis-christianity-dvd](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0c9q3DAQBvCnkW820six5YMPCc5CIWnpH8hRaKVZe0CWjDXesG9ftmyh515nhvnB932823dHkdL81a04Uik25GADFZ-vuPOCZ3QH31wKvB-8WJDQ1dLUoKzzTFe0ravC-ATKXEyFo-pNrxVIgGoZB6NN6wMowKfeyXZQrtX9YAbXXbwaZEXj_Z80oJTSupWNaeEcOn12aOSAuhOtPLbgGBtKhQIWn_O25UhMvjR5n6s4LsxbEfpZwEnAidIlNwvFWIKL2GA4BJwuO2LtSx3xk0rtl50Kk0vEtzpcg9Cn4oWepATQz1JK9aaG6ds0vf4U0B282pKP3aPQ07bnsqFnSvNjtWKgYxV6wtVRfAy9WzdHcxJ68sX-Ue2_qr2rj9OcGBMLPb18eXl7td_7-uPXj_pvLtU-hu2TYqTS9aKV811pfF4r_t-2riP8DgAA__9VsaZI)

subject: They kicked me out of the House chamber
body:
---
| [](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-pearson-split?amount=20&refcode=em_20260821_8682_fr&refcode2=8682_22930333_cDe110&akid=8682%2E22930333%2EcDe110)
---
Derek, my name is Justin Pearson, and I just became the Democratic nominee for Congress in Tennessee’s 9th Congressional District.
I won my primary exactly 61 years after President Johnson stood alongside Reverend Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., Reverend Ralph Abernathy, John Lewis, and Rosa Parks and signed the Voting Rights Act into law.
Today, that same Voting Rights Act has been severely undermined by the Supreme Court, and the Tennessee state legislature has taken advantage of those weaker protections by separating Memphis and Shelby County, our only majority-Black congressional district, into thirds.
**The political dilution and deprivation of our rights is happening in our lifetime. It’s a blatant attempt to keep people like me out of power.**
This election is about a vision for 61 years from today. Not just for my district, but in races across the country.
**In 74 days, we will face a choice:** We can start to build an America that reflects the true spirit of generosity and kindness that I have always known our communities to have. Or, we can let our country continue to be permanently scarred by two more years of unchecked power for Donald Trump. By two more years of chaos and cruelty. By two more years of the systematic dismantling of our fundamental rights and freedoms.
**Derek, we can’t let that choice be made for us on Election Day._We_ have to make that choice in these next 74 days.** We have to choose to fight, to knock doors and make calls and do everything we can to power Democrats to victory, or we can choose to sit back and wait.
I’ve made my choice. I’m going to do everything I can to make sure that Democrats take back the House and the Senate this November.
The DNC is doing everything that they can too. **They’re sending organizers out to register tens of thousands of new Democratic voters in swing states and supporting over 10,000 Democrats running for office across the country, from the school board to the Senate.**
[**So Derek, if you’re in this fight with us and you’re looking for a quick way to make a big impact, splitting a $20 between my campaign and the DNC today is a great place to start. We’ll put your donation to work immediately to win here in Tennessee and power Democrats to victory up and down the ballot, across the country.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-pearson-split?amount=20&refcode=em_20260821_8682_fr&refcode2=8682_22930333_cDe110&akid=8682%2E22930333%2EcDe110)

name: Darline Graham
subject: Before I take the stage with President Trump
body:
Tonight, I want to tell President Trump you're with us. |
---

Tonight I will join President Trump on stage - but before I do, I need to know if you're with me, Fellow Patriot.

President Trump is coming to South Carolina to stand with our campaign, days before Tuesday's runoff. _He didn't have to do that._ **He's doing it because he believes in this movement, and because he gave me his "Complete and Total Endorsement."**

I am the only candidate in this race who can beat South Carolina's most liberal Democrat candidate in November. Not close. Not "maybe." The only one. My opponents know it, President Trump knows it, and that's exactly why he's walking on that stage with me tonight.

This wasn't a situation where we caught Republicans off guard. They pulled out all the stops to hold this seat, and it wasn't enough.
And how did Brandon win?

clean_body: Tonight, I want to tell President Trump you're with us. | Tonight I will join President Trump on stage - but before I do, I need to know if you're with me, Peter. President Trump is coming to South Carolina to stand with our campaign, days before Tuesday's runoff. He didn't have to do that. He's doing it because he believes in this movement, and because he gave me his "Complete and Total Endorsement." I am the only candidate in this race who can beat South Carolina's most liberal Democrat candidate in November. Not close. Not "maybe." The only one. My opponents know it, President Trump knows it, and that's exactly why he's walking on that stage with me tonight. Peter, a crowd doesn't win a runoff. Grassroots support does. Before I take that stage, my team set a goal - - to show President Trump, and every voter watching, that South Carolina is fired up and ready to finish this on Tuesday. We are not there yet. And the doors open in just a few hours. I don't need a handful of max-out checks. I need YOU. Every single runoff contribution tells President Trump his trust in me was not misplaced. This runoff is Tuesday - just 4 days away. So before I walk out to join President Trump tonight, I want to walk out knowing you had my back. Let's finish this on Tuesday. Darline Graham P.S. name: Conrad (personal)
subject: Johnson says stopping data centers would be “dangerous”
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY COMMITTEE TO ELECT CONRAD CABLE
body:
His actual message: Mike Johnson wants data centers in your town (just not his).
| | | | | [](https://jseax8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001lablS4mkpS-bolCaC2ITESmkgcEG46JyCtzLFSg_h5aZDem1-3VjAK7At_Qjyngn525cyoISrhNx33X5eUE2YbgWtds58BuLwjST-mpSG5lc6c00tAKEXWoqUxYL2fz5OZKf6RmsYxL-xIkc63USuwTpx2bVcbEkxyQ8jtTzTmhHld77e2fkGYlGEoH90rYhOpQIbAqaVuqmJp5hp_YQjvbG9bpa3YMt&c=vJtX43rponX3x3jnW58-OZgo9_cCGlh4HAWvOjELuqv6s0hxAe3A7A==&ch=yGMEfdLCKj4x5ltKWLJ9kTBG0dnZrkuRA3YRq4GQeJmF_RHrwOmcag==)
---
| Conrad Cable here, the Democrat taking on Mike Johnson this November.
I may be a farmer, but I am not anti-technology.
However, what I AM against is Big Tech companies and billionaire investors pushing expensive, wasteful, and polluting AI data centers over the vocal objection of the people in those communities.
The oligarchs who have gone all-in on AI and who stand to profit from construction of massive new data centers in the backyards of regular people have clearly bought the cooperation of politicians who are supposed to listen to and represent the PEOPLE.
Politicians like my opponent in this critical race against MAGA, Speaker of the House Mike Johnson, for example.
Johnson is a prolific fundraiser for groups that prop up MAGA House Republicans everywhere, and one way he is able to do that is by currying favor with AI owners and the billionaire class. He himself is bankrolled by right wing tech and finance bros like Peter Thiel.
That's why he defends gargantuan data centers that have been shown to pollute local drinking water and drive residents out of their own neighborhoods. Johnson ominously said any kind of pause on data centers, even if people vote for it or demand it from their leaders, would be "dangerous."
---
| [](https://jseax8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001lablS4mkpS-bolCaC2ITESmkgcEG46JyCtzLFSg_h5aZDem1-3VjAK7At_Qjyngn525cyoISrhNx33X5eUE2YbgWtds58BuLwjST-mpSG5lc6c00tAKEXWoqUxYL2fz5OZKf6RmsYxL-xIkc63USuwTpx2bVcbEkxyQ8jtTzTmhHld77e2fkGYlGEoH90rYhOpQIbAqaVuqsQenZ0r9c4o_tfkmGw-nU&c=vJtX43rponX3x3jnW58-OZgo9_cCGlh4HAWvOjELuqv6s0hxAe3A7A==&ch=yGMEfdLCKj4x5ltKWLJ9kTBG0dnZrkuRA3YRq4GQeJmF_RHrwOmcag==)
---
Johnson is the servant of Trump and the MAGA corporate overlords who would cut off their support for him and his MAGA caucus if he ever defied them.

If you check out Facebook this week, you can see the difference in how Mike Rogers and I see the world. Mike visited some businesses in Lee County and took staged photos with businesspeople, most of whom rely on government contracts or grants. Not spontaneous. Not open to the public.
Go back through his posts from the last 6 months (it won't take long). You'll see him in Calhoun and Lee Counties. That's about it.
On my feed, you'll see me at public events, handing out cards and talking with people. Nothing staged. Nothing scripted. Just me showing respect for the people of this district by asking what they need from their congressional representative.

Don't forget that our town hall meeting in Opelika is this Thursday. Bring some friends who aren't Democrats.

Dear Patriot,
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e805273/VaHR0cHM6Ly9mcmVlZG9td2F0Y2gucmV2di5jby9mdy0xNS1kYXlzLW1iLW9tLw/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjA4MjE/LbmNsOVJEU0dYWQ/qP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZnctMTUtZGF5cyZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPW9tJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1tYiZ1dG1fdGVybT0yMzQ4M193cjEmYW1vdW50PTI1/gaohTIA/sftc6d9cf7b)Do you remember when it was only fifteen days? Fifteen days to slow the spread. That was the promise they made you, and you believed it, because a doctor on television told you that the science demanded it and you are a decent person who did not want to hurt anybody. Do you remember what your street sounded like that spring? Nothing at all — no traffic, no children playing outside, no church bells on Sunday morning. Only sirens, running all day and into the night, and the sound of your own television counting the dead. Do you remember the plywood going up over the storefronts downtown? The caution tape wrapped around the swing sets? The arrows taped to the floor of the grocery store, and the man who shouted at you for standing too close to him in the aisle? Fifteen days eventually became two years. So let me ask you the question that nobody in Washington has ever bothered to ask you. **What did those two years take from you?** Not from the country. From **you**. [**Help me get you the answer, under oath.**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e805273/VaHR0cHM6Ly9mcmVlZG9td2F0Y2gucmV2di5jby9mdy0xNS1kYXlzLW1iLW9tLw/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjA4MjE/LbmNsOVJEU0dYWQ/qP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZnctMTUtZGF5cyZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPW9tJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1tYiZ1dG1fdGVybT0yMzQ4M193cjEmYW1vdW50PTI1/gaohTIA/sftc6d9cf7b) Maybe it was the business — thirty years of your life invested in it, and then a paper sign taped to the glass. The big chain store down the road stayed open and sold the very same goods, because yours was ruled "non-essential." Some of you never opened those doors again. Maybe it was your father's funeral, with only ten mourners permitted, while you watched your own father buried through a telephone screen at your kitchen table. Maybe it was your church, chained shut on Easter Sunday while the state government announced that the liquor store and the casino could remain open for business. I sued over exactly that, because congregations were treated as a public menace while gambling halls ran all night. Maybe it was your children — two years staring at a laptop, a child who now reads two grades behind, a graduation year that simply never happened, and a teenager who has never really been the same since. Maybe it was your mother in the nursing home. Ten months of waving at her through a window, and near the end she no longer knew who was waving. You did all of it. You closed up your business, you stayed inside your home, and you buried people alone, because you were repeatedly assured that there was no alternative. **Now here is what that man was doing while you obeyed.** Senator Rand Paul released 1,100 pages of Anthony Fauci's private diary. In his own words, written at the time, Fauci kept "an open mind about the possibility of a lab leak" — while publicly branding that same idea a conspiracy theory and smearing anyone who dared to raise it. People like you. People like me. So while you sat in that parking lot, the man giving the orders privately had his doubts, and he simply never shared a single one of them with you. **[GIVE $25, $50 OR $100 — MAKE HIM EXPLAIN IT UNDER OATH](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e805273/VaHR0cHM6Ly9mcmVlZG9td2F0Y2gucmV2di5jby9mdy0xNS1kYXlzLW1iLW9tLw/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjA4MjE/LbmNsOVJEU0dYWQ/qP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZnctMTUtZGF5cyZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPW9tJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1tYiZ1dG1fdGVybT0yMzQ4M193cjEmYW1vdW50PTI1/gaohTIA/sftc6d9cf7b)** | | [**$25**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e805273/VaHR0cHM6Ly9mcmVlZG9td2F0Y2gucmV2di5jby9mdy0xNS1kYXlzLW1iLW9tLw/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjA4MjE/LbmNsOVJEU0dYWQ/qP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZnctMTUtZGF5cyZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPW9tJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1tYiZ1dG1fdGVybT0yMzQ4M193cjEmYW1vdW50PTI1/gaohTIA/sftc6d9cf7b)
