# Other International News
* **Ebola virus outbreak in DRC "growing exponentially":** The Ebola virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is "growing exponentially," the UN warned on Friday. Julien Harneis, the UN's Senior Ebola Coordinator, said in a [statement](https://substack.com/redirect/94168273-9fb7-4705-a804-89f31838acb8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that more than 2,500 people had died in the last three months, with over half of all deaths occurring in just the last 20 days. "The epidemic is spreading to an area that is bigger than France. And the outbreak is growing faster and wider than the Ebola response," Harneis said. He also stressed the "brutal" conditions facing healthcare workers with 160 healthcare workers contracting Ebola, with 43 dying.
* **U.S. imposes new Cuba sanctions, detains Americans returning from island:** The Treasury and State departments [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/10dc3dc1-919f-4d45-b946-1254e42afef5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) new sanctions Thursday against nine Cuban state-owned mining, metal, and construction companies, and on the leadership of the Cuban Institute of Friendship with the Peoples, which Secretary of State Marco Rubio accused of sponsoring "a vast subversive network in the United States aimed at identifying, cultivating, and radicalizing" Americans, according to the Associated Press.
* The move follows an operation at the Miami airport last weekend in which several Americans returning from Cuba after attending events marking Fidel Castro's 100th birthday were briefly detained and had electronic devices seized for inspection.
* Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodriguez said that the U.S. imposed the sanctions with the "deliberate aim of harming" the country's economy "to prevent the provision of basic services to the population." The measures add to an oil blockade the U.S. imposed earlier this year following the removal of Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro, which has resulted in regular blackouts and medical shortages on the island.
* **Imran Khan sent back to prison hours after hospital visit:** Former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan was briefly [hospitalized](https://substack.com/redirect/6ede24c5-8408-4363-bd63-0712a83bda0f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), declared medically fit, and returned to prison within hours early Friday, a move his Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf party said violated a Supreme Court order requiring him to remain under medical supervision until at least mid-September.
* Khan's sister, Uzma Khan, said he told her he was being "repeatedly" tortured in prison, and party officials accused authorities of "contempt of the Supreme Court" after Khan was examined at a state-run hospital, contrary to a court order mandating that he be treated at a private facility.
* Khan has been imprisoned since August 2023 on charges he has characterized as "politically motivated." PTI officials have announced a nationwide march, planned to take place on September 27, in response to his medical deterioration.
* Separately, Zulfikar Bukhari, a top aide to Khan, told Reuters on Thursday that the former PM would not confront army chief Asim Munir if freed, marking a significant shift in rhetoric from a party whose supporters have long rallied against the military leader they blame for Khan's 2023 imprisonment.
* **Hundreds protest against Tunisian President Kais Saied:** Hundreds of protesters [marched](https://substack.com/redirect/62d5545a-bc7c-4797-a05a-887453f346dd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Tunis Thursday calling for President Kais Saied's ouster and rejecting what they called "one-man rule" and "a slide towards dictatorship," urging the release of jailed opposition figures, activists, and journalists, Al Jazeera reported.
* The demonstration follows a similar protest on July 25 marking the anniversary of Saied's 2021 dismissal of the government and suspension of parliament.
* Saied, a 68-year-old former constitutional lawyer elected in 2019 on an anti-corruption platform, has faced international criticism for consolidating control over the judiciary and overseeing mass trials of political opponents.
* The country has been racked by mounting economic pressure, with inflation at 5.2%, according to the World Bank. Protests have also emerged in response to widespread water and power cuts, and the environmental problems that accompanied wildfires that hit the country earlier this summer.
* **HRW: Russian paramilitaries "summarily killed" nine Mali civilians, including four children**: Human Rights Watch [said](https://substack.com/redirect/6bc8793c-e5a8-4e07-9a1d-6cf41fa32759?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Thursday that Russia's Africa Corps summarily killed nine civilians, including four children, in Mali's central Mopti region in the presence of Malian soldiers earlier last month, alleging the paramilitary group also beat dozens of people and burned at least eight homes.
* HRW said more than 100 Africa Corps fighters rounded up at least 80 men and boys in Bombori village on July 10, beating them while interrogating them about alleged ties to armed groups, before shooting six who tried to escape and executing three others in custody, one allegedly by beheading.
* The killings come amid Mali's ongoing civil war against armed groups linked to al-Qaeda and ISIL, with Russia's Africa Corps having become the country's main military partner since Bamako's relations with Western nations, particularly its former colonizer France, deteriorated following the military's 2021 seizure of power.
* **Ukraine hits Russian oil and power sites in overnight drone barrage, blacking out much of Crimea:** Ukraine [struck](https://substack.com/redirect/bc0dc6f9-a43b-4837-8729-b7a8c00cbe7e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a wave of Russian energy targets overnight into Thursday, Aug. 20, in one of its heaviest long-range drone campaigns of the war, hitting oil refineries, a Black Sea export terminal, and a substation feeding occupied Crimea, according to Ukraine's General Staff. Ukrainian drones struck a substation in Krasnodar Krai, which provides Russian-occupied Crimea with much of its power, leading to a blackout in the area overnight. Drones also struck an export terminal at Volna and a refinery in Tatarstan.
* **RSF attacks kill six, displace over 1,000 in Sudan 's North Kordofan: **Rapid Support Forces fighters [raided](https://substack.com/redirect/958f3599-1c00-4d67-bb4c-40c87525c111?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the villages of Um Dareisa and Al-Shaqla in Sudan's North Kordofan state Wednesday, killing six civilians and forcing more than 1,000 people to flee on foot to the state capital El Obeid, Sudan Tribune reported. A local official accused RSF fighters of widespread abuses in the area in recent days, including unlawful killings, physical assaults, sexual violence, looting supplies at gunpoint, and forced displacement. The attack follows a raid last week on the nearby town of Um Arda that killed 18 people and displaced more than 300 families.
* **U.S. deportees arrive in Liberia:** Twenty people deported from the United States [arrived](https://substack.com/redirect/866bef61-f8d5-45bd-b959-e4e2f920cad1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at Roberts International Airport outside Monrovia on Thursday, the first group transferred under a $5 million deal allowing the U.S. to send up to 1,200 third-country deportees to Liberia over the next year. Liberian officials said the group will include people from Africa, North and South America, and the Caribbean, but most of the first arrivals came from Latin America, including Venezuela and Cuba.

* **Syria weighs joining security pact with Pakistan, Turkey, Saudi Arabia:** Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad Hassan al-Shaibani said Damascus was [reviewing](https://substack.com/redirect/122186c8-c97f-4fc8-a049-815b6ee74b4c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) whether to join the trilateral "Mecca Joint Defence Agreement" between Turkey, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, but has not yet made a decision. Speaking on a state visit to Islamabad, al-Shaibani said Syria was seeking to deepen ties with Pakistan, with the two sides moving toward exchanging ambassadors, establishing direct flights and reviving a joint ministerial commission.
* **Hong Kong Tiananmen vigil organizers convicted under national security law:** Lee Cheuk-yan and Chow Hang-tung, former leaders of the Hong Kong Alliance in Support of Patriotic Democratic Movements of China, were [convicted](https://substack.com/redirect/677acb2c-c2b9-467c-b6bc-a763351964cf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Friday of inciting subversion, following a national security law imposed on the region by the Chinese government. Both were charged in 2021 after organizing annual vigils in commemoration of China's 1989 Tiananmen Square crackdown. Lee and Chow now face up to 10 years in prison.
* **Judge rules Palestine Action did not violate UK terrorism laws:** UK Judge Robert Altham ruled on Friday that five Palestine Action activists would not be sentenced under the country's terrorism laws, after the cohort was found guilty in June of causing $290,000 worth of damage to a Barclays Bank during an August 2024 protest against the bank's shareholdings in the Israeli defense company Elbit Systems.

Ukraine hits Russian oil and power sites in overnight drone barrage, blacking out much of Crimea. RSF attacks kill six, displace over 1,000 in Sudan's North Kordofan. U.S. deportees arrive in Liberia. Syria weighs joining security pact with Pakistan, Turkey, Saudi Arabia. Hong Kong Tiananmen vigil organizers convicted under national security law. Judge rules Palestine Action did not violate UK terrorism laws. This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Palestine 15-year-old boy dies after being shot in the head by Israel in Gaza: A 15-year-old Palestinian boy died on Thursday after being shot by Israeli troops in Beit Lahia, northern Gaza. Footage appears to show him shot in the head. Israeli forces and settlers kill two Palestinians, wound several others in occupied West Bank attacks: Hebron: A 17-year-old Palestinian boy was after being shot in the chest by armed Israeli settlers during an attack on homes in Khirbet Hamroush, northeast of Hebron, WAFA reported. A 70-year-old man was also shot and wounded, and settlers burned down a home. In southern Hebron, settlers homes near Al-Dhahiriya and Al-Samu, injuring five Palestinians, stealing sheep and attacking a Palestinian Red Crescent ambulance, preventing it from reaching the wounded. Israeli forces later arrested four Palestinians in Shaab Al-Butum, including a father and son, and three others during a raid on Beit Ummar. Jenin: Israeli forces Fathi Hazem, a 58-year-old retired police colonel in the Palestinian National Security Forces, during a raid on his home in central Jenin and withheld his body. An eyewitness told AFP, "They shot him seven times in front of his 10-year-old son. They dragged him down the stairs and took him with them." Two of Hazem's other sons were killed by the Israeli military in 2022. In Zababdeh, south of Jenin, Israeli forces shot a 14-year-old boy in the chest and back during a raid. Israeli forces also hung Israeli flags along several points of the Jenin-Nablus road. Nablus: Israeli settlers attacked the Bula Al-Hawa area, east of Nablus, a Palestinian. Drop Site reports on detained Palestinian journalist: After more than two years in Israeli detention, the first photo of Palestinian journalist Mohammed Arab emerged on Monday. Israeli forces seized Arab from Gaza's Al-Shifa Medical Complex on March 18, 2024. "They are calling on us using the quadcopters. Pray for me, and take care of the children," Arab told his wife Wafaa Abu Al-Laban in their final conversation. "Mohammed's health is very, very poor," Abu Al-Laban told Drop Site's Abdel Qader Sabbah. Arab was subjected to severe abuse at Sde Teiman and forced to remain on his knees for prolonged periods, causing a slipped disc and serious back problems. His eyesight also deteriorated after his glasses were taken away, his lawyer said. After more than two years in detention, Arab told his lawyer that seeing his own face had become a dream. "I just want to know what I look like," he said. A petition had to be filed to obtain underwear and a mirror for him. Watch Abdel Qader Sabbah 's video report on Mohamed Arab for Drop Site . Hamas is "fully committed" to Board of Peace roadmap, official says: Basem Naim, a senior Hamas official, CNN on Thursday that the group remains fully committed to the "agreed version" of the "Board of Peace" roadmap for Gaza, noting that the group believes that the roadmap satisfactorily handles the decommissioning of its weapons, the future of its tunnels, and implementation timelines. President Donald Trump's envoy Nickolay Mladenov had pledged to secure Israel's approval for the deal, Naim said, but Israel has since rejected the deal and carried out massacres in Gaza in a deliberate attempt to derail it. Naim also CNN that Board of Peace mediators and Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner are asking Hamas to be "sensitive" to Benjamin Netanyahu's political position ahead of Israel's upcoming election over the already-agreed Gaza roadmap. "As a Palestinian, I am not in a position to pay the price from the bodies and blood and the lives of our people in order to secure the victory of Netanyahu's election," Naim noted to CNN in response. Qatar, Turkey, and Egypt condemn Israeli attacks on Gaza: Qatar, Egypt, and Turkey "strongly " recent Israeli attacks on Gaza that have killed civilians, including women and children, in a joint statement Wednesday. The statement said the intensification of Israeli attacks "undermines regional and international efforts at a critical juncture," as work continues to implement the plan to end the war, including the Board of Peace's meeting with Israeli officials. They stressed that Israel must "fully comply with all its obligations under the ceasefire agreement" and refrain from actions that could escalate tensions. European leaders condemn Israeli settlement expansion: The leaders of the UK, France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Norway and Canada Israel's decision to issue construction tenders for the E1 settlement project in the occupied West Bank in a joint statement on Thursday. The statement urges Israel to "retract these plans immediately" and halt settlement expansion. It also warns businesses not to bid on the tenders, citing possible "legal and reputational consequences" and the risk of involvement in "serious breaches of international law." Turkey seeks Interpol red notice for Netanyahu over Global Sumud Flotilla attack: Turkey Interpol to issue a red notice for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu over the Israeli attack on activists aboard the Global Sumud Flotilla carrying humanitarian aid to Gaza, Justice Minister Akin Gurlek said Friday via Anadolu Agency. Gurlek said proceedings are continuing before an Istanbul court against 35 defendants over the attack in international waters and the detention of activists. Arrest warrants were issued for Netanyahu and Israeli official Afek Moskovitch on July 14 on charges including genocide, crimes against humanity, torture, aggravated deprivation of liberty and hijacking, prompting the Justice Ministry to request Interpol red notices. Three Palestinian parties in Israel revive Joint List ahead of October Knesset election : Three Palestinian parties in Israel, Hadash, Balad, and Ta'al, a reconstituted Joint List on Wednesday ahead of the October 27 Knesset election. The list will be led by Hadash's Yousef Jabareen, followed by Ta'al's Ahmad Tibi and Balad's Sami Abu Shehadeh, with the parties targeting at least 10 seats and competing against the United Arab List led by Mansour Abbas. Balad deputy secretary-general Yousef Tatur said the party made concessions to reach the agreement given "the gravity of the current moment," citing Israel's genocide in Gaza, West Bank displacement, and attacks in Jerusalem, and called on Palestinian voters with Israeli citizenship who are eligible to vote to help "turn unity into a real force on the ground." Iran U.S. threatens countries trading with Iran with "economic oblivion": U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Thursday that Washington would impose the "toughest sanctions in history" on Iran following Trump's declaration of "economic warfare." "The economic pressure means that we are going to all of our allies, and this is going to be the greatest coordinated economic isolation in the history of the world," Bessent told CNBC, noting that all countries will now be judged as "either with us or against" the U.S. based on their economic relationship with Iran. "If you insist on doing business with them, either transferring money or buying their oil, they are doing seaborne ship transfers, then the US Treasury and the U.S. government, they will put its full might and force toward enforcing against you," Bessent told CNBC. Separately, Bessent his confusion at rising oil prices, saying that the U.S. had "asymmetric information" and he was "not sure why oil has popped up on this." Vice President JD Vance said Thursday that the war with Iran had entered "a new phase where the most effective tool we have is the economic pressure we can impose on them." "It will be a delicate dance," he added, because Iran "will try to put economic pressure on us." Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf called for a plan to overcome what he described as "cruel sanctions" following the U.S. Treasury announcement. Speaking during a visit to Iraq, Ghalibaf said Iran and other Muslim countries possess significant resources and raw materials that their "enemies are coming to plunder," and urged Baghdad to cooperate with Tehran in confronting the sanctions. China registers opposition to U.S. economic campaign against Iran: Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Lin Jian on Friday that the newest round of U.S. economic pressure would "not help to resolve" the conflict in the Middle East. Lin called on all sides to address tensions through political and diplomatic means. China has repeatedly rejected unilateral U.S. sanctions, arguing that measures not authorized by the UN Security Council lack standing in international law. Oil traffic through Hormuz remains constrained: Kpler 10.73 million barrels of west-to-east liquid tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz from August 14-20, an average of just 1.53 million barrels per day, a sharp contrast from the 10 million barrels per day figure that two U.S. officials gave Axios. Only 14 outbound tankers were observed during the entire week, with no recorded traffic on August 14 or 17, according to the maritime tracking firm. Kpler cautions that its figures may change as more vessel-position data becomes available, including from ships traveling with their tracking systems switched off. But the currently observed traffic is nowhere near the scale Washington described. Iranian crude oil offers to Chinese buyers decline: Offers of Iranian crude to Chinese buyers have fallen this week, Reuters on Friday, while prices have jumped. The number of planned deliveries for September and October declined from July and August, and barrels shipped earlier have already been sold. Crude oil, which is usually sold at a lower price, is now being sold at premiums, Reuters reported. Lebanon Israeli army continues attacks in Lebanon despite "ceasefire" agreement: Israeli forces a "massive explosion," conducted in two stages, in the area between the towns of Arnoun and Kfar Tebnit, in the Nabatieh district in southern Lebanon, the Lebanese National News Agency reported on Friday. In Tyre (Sour), Israeli attacks were in the Mansouri-Majdal Zoun area, according to the NNA, with the Israeli military firing artillery shells on Mansouri. Israeli soldiers also fired on Khiam, where Israeli forces had blown up a house. Israeli warplanes also struck the outskirts of Baraashit, in the Bint Jbeil district, targeting a house, early Friday morning. Israeli forces bombarded the strategic Ali Taher hill in southern Lebanon for more than five hours overnight, with artillery fire beginning after 11 p.m. and continuing until around 5 a.m., L'Orient Today reported. Explosions heard over Tyre as PM Salam tells army its deployment restores state "sovereignty, authority and prestige": Explosions were heard over the southern Lebanese city of Tyre (Sour) on Friday as Prime Minister Nawaf Salam a speech at the Benoit Barakat Barracks, Lebanon's National News Agency reported. Speaking as Israeli attacks on Lebanon continue, Salam said restoring sovereignty requires "one strong army" and bringing all of southern Lebanon under the authority of the state. He said the Lebanese state and its constitutional institutions must regain the "decision of war and peace," describing the army's deployment in the south as the restoration of state "sovereignty, authority and prestige." U.S. issues sanctions on Hezbollah: The U.S. Treasury Department 10 people it says form a network smuggling cash to Hezbollah, and redesignated Hezbollah itself as operating "under the command" of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps-Quds Force (IRGC-QF), OFAC announced Thursday. The Treasury Department accused the network of using couriers on commercial flights between Lebanon, Turkey, the UAE, and Iran to move "up to hundreds of millions of dollars," giving Hezbollah a channel outside the banking system to obtain foreign currency and evade sanctions. A State Department official said the redesignation is meant to show Hezbollah is "not a stand-alone operation" but acts for Iran. Hezbollah to the sanctions on Friday morning, rejecting its characterization as "under the command" of the IRGC, adding it did not need anyone to certify its Lebanese identity or patriotism, and describing its relationship with Iran as a "close and fraternal" relationship. It described the move as part of longstanding U.S. policies aimed at targeting Hezbollah through political, financial, and security pressure, which it said was intended to "protect the security of the Israeli enemy," and said the sanctions would "not deter" its fight against Israel. U.S. News Progressive Aisha Wahab wins California special election, dealing blow to AIPAC-backed opponent : State Senator Aisha Wahab transit official Melissa Hernandez in the special election to fill former Representative Eric Swalwell 's House seat, despite Hernandez's backing from the American Israel Public Affairs Committee's super PAC, United Democracy Project, which spent roughly $2.5 million in the race. Wahab, who opposes unconditional aid to Israel and has characterized Israel's conduct in Gaza as a "genocide," will represent the district for the remainder of the year. Emails reveal ICE quietly coordinated with Iran on deportation flights : Newly released emails obtained by the National Iranian American Council show U.S. immigration officials worked with Iranian government representatives to deport more than 100 Iranians on three flights between September 2025 and January 2026, with Iranian officials influencing which individuals were included on deportation manifests and ICE at times heeding last-minute requests from the Iranian Embassy, according to CBS News. The coordination continued even during the June 2025 U.S.-Israel war with Iran. Then-acting ICE Director Todd Lyons called Iranian repatriation a "priority" days after President Donald Trump warned Tehran residents to evacuate, and an ICE official described the deportations as a "White House priority" despite Iran's closed airspace. A separate lawsuit filed by Iranian asylum seekers in July alleges ICE illegally shared confidential information with Iranian officials while the migrants were in detention. Trans migrants in ICE detention losing rights, medical care, NYT finds : The federal government has halted specialized care for transgender detainees at more than 10 immigration detention centers and deleted an Obama-era policy assuring the basic rights of transgender people in immigration custody, according to a Thursday from The New York Times. Camila Toro de Paula , a 25-year-old transgender Venezuelan asylum seeker who has spent 11 months in a men's facility in Jena, Louisiana, described being assaulted, denied hormone treatment, and held in solitary confinement without consistent water access to the Times. Another transgender asylum seeker, Wilmar Quintero , who left her native Venezuela after being tortured by police officers for her transgender identity, described being sexually assaulted while detained in Michigan before she was deported in April. DHS spied on at least five Midwest churches amid anti-ICE activist probe, court records show: Court filings that emerged last week DHS agents surveilled five churches in Minnesota and Michigan as part of an investigation into activists opposing ICE known as "Operation Puppet Master." Undercover agents attended events at First Universalist Church of Minneapolis and University Baptist Church, with one undercover agent attending a Mixed Martial Arts class at University Baptist Church in May with a hidden audio recorder, and another agent collecting license plate information near St. John the Evangelist Episcopal Church in St. Paul during an April activist meeting. The revelations raise questions about whether DHS violated a February court injunction barring warrantless enforcement actions at churches. Texas Gov. Abbott targets Muslim washing stations at airports : Texas Gov. Greg Abbott a letter Friday to the heads of Houston and Dallas-Fort Worth airports alleging that their Muslim wudu washing stations constituted "religious discrimination." Abbott, has consistently pursued anti-Muslim policies, asked the U.S. Department of Transportation to investigate and warned his office is "reviewing all grants" to entities involved, according to The Washington Post. Missouri judge allows Trump-backed congressional map for November election : Cole County Circuit Judge Daniel Green Wednesday that Missouri's new Republican-friendly U.S. House districts can be used in November, rejecting a bid by the group People Not Politicians to put the map to a statewide referendum. The redistricting, prompted by President Donald Trump's push for Republican-led states to redraw boundaries ahead of the midterms, targets Democratic Rep. Emanuel Cleaver by splitting Kansas City among Republican-held districts and extending his 5th District into rural GOP territory, with about 59% of the district's voters newly assigned under the plan. People Not Politicians executive director Richard von Glahn said the group plans to appeal to the Missouri Supreme Court. Missouri's fight joins roughly a dozen lawsuits nationally over redistricting efforts that could net Republicans up to 16 additional House seats across eight states. Research finds over 150 Polymarket wallets likely traded on inside U.S. military information: More than 150 wallets on Polymarket International to have traded on insider U.S. military information, collectively earning $8 million with a 97.2% win rate on defense-related bets, according to research from the nonprofit Anti-Corruption Data Collective. ACDC also found that bets from these accounts appear to attract copycat wagers from larger traders and automated bots, including $200,000 and $100,000 copycat bets placed hours before June 2025 U.S. strikes on Iran. Private prison giant GEO Group donated $1.4 million to pro-Trump PAC after landing major ICE contracts : GEO Group's reentry services division contributed $1.4 million to MAGA Inc., a super PAC supporting President Donald Trump, in July, according to Federal Election Commission records reviewed by The Lever, just weeks after the company secured two five-year Department of Homeland Security contracts to operate ICE detention facilities in Colorado and North Carolina worth a combined estimated $165 million in annual revenue. The Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment recently sued GEO Group, forcing the company to allow state inspectors to investigate a tuberculosis outbreak at one of its facilities. More on the GEO Group's political activities is available from The Lever . 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News Ebola virus outbreak in DRC "growing exponentially": The Ebola virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is "growing exponentially," the UN warned on Friday. Julien Harneis, the UN's Senior Ebola Coordinator, said in a that more than 2,500 people had died in the last three months, with over half of all deaths occurring in just the last 20 days. "The epidemic is spreading to an area that is bigger than France. And the outbreak is growing faster and wider than the Ebola response," Harneis said. He also stressed the "brutal" conditions facing healthcare workers with 160 healthcare workers contracting Ebola, with 43 dying. U.S. imposes new Cuba sanctions, detains Americans returning from island: The Treasury and State departments new sanctions Thursday against nine Cuban state-owned mining, metal, and construction companies, and on the leadership of the Cuban Institute of Friendship with the Peoples, which Secretary of State Marco Rubio accused of sponsoring "a vast subversive network in the United States aimed at identifying, cultivating, and radicalizing" Americans, according to the Associated Press. The move follows an operation at the Miami airport last weekend in which several Americans returning from Cuba after attending events marking Fidel Castro's 100th birthday were briefly detained and had electronic devices seized for inspection. Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodriguez said that the U.S. imposed the sanctions with the "deliberate aim of harming" the country's economy "to prevent the provision of basic services to the population." The measures add to an oil blockade the U.S. imposed earlier this year following the removal of Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro, which has resulted in regular blackouts and medical shortages on the island. Imran Khan sent back to prison hours after hospital visit: Former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan was briefly , declared medically fit, and returned to prison within hours early Friday, a move his Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf party said violated a Supreme Court order requiring him to remain under medical supervision until at least mid-September. Khan's sister, Uzma Khan, said he told her he was being "repeatedly" tortured in prison, and party officials accused authorities of "contempt of the Supreme Court" after Khan was examined at a state-run hospital, contrary to a court order mandating that he be treated at a private facility. Khan has been imprisoned since August 2023 on charges he has characterized as "politically motivated." PTI officials have announced a nationwide march, planned to take place on September 27, in response to his medical deterioration. Separately, Zulfikar Bukhari, a top aide to Khan, told Reuters on Thursday that the former PM would not confront army chief Asim Munir if freed, marking a significant shift in rhetoric from a party whose supporters have long rallied against the military leader they blame for Khan's 2023 imprisonment. Hundreds protest against Tunisian President Kais Saied: Hundreds of protesters in Tunis Thursday calling for President Kais Saied's ouster and rejecting what they called "one-man rule" and "a slide towards dictatorship," urging the release of jailed opposition figures, activists, and journalists, Al Jazeera reported. The demonstration follows a similar protest on July 25 marking the anniversary of Saied's 2021 dismissal of the government and suspension of parliament. Saied, a 68-year-old former constitutional lawyer elected in 2019 on an anti-corruption platform, has faced international criticism for consolidating control over the judiciary and overseeing mass trials of political opponents. The country has been racked by mounting economic pressure, with inflation at 5.2%, according to the World Bank. Protests have also emerged in response to widespread water and power cuts, and the environmental problems that accompanied wildfires that hit the country earlier this summer. HRW: Russian paramilitaries "summarily killed" nine Mali civilians, including four children: Human Rights Watch Thursday that Russia's Africa Corps summarily killed nine civilians, including four children, in Mali's central Mopti region in the presence of Malian soldiers earlier last month, alleging the paramilitary group also beat dozens of people and burned at least eight homes. HRW said more than 100 Africa Corps fighters rounded up at least 80 men and boys in Bombori village on July 10, beating them while interrogating them about alleged ties to armed groups, before shooting six who tried to escape and executing three others in custody, one allegedly by beheading. The killings come amid Mali's ongoing civil war against armed groups linked to al-Qaeda and ISIL, with Russia's Africa Corps having become the country's main military partner since Bamako's relations with Western nations, particularly its former colonizer France, deteriorated following the military's 2021 seizure of power. Ukraine hits Russian oil and power sites in overnight drone barrage, blacking out much of Crimea: Ukraine a wave of Russian energy targets overnight into Thursday, Aug. 20, in one of its heaviest long-range drone campaigns of the war, hitting oil refineries, a Black Sea export terminal, and a substation feeding occupied Crimea, according to Ukraine's General Staff. Ukrainian drones struck a substation in Krasnodar Krai, which provides Russian-occupied Crimea with much of its power, leading to a blackout in the area overnight. Drones also struck an export terminal at Volna and a refinery in Tatarstan. RSF attacks kill six, displace over 1,000 in Sudan 's North Kordofan: Rapid Support Forces fighters the villages of Um Dareisa and Al-Shaqla in Sudan's North Kordofan state Wednesday, killing six civilians and forcing more than 1,000 people to flee on foot to the state capital El Obeid, Sudan Tribune reported. A local official accused RSF fighters of widespread abuses in the area in recent days, including unlawful killings, physical assaults, sexual violence, looting supplies at gunpoint, and forced displacement. The attack follows a raid last week on the nearby town of Um Arda that killed 18 people and displaced more than 300 families. U.S. deportees arrive in Liberia: Twenty people deported from the United States at Roberts International Airport outside Monrovia on Thursday, the first group transferred under a $5 million deal allowing the U.S. to send up to 1,200 third-country deportees to Liberia over the next year. Liberian officials said the group will include people from Africa, North and South America, and the Caribbean, but most of the first arrivals came from Latin America, including Venezuela and Cuba. Syria weighs joining security pact with Pakistan, Turkey, Saudi Arabia: Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad Hassan al-Shaibani said Damascus was whether to join the trilateral "Mecca Joint Defence Agreement" between Turkey, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, but has not yet made a decision. Speaking on a state visit to Islamabad, al-Shaibani said Syria was seeking to deepen ties with Pakistan, with the two sides moving toward exchanging ambassadors, establishing direct flights and reviving a joint ministerial commission. Hong Kong Tiananmen vigil organizers convicted under national security law: Lee Cheuk-yan and Chow Hang-tung, former leaders of the Hong Kong Alliance in Support of Patriotic Democratic Movements of China, were Friday of inciting subversion, following a national security law imposed on the region by the Chinese government. Both were charged in 2021 after organizing annual vigils in commemoration of China's 1989 Tiananmen Square crackdown. Lee and Chow now face up to 10 years in prison. Judge rules Palestine Action did not violate UK terrorism laws: UK Judge Robert Altham ruled on Friday that five Palestine Action activists would not be sentenced under the country's terrorism laws, after the cohort was found guilty in June of causing $290,000 worth of damage to a Barclays Bank during an August 2024 protest against the bank's shareholdings in the Israeli defense company Elbit Systems. | | ---|---|--- 📖 The Israeli Siege of Palestinian Families in Qusra Is Part of an Escalating Tactic 🛒 for your Drop News/Not Bombs Hoodie 💬 our Whatsapp Broadcast Channel for the latest reporting, podcasts, and breaking news, delivered directly ⚠️ You can go to your to unsubscribe from the Drop Site Daily newsletter--while still getting the rest of our reporting Become a Drop Site News Paid Subscriber Drop Site News is reader-supported. Friend, It's happening. We knew it would. We knew Kim would build the foundation of a winning campaign. | Friend,
---

My name is Mary Peltola, and after Tuesday’s primary, I am officially running in the general election for United States Senate in Alaska.

I want to share with you why I made the decision to run – and to ask for your support as we begin the general election together.

But if you already understand how important this race and your support are, and you’re ready to join our fight for fish, family, and freedom, please use this button to split a contribution between my campaign for U.S. Senate and Jacky Rosen’s:

---
Now here’s a bit more on how I came to this decision.

When I was growing up in Bethel, salmon fishing with my father in the summers and dog mushing in the winters, Alaska was a place of abundance.

Now, all across Alaska, we have scarcity.

Multi-national companies are trawling our waters and decimating our fish stocks. The moose, caribou, and migratory birds that used to fill our freezers are harder to find.

So we buy more groceries, where the prices are just crushing Alaska families.

And I've got to tell you, DC people do not care that we are paying nearly 20 bucks for a gallon of fuel. They don’t even believe us.

They're focused on their own wallets – not ours.

And when they actually work together on something, it’s usually to help themselves. The rigged system in DC is shutting down Alaska and hurting all of us while politicians and their millionaire and billionaire donors feather their own nest.

It’s why our prices keep rising, all while the healthcare and services Alaskans rely on get gutted.

I'm done with politicians getting richer while things get tougher here at home.

My agenda for Alaska will always be: fish, family, freedom. These values have been the core values of my campaigns since the very beginning.

But if we’re going to secure Alaska’s future, we need another priority: fighting corruption.

I'm running for Alaska's Senate seat because it is the fight for our future.

The future of work in the age of artificial intelligence.| | | |
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137663075/641531949/-642992695?amount=25&refcode=260821em_sjj_aitaxbill-rs&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84OTMxMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwZDM2ODkwZC03YTlkLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=R4BBp-8160bdt6Q2O6sNLshcG9UE0ZOcjmQaf_xHuXM=)
---
Friends, I want to talk to you about something that’s been keeping me up at night: the future of work in the age of AI.

The CEO of AI giant Anthropic has predicted _Great Depression levels of unemployment within the next five years_ , while Bill Gates has said that humans won't be needed at all for most things within a decade. Corporate leaders at Intuit, Oracle, and Block are already citing AI as the reason for mass layoffs. And young workers in AI-exposed careers are struggling to find jobs.

_The impacts of AI are already here, and the federal government has no real plan to deal with them._ Meanwhile, AI billionaires are positioning themselves to make _trillions_ off AI systems trained on human work and ultimately designed to push out workers.

We need to make sure AI augments human labor, not replaces it — and it is the job of the federal government to set up systems that support our workforce and economy. **That's why I just introduced the AI Tax and Work Protection Act, a bill that levies a tax on AI companies based on their usage and revenue.**

The tax rate starts low, but if unemployment rises as a result of AI, the rate rises with it. Revenue from the tax goes directly into a trust fund that powers a new Work Protection Administration, a jobs program housed in the Department of Labor that provides grants to states, cities, tribes, nonprofits, unions, and educational institutions to create good jobs.

**In plain English: if AI companies eliminate jobs, they’ll pay more in taxes, and that money will go directly to creating new jobs in the public interest to replace the ones lost.**

Right now, companies effectively get a tax break for automating jobs. My bill reverses that.

I’m proud to be leading this fight, and I’m going to push as hard as I can in the House to get this bill through and advocate for workers — but you know as well as I do that real progress is going to depend on whether we take back a Democratic majority this November.

**[If you want to see this legislation and more like it actually move forward, will you contribute to our efforts to flip the House? We have less than 75 days left until Election Day, and it’s going to take everyone working together to get this done.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137663077/641531954/-642992695?refcode=260821em_sjj_aitaxbill-rs&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84OTMxMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwZDM2ODkwZC03YTlkLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=R4BBp-8160bdt6Q2O6sNLshcG9UE0ZOcjmQaf_xHuXM=)**

clean_body: The future of work in the age of artificial intelligence.| | | | = Friends, I want to talk to you about something that’s been keeping me up at night: the future of work in the age of AI. The CEO of AI giant Anthropic has predicted Great Depression levels of unemployment within the next five years , while Bill Gates has said that humans won't be needed at all for most things within a decade. Corporate leaders at Intuit, Oracle, and Block are already citing AI as the reason for mass layoffs. And young workers in AI-exposed careers are struggling to find jobs. The impacts of AI are already here, and the federal government has no real plan to deal with them. Meanwhile, AI billionaires are positioning themselves to make trillions off AI systems trained on human work and ultimately designed to push out workers. We need to make sure AI augments human labor, not replaces it — and it is the job of the federal government to set up systems that support our workforce and economy. That's why I just introduced the AI Tax and Work Protection Act, a bill that levies a tax on AI companies based on their usage and revenue. The tax rate starts low, but if unemployment rises as a result of AI, the rate rises with it. Revenue from the tax goes directly into a trust fund that powers a new Work Protection Administration, a jobs program housed in the Department of Labor that provides grants to states, cities, tribes, nonprofits, unions, and educational institutions to create good jobs. In plain English: if AI companies eliminate jobs, they’ll pay more in taxes, and that money will go directly to creating new jobs in the public interest to replace the ones lost. Right now, companies effectively get a tax break for automating jobs. My bill reverses that. I’m proud to be leading this fight, and I’m going to push as hard as I can in the House to get this bill through and advocate for workers — but you know as well as I do that real progress is going to depend on whether we take back a Democratic majority this November. = If you’ve saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | = | = ---|--- = | = = | = | | | Thank you for being in this fight with me! — Sara = Congresswoman Sara JacobsCalifornia’s 51st District = | = Paid for by Sara Jacobs for Congress Sara Jacobs for Congress PO Box 120085 San Diego, CA 92112 United States | | | | | | ---|---|--- We believe these emails are a critical way for Sara to stay in touch with supporters and constituents. Peter, I need to be candid with you.

Our grassroots fundraising isn’t where it needs to be right now, and we’ve had to drop our August projections.
At the same time as we’re falling behind, the GOP’s money, lies and attacks against me are ramping up. They’re pouring nearly $100 million so far into this race to defeat me – because if we lose in North Carolina, Democrats will have no shot at taking back the Senate.
**Now, the polls are tightening, and my opponent, Republican Michael Whatley, is within striking distance of taking the lead.**
The only way we can protect our narrow edge and keep powering forward is with a surge of grassroots support from people like you – so today, I’m trying something different. **I’m lowering my ask to just $1 in the hopes that every person reading this message chips in.**
While we have fundraising goals to hit, what matters most to me today is how many contributions we’re able to get in the door. Every dollar adds up fast when we’re all pitching in, and together, we can rebuild our momentum and show the strength of this grassroots movement.
**[Please, Peter, will you chip in $1 to help me flip North Carolina and take back the Senate for Democrats?](https://act.roycooper.com/go/19551?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1151&t=8&akid=2900%2E124072%2EX2Uu_6)**

Fellow Republicans,
This week, my friend Rob Rohrbough, who is a thoughtful, faith-filled, and reasoned thinker shared with me some of his thoughts on the necessity of the Christian vote. I want to pass on his thoughts to you. The Bill of Rights to the US Constitution includes in the First Amendment "Congress shall make no law respecting an establishment of religion, or prohibiting the free exercise thereof." This right is important to people of all faiths. We have seen in Communist countries where faith in God is suppressed, attacked, and/or abolished by government in order to have government replace God as the arbiter of our conscience and conduct. We have history to show us and our faith to guide us, so let us not sleepwalk into allowing it to happen in the Nebraska or the United States at large.
Pews to Politics Why Christians Need to be Involved in Politics Saturday, August 8, 2026 Rob Rohrbough

Have you ever thought politics was dirty and messy? As Christians, the most important thing in our lives is our relationship with Jesus Christ. Does it stop there? What about the Great Commission? What about defending our right to carry out The Great Commission? Or even practice Christianity?
Do you know that there is a movement to take away your right to evangelize? In 1964 the Department of Education implemented the results mainly of three court cases -- McCollum v Board of Education in 1948, Engel v Vitale in 1962, and Murray v Curlett in 1963 -- to remove God, prayer, and the Bible from public schools. How can we expect the Christian culture upon which our nation was founded to continue? That precedent has encouraged movement to a more secular society over the past 60+ years. Church attendance has dropped and more people consider capitalism to be evil and selfish. Young people in particular are starting to consider socialism a preferable economic model.
With that background, how can church-going Christians be content to let others determine how government should work? Who gets elected? There is an old cliche -- if Christians do not get involved in politics, they will be ruled by those who do not believe nor share their values. Our current president put it even more strongly -- "If Christians don't get involved in politics, politics will erase their right to be Christians." These are no idle speculations. I have observed the willful decline over six decades.
So, what do we do? Register to vote if you haven't already. Don't register as an independent. Register in a party so you can have influence in it. Be sure your party supports Christian principles and values. Become active in it. Examine its platform so you know where it stands. Long term, influence the platform if it does not fully support those values. Once you are comfortable with your party's principles, examine the candidates and how they align with those principles and your priorities as a Christian. Help them win in every way you can with your time, talent, and treasure.

How can we expect the Christian culture upon which our nation was founded to continue? That precedent has encouraged movement to a more secular society over the past 60+ years. Church attendance has dropped and more people consider capitalism to be evil and selfish. Young people in particular are starting to consider socialism a preferable economic model. With that background, how can church-going Christians be content to let others determine how government should work? Who gets elected? There is an old cliche -- if Christians do not get involved in politics, they will be ruled by those who do not believe nor share their values. Our current president put it even more strongly -- "If Christians don't get involved in politics, politics will erase their right to be Christians." These are no idle speculations. I have observed the willful decline over six decades. So, what do we do? Register to vote if you haven't already. Don't register as an independent. Register in a party so you can have influence in it. Be sure your party supports Christian principles and values. Become active in it. Examine its platform so you know where it stands. Long term, influence the platform if it does not fully support those values. Once you are comfortable with your party's principles, examine the candidates and how they align with those principles and your priorities as a Christian. Help them win in every way you can with your time, talent, and treasure. Short term, identify others who sit with you on that pew and are not active politically. Help them understand how important it is to get involved. You have several resources at your command to prepare you for the task. Here are a few from my Facebook page: Christians not to fall into Satan's trap == and the need to return to Jesus Christ. to engage David and Tim Barton's answer to, "==" And a few more: The sin of pietism -- == Kirk's minister). on 250th) == (also Wallbuilders) Those who disagree with you know how to get out the vote, and they do not intend to allow Christianity to thrive. Lord of Hosts Church encourages their members to be active politically. Dr. Dodd at Westside Church does a good job. Some churches, including mine, do not encourage political activity. Does yours? Would the United States exist without the activism of preachers like the Muellenberg brothers? Would Christianity be one of the three major world religions had the Apostles Paul or Luke worried only about their own relationship with Christ? When the righteous are in authority, the people rejoice: but when the wicked beareth rule, the people mourn. Proverbs 29:2 (KJV) | | == | Together, We Win! * * *
Hey folks,
My dad and I disagree about a lot. And I mean **a lot**.
For the first episode of _**Nellis vs. Nellis**_ , I sat down with my Trump-voting, retired FBI agent father to talk about the DOJ coming after my company, the bizarre Natalie Harp story, ICE's new stun gloves, and what happens when politics gets personal.
We agreed. We argued. At one point my own father accused me of pivoting from political corruption to World War II. This one got heated--but that's exactly why I think these conversations matter.
* [**00:02:14**] My dad reacts to the DOJ inquiry into my company--and explains the questions he'd want answered as a retired FBI agent.
* [**00:10:03**] We get into one of our oldest arguments: are all politicians corrupt, or does pretending they're all equally bad help people like Trump?
* [**00:15:10**] Natalie Harp enters the chat, and we try to make sense of one of the strangest relationships inside Trump's White House.
* [**00:30:34**] We debate ICE's new stun gloves, law enforcement training, and whether giving agents another less-lethal tool makes anyone safer.
* [**00:39:17**] The conversation gets genuinely heated over Alex Pretti, guns, protests, police accountability, and what "following orders" actually means.

This is what I want _Nellis vs. Nellis_ to be: two people who love each other, see the country very differently, and are still willing to sit down and actually talk. No cable-news performance. No pretending the disagreements aren't real. And no giving up on each other because politics gets uncomfortable. **If you value honest conversations like this --and want to help us build a place where they can keep happening--help me keep them going.**

--Mike

We have an opportunity this November to change the course of our country.

Control of the Senate comes down to a net gain of four seats. Republicans know it as well as we do, and they are not planning to hold their majority by virtue of their policies and arguments. _They are planning to outspend us._

Dark money donors. Handpicked self-funders. Super PACs behind every vulnerable Republican on the map. All to hold onto their Senate majority.

And we know what a Republican majority does with its oversight power, because we have watched it sit unused for two years. They will do nothing.

The president has personally taken in billions since taking office, and this Senate has not asked him or his cronies a single question about it under oath. He has gone after the machinery of our elections, and this Senate has called it overreach to object. A Senate that will not use its subpoena power is a Senate that has decided the president answers to no one.

We must flip four seats to take power, and there are eight places to get them — North Carolina, Ohio, Maine, Alaska, Iowa, Florida, Mississippi and Texas. Every one is winnable and not one is safe.

body:
Over the years, I have met brave men and women who dedicate their lives to rescuing children from trafficking and exploitation.

| | | |
---
| |
---
| | GOD'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE
---
|
---
| | | Friend, A child who has been trafficked often learns a heartbreaking lesson: **Don't trust anyone. **
**Not adults.**
**Not authority figures.** Not even the people trying to help. That is one of the many reasons I am writing to you today. My name is Eduardo Verastegui. I am the producer of the film _Sound of Freedom_ and founder of the Sound of Freedom Foundation. After learning firsthand about the horrors of child trafficking, I dedicated my life to helping protect vulnerable children and supporting efforts to stop this evil. Over the years, I have met brave men and women who dedicate their lives to rescuing children from trafficking and exploitation. They walk into places most of us could never imagine. They investigate crimes no human being should ever have to see. They sit with children whose innocence has been stolen. And they carry those memories with them. **Day after day.**
**Year after year.** **That burden is heavy. **
---
[ Give Now. Bring Comfort.](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckT1v3DAMhn-NvMXQhz90g4YC7m0pii4dBR5FnYVIlivJCfrvC19u6ZqRfMmHeMDfr_YVQgzb_QckMqV5W6pNRC1vlH1bKeXa9vxBxR8xWcnl9ML1ixQWsIV3smPnjEMHAjsyYtazkhc96241Qg3uotFJcuMonXYaL8MMKBD1RLPsgjlxXEshJiXE1N8uk5MkYOQ3NfMR2cAhUml9of24xYCwNahvPhekHnPqollb2ytT35i8MnmthEehvuZjc9n7QuRy8mcFLeStz-V-TmVvU47x70PHAv5h6lrzUZAsZkdMLb--_1yE4oPQTE5HSzaRC0diaqEEIT6bnztMLSsUB_XtgfqMENIO4b4xtfx_7pk3KietK8btHyHGUKeZDfx-0h9q7WvPeDfyXwAAAP__Snqd5g)
---
Sometimes heavier than words can describe. And that is why I want you to meet someone very special. Her name is **Molly.**
---
[](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckT1v3DAMhn-NvMXQhz90g4YC7m0pii4dBR5FnYVIlivJCfrvC19u6ZqRfMmHeMDfr_YVQgzb_QckMqV5W6pNRC1vlH1bKeXa9vxBxR8xWcnl9ML1ixQWsIV3smPnjEMHAjsyYtazkhc96241Qg3uotFJcuMonXYaL8MMKBD1RLPsgjlxXEshJiXE1N8uk5MkYOQ3NfMR2cAhUml9of24xYCwNahvPhekHnPqollb2ytT35i8MnmthEehvuZjc9n7QuRy8mcFLeStz-V-TmVvU47x70PHAv5h6lrzUZAsZkdMLb--_1yE4oPQTE5HSzaRC0diaqEEIT6bnztMLSsUB_XtgfqMENIO4b4xtfx_7pk3KietK8btHyHGUKeZDfx-0h9q7WvPeDfyXwAAAP__Snqd5g)
---
**Molly** is a Labradoodle. But to the officers, investigators, and rescued children she serves, she is so much more than a dog. **She is a source of comfort.**
**A source of peace.**
**A source of healing.** When an officer has spent hours working a difficult trafficking case, when they've witnessed evil no person should ever have to witness and the weight of the day feels almost unbearable...**Molly** quietly walks over. She leans against them.
And she stays. **She does not ask questions.**
**She does not need explanations.** **Her presence alone reminds them they are not carrying this burden by themselves. **Sometimes that simple moment is enough to help someone breathe again.
---
[ Give Now. Bring Comfort.](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckT1v3DAMhn-NvMXQhz90g4YC7m0pii4dBR5FnYVIlivJCfrvC19u6ZqRfMmHeMDfr_YVQgzb_QckMqV5W6pNRC1vlH1bKeXa9vxBxR8xWcnl9ML1ixQWsIV3smPnjEMHAjsyYtazkhc96241Qg3uotFJcuMonXYaL8MMKBD1RLPsgjlxXEshJiXE1N8uk5MkYOQ3NfMR2cAhUml9of24xYCwNahvPhekHnPqollb2ytT35i8MnmthEehvuZjc9n7QuRy8mcFLeStz-V-TmVvU47x70PHAv5h6lrzUZAsZkdMLb--_1yE4oPQTE5HSzaRC0diaqEEIT6bnztMLSsUB_XtgfqMENIO4b4xtfx_7pk3KietK8btHyHGUKeZDfx-0h9q7WvPeDfyXwAAAP__Snqd5g)
---
But **Molly's** work does not stop there. Some of the children rescued from trafficking are terrified, confused, and broken. Many have been manipulated for so long that they do not immediately trust the people trying to help them. Imagine that. Rescue has arrived. But trauma has taught them to fear everyone. **Then Molly enters the room.** No uniform. No questions. No pressure. **Just gentleness and love.**
---
[](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckT1v3DAMhn-NvMXQhz90g4YC7m0pii4dBR5FnYVIlivJCfrvC19u6ZqRfMmHeMDfr_YVQgzb_QckMqV5W6pNRC1vlH1bKeXa9vxBxR8xWcnl9ML1ixQWsIV3smPnjEMHAjsyYtazkhc96241Qg3uotFJcuMonXYaL8MMKBD1RLPsgjlxXEshJiXE1N8uk5MkYOQ3NfMR2cAhUml9of24xYCwNahvPhekHnPqollb2ytT35i8MnmthEehvuZjc9n7QuRy8mcFLeStz-V-TmVvU47x70PHAv5h6lrzUZAsZkdMLb--_1yE4oPQTE5HSzaRC0diaqEEIT6bnztMLSsUB_XtgfqMENIO4b4xtfx_7pk3KietK8btHyHGUKeZDfx-0h9q7WvPeDfyXwAAAP__Snqd5g)
---
And somehow, walls begin to come down. Small hands reach out. Tears begin to flow. Fear begins to soften. **And healing can begin.** **That healing does not happen by accident.** It happens because one of our trusted anti-trafficking partners walks alongside survivors and the agencies that serve them.

They provide trauma-informed support, resources, and advocacy for lives shattered by trafficking.

Every day, they help children move from fear to freedom, from exploitation to safety, and from hopelessness to renewed hope.
---
[ Give Now. Bring Comfort.](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckT1v3DAMhn-NvMXQhz90g4YC7m0pii4dBR5FnYVIlivJCfrvC19u6ZqRfMmHeMDfr_YVQgzb_QckMqV5W6pNRC1vlH1bKeXa9vxBxR8xWcnl9ML1ixQWsIV3smPnjEMHAjsyYtazkhc96241Qg3uotFJcuMonXYaL8MMKBD1RLPsgjlxXEshJiXE1N8uk5MkYOQ3NfMR2cAhUml9of24xYCwNahvPhekHnPqollb2ytT35i8MnmthEehvuZjc9n7QuRy8mcFLeStz-V-TmVvU47x70PHAv5h6lrzUZAsZkdMLb--_1yE4oPQTE5HSzaRC0diaqEEIT6bnztMLSsUB_XtgfqMENIO4b4xtfx_7pk3KietK8btHyHGUKeZDfx-0h9q7WvPeDfyXwAAAP__Snqd5g)
---
I have seen firsthand how powerful these moments can be. They remind me of the words of Jesus: "Let the little children come to Me and do not hinder them." (Matthew 19:14) Every child deserves safety, protection and **every child deserves to know they are loved.** **And sometimes God uses something as simple as a dog named Molly to help a hurting child take the first step toward healing.** What many people do not realize is that dogs like **Molly** require up to two years of specialized training. They are carefully prepared to remain calm in chaotic situations. They comfort children experiencing trauma and support officers carrying enormous emotional burdens.

They serve in places where hope can feel hard to find. This training, care, and support are only possible because compassionate people choose to stand with this mission.

clean_body: Over the years, I have met brave men and women who dedicate their lives to rescuing children from trafficking and exploitation. | | | | | | | | GOD'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE | | | | Friend, A child who has been trafficked often learns a heartbreaking lesson: Don't trust anyone. Not adults. Not authority figures. Not even the people trying to help. That is one of the many reasons I am writing to you today. My name is Eduardo Verastegui. I am the producer of the film Sound of Freedom and founder of the Sound of Freedom Foundation. After learning firsthand about the horrors of child trafficking, I dedicated my life to helping protect vulnerable children and supporting efforts to stop this evil. Over the years, I have met brave men and women who dedicate their lives to rescuing children from trafficking and exploitation. They walk into places most of us could never imagine. They investigate crimes no human being should ever have to see. They sit with children whose innocence has been stolen. And they carry those memories with them. Day after day. Year after year. That burden is heavy. Sometimes heavier than words can describe. And that is why I want you to meet someone very special. Her name is Molly. Molly is a Labradoodle. But to the officers, investigators, and rescued children she serves, she is so much more than a dog. She is a source of comfort. A source of peace. A source of healing. When an officer has spent hours working a difficult trafficking case, when they've witnessed evil no person should ever have to witness and the weight of the day feels almost unbearable...Molly quietly walks over. She leans against them. And she stays. She does not ask questions. She does not need explanations. Her presence alone reminds them they are not carrying this burden by themselves. Sometimes that simple moment is enough to help someone breathe again. But Molly's work does not stop there. Some of the children rescued from trafficking are terrified, confused, and broken. Many have been manipulated for so long that they do not immediately trust the people trying to help them. Imagine that. Rescue has arrived. But trauma has taught them to fear everyone. Then Molly enters the room. No uniform. No questions. No pressure. Just gentleness and love. And somehow, walls begin to come down. Small hands reach out. Tears begin to flow. Fear begins to soften. And healing can begin. That healing does not happen by accident. It happens because one of our trusted anti-trafficking partners walks alongside survivors and the agencies that serve them. They provide trauma-informed support, resources, and advocacy for lives shattered by trafficking. Every day, they help children move from fear to freedom, from exploitation to safety, and from hopelessness to renewed hope. I have seen firsthand how powerful these moments can be. They remind me of the words of Jesus: "Let the little children come to Me and do not hinder them." (Matthew 19:14) Every child deserves safety, protection and every child deserves to know they are loved. And sometimes God uses something as simple as a dog named Molly to help a hurting child take the first step toward healing. What many people do not realize is that dogs like Molly require up to two years of specialized training. They are carefully prepared to remain calm in chaotic situations. They comfort children experiencing trauma and support officers carrying enormous emotional burdens. They serve in places where hope can feel hard to find. This training, care, and support are only possible because compassionate people choose to stand with this mission. Friend, every rescue operation involves people willing to walk into darkness so others can find freedom. But even heroes need support. And so do the children they serve.And sometimes healing begins with four paws, a gentle heart, and a quiet presence named Molly. Today, I am asking if you will become part of that healing. Because every child matters. Every rescue matters. And every act of compassion matters. Will you make your first gift today? Together, we can help protect God's children and bring light into some of the darkest places on earth. With gratitude and prayer, Eduardo Verastegui Sound of Freedom, Producer For the Sound of Freedom Foundation P.S. Molly cannot rescue a child by herself. But she helps wounded children begin to trust again. She helps exhausted officers keep going. And she reminds everyone she meets that compassion still exists. Your gift today helps provide that healing presence where it is needed most. 6671 Southwest Freeway, Suite 700, Houston TX 77074 Pop Acta Media | Republican Task Force PO Box 461 Fort Collins, CO 80522 |

Peter,
Did you see Kailee’s message?
I wanted to forward it because we are now just $1,456 away from fully funding our next wave of ads, and the deadline is TONIGHT at midnight.
_**If we come up short, we will have to cut placements and leave voters unreached. In a race this important, that is a risk we cannot take.**_
Can Kailee count on you to rush a contribution before midnight?
[**QUICK DONATE $35 >> **](https://us.list-manage.com/Vy4mkPABWyb?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)

Kailee is working every day to carry our message directly to Central New Yorkers. Your support right now will help make sure voters hear it.
Thanks for being on this team!

From: Kailee Buller for CongressTo: dpwillis67@gmail.com

Peter,
This race will be won by reaching voters where they are... and telling them exactly what is at stake.
Central New York families are paying more for groceries, utilities, housing, healthcare, and childcare. Farmers and small businesses are buried in red tape. Too many young people believe they have to leave home to find opportunity.
_The people of this district deserve to know there is another choice._
That is why my team is preparing our next wave of digital, television, and radio ads to take our message directly to voters across NY-22.
**But our placement deadline is at MIDNIGHT, and we still need to raise $6,932 to fully fund the campaign.**
[**Will you chip in $25, $50, $100, or whatever you can before midnight to help us get these ads in front of Central New York voters?**](https://us.list-manage.com/oFUPz0FFTxt?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)

# DNC Sues Trump Administration for Records on Ballot Seizures
---
| | | | _The Trump administration has refused to comply with the DNC’s FOIA requests regarding ballot seizures during the upcoming election_
Today, the DNC sued the Trump administration over its failure to respond to Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) requests seeking records about any plans to seize ballots in the midterm elections. The DNC requested these records to defend the integrity of our elections from attempts to seize lawfully cast ballots and to fight for the First Amendment right of eligible voters to have their voices heard.

Following the seizure of [archived ballots](https://us.list-manage.com/BPRsP739Llz?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e) from Fulton County, Georgia, the DNC sent requests for records to the Federal Bureau of Investigation and the Criminal Division of the Department of Justice regarding seizure of ballots, voting machines, and other voting system components. Nearly five months later, the DNC has not received a single responsive document, in clear violation of FOIA. This lawsuit comes as Trump is [publicly musing](https://us.list-manage.com/8YIgVOKFl8K?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e) about declaring an emergency to attempt to take over the midterm elections.

The DNC previously [sued](https://us.list-manage.com/WsyX3OWFR4R?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e) the Trump administration for refusing to provide records regarding any plans to deploy federal agents or troops to polling places, drop boxes, and election offices in upcoming elections and won a court order forcing the administration to produce thousands of pages.

The DNC filed the FOIA requests to inform the public and prepare for any legal actions needed to protect Americans’ right to vote and to protect the security, transparency, and integrity of elections across the country. The DNC will continue holding the administration accountable and demanding they not subvert or undermine the will of the voters.

_**DNC Chair Ken Martin released the following statement:**_
“Donald Trump is historically unpopular and doing everything he can to subvert our elections this November — which is why we’re suing his administration once again. In our ongoing fight to protect free and fair elections, the DNC is holding Trump and his cronies accountable for their continued threats to our democracy. Whether in court or at the ballot box, we will stand with voters and defend them from Trump’s attempts to suppress their voices.”

| | | For the first time in nearly a decade, I won't be on the ballot this November.
I'll be honest — that's a strange thing to sit with. For years, asking for your vote has been how I showed up in this fight. This year, that's not an option for me.
But here's what hasn't changed: I am not going anywhere.
**I started Equal Opportunity Now because I refuse to sit on the sidelines while Donald Trump and his MAGA allies try to dismantle everything that made my family's story possible.** Not being on the ballot doesn't change that belief. If anything, it's freed me up to do something I care about just as much: help elect the next generation of Democrats who will fight for working families and take back power from MAGA extremists.
That's not just a talking point. **This month alone, Equal Opportunity Now is putting $100,000 directly into the hands of Democratic candidates and causes** — in Illinois and around the country. We're doing it because I know firsthand what it takes to run a campaign, and I know how much difference an early, real investment can make for a candidate who's ready to fight but needs the resources to do it.
I've spent my career fighting for fair wages, for a democracy that works for everyone, for an economy where hard work still leads somewhere. I'm not done fighting for any of that just because my name isn't on a ballot this year. If anything, I'm just getting started in a new way — finding the leaders who will carry this fight forward, and making sure they have what they need to win.

Peter, My name is Mary Peltola, and after winning yesterday's primary, I am officially running in the general election for United States Senate in Alaska.
I want to share with you why I made the decision to run - and to ask for your support as we begin the general election together.
But if you already understand how important this race and your support are, and you're ready to join our fight for fish, family, and freedom, please use this button to split a contribution between my campaign for U.S. Senate and the Nebraska Democrats:

---
| [CONTRIBUTE](https://eeuwd7hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001RUAdrFqzh7iK1oGi_D2ztXDEzIp5LSLplnFiyQRyWDVeOIsy69dZ6CTiw8cW3PBBStimiAzPZ8gAcNANd9-5-tRT_ke5yqZIz4bEt_KLTMKpiGKKESEiXfx1KG7gEq0De6qY7U6GDlPRCTjNenTivCSIEkpLu4oGT8D58mq2e1YbGqNtETZDDCgFQeuklKuEq2ZOL-WUNuRJcyYKlBz0_-cpyqfqoQS_Vn8H4MFMzio=&c=qwI0VY2Nl1L0aKC-Cx_ZCBvRZs2Mo_irSvKgRC_VPk_EciQVPuU-YA==&ch=Zs11RHYbV99MbF5W5VWb5iOYkiZy_SH9wsQlmdOw6ZZokdjrOGdW5w==)
---
Now here's a bit more on how I came to this decision.
When I was growing up in Bethel, salmon fishing with my father in the summers and dog mushing in the winters, Alaska was a place of abundance.
Now, all across Alaska, we have scarcity.
Multi-national companies are trawling our waters and decimating our fish stocks. The moose, caribou, and migratory birds that used to fill our freezers are harder to find.
So we buy more groceries, where the prices are just crushing Alaska families.
And I've got to tell you, DC people do not care that we are paying nearly 20 bucks for a gallon of fuel. They don't even believe us.
They're focused on their own wallets - not ours.
And when they actually work together on something, it's usually to help themselves. The rigged system in DC is shutting down Alaska and hurting all of us while politicians and their millionaire and billionaire donors feather their own nest.
It's why our prices keep rising, all while the healthcare and services Alaskans rely on get gutted.
I'm done with politicians getting richer while things get tougher here at home.
My agenda for Alaska will always be: fish, family, freedom. These values have been the core values of my campaigns since the very beginning.
But if we're going to secure Alaska's future, we need another priority: fighting corruption.
I'm running for Alaska's Senate seat because it is the fight for our future.
This is going to be the closest and most consequential Senate race this year, and I cannot do this alone. There is only one way we'll be able to flip this seat... and that is together.
So I am asking: [Please split a contribution between the Nebraska Democratic Party and my campaign for the U.S. Senate today as we begin the general election. We are looking for a huge number of day one donors to get our general election campaign off to a strong start and put us in a position to win. No donation is too small. clean_body: Let the general election begin! | | | | | == Peter, My name is Mary Peltola, and after winning yesterday's primary, I am officially running in the general election for United States Senate in Alaska. I want to share with you why I made the decision to run - and to ask for your support as we begin the general election together. But if you already understand how important this race and your support are, and you're ready to join our fight for fish, family, and freedom, please use this button to split a contribution between my campaign for U.S. Senate and the Nebraska Democrats: | == Now here's a bit more on how I came to this decision. When I was growing up in Bethel, salmon fishing with my father in the summers and dog mushing in the winters, Alaska was a place of abundance. Now, all across Alaska, we have scarcity. Multi-national companies are trawling our waters and decimating our fish stocks. The moose, caribou, and migratory birds that used to fill our freezers are harder to find. So we buy more groceries, where the prices are just crushing Alaska families. And I've got to tell you, DC people do not care that we are paying nearly 20 bucks for a gallon of fuel. They don't even believe us. They're focused on their own wallets - not ours. And when they actually work together on something, it's usually to help themselves. The rigged system in DC is shutting down Alaska and hurting all of us while politicians and their millionaire and billionaire donors feather their own nest. It's why our prices keep rising, all while the healthcare and services Alaskans rely on get gutted. I'm done with politicians getting richer while things get tougher here at home. My agenda for Alaska will always be: fish, family, freedom. These values have been the core values of my campaigns since the very beginning. But if we're going to secure Alaska's future, we need another priority: fighting corruption. I'm running for Alaska's Senate seat because it is the fight for our future. This is going to be the closest and most consequential Senate race this year, and I cannot do this alone. There is only one way we'll be able to flip this seat... and that is together. Peter,
**I will officially face off against MAGA extremist Andy Biggs in the general election this November.**
**[Rush a split donation of $5 between me and Small Town PAC to fuel our re-election campaign as we enter the final chapter of this toss-up race.](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20260821-partner-kh.7-0ixk&amount=5&refcode=em20260821-991&t=3&akid=991%2E34582%2E3aJHlI)**
If you don’t know who Biggs is, he is nearly identical to my 2022 opponent, Kari Lake, who we narrowly defeated by less than 1 percent of the vote.
He’s denied the 2020 election results and pushed bogus conspiracy theories, he’s attacked our reproductive rights, and he’s loyally supported every part of the MAGA agenda that’s actively hurting Arizona’s working families.
We’re not surprised Biggs won this primary — **he was hand-picked by Donald Trump and backed by far-right groups like Turning Point USA** long before he became the official Republican nominee for governor.
Now, _the full force of the Republican machine_ will rapidly pour their resources from millionaires, billionaires, and super PACs into this race in an attempt to defeat me and flip Arizona ahead of the 2028 presidential election.
My mission while running for re-election is two-fold: to prevent a far-right election denier and Trump loyalist from taking power and wreaking havoc in Arizona, and to keep delivering lower costs and better outcomes for ALL Arizonans.
But if 2022 taught me anything, it’s that I need people like you in my corner if I’m going to win and defend Arizona from Biggs, Trump, and MAGA. **We won by 17,117 votes last time around, and we can expect this November’s election to be just as close.**
**[That’s why I’m urgently asking: will you pitch in ANY amount to me and Small Town PAC to power our campaign to victory between now and November 3rd?](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20260821-partner-kh.7-0ixk&amount=5&refcode=em20260821-991&t=4&akid=991%2E34582%2E3aJHlI)**

I can’t thank you enough. Let’s go WIN!
— Katie Hobbs

Then they tell us that standing for our values is "too risky" with the election so close, and surrendering ground to Republicans is somehow the safer choice.
They call it strategy, but we can see the fear behind it.
People are tired of watching Democrats run from their own beliefs and of leaders who find their courage during a competitive primary, but then lose it when it matters most.
I'm going to Congress because I will not lose mine.
I'm fighting to abolish ICE and elect more progressive leaders who will hold the line even when Washington tells them to back down.
