| | | **[National Park Week](https://click.everyaction.com/k/137671630/641551749/797798769?utm_campaign=event&utm_medium=email&utm_source=ea-news-all&sourceid=1170896&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9TVFJXTC9TVFJXTC8xLzg5NTc0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjI1MTNmZjQ4LTg0OWQtZjExMS05YjMzLTAwMGQzYTExZmEzMCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=Pb9C7lWB0U0-ZjB_2vW4lknl_kxjMkXaLKr5JPcRQp0=&emci=cbc30fd8-fb9b-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=2513ff48-849d-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=1504551) **kicks off August 22 and this celebration has us reflecting on one of our country’s best ideas: protecting extraordinary places and opening them up to everyone. It’s easy to take national parks for granted, but there’s nothing inevitable about them. We can camp beneath ancient trees in Redwood National and State Parks, climb Yosemite’s granite cathedrals, or wander gobsmacked through the old-growth groves of Sequoia National Park because generations of people decided these places were worth protecting and sharing. We’re grateful they did.
---
---
That sense of gratitude came through in a recent note from one of our readers, who visited national parks as a young adult and is now bringing their children to see these irreplaceable spots: _“National parks mean everything to me. They're places of beauty, inspiration, and where we learn about our natural and cultural history. I’ll never forget the parks I’ve visited, and there are still more I hope to see. Park rangers are my heroes, stewarding these precious places while learning from the original Indigenous stewards of these lands.”_ We couldn’t agree more. National parks give us access to some of the most remarkable places on Earth, and remind us that safeguarding irreplaceable landscapes is both a legacy and a responsibility. This August 25, entrance fees are waived for the National Park Service’s 110th birthday—a perfect nudge to experience these protected places for yourself.

Tano Tijerina (TX-28): A born and raised South Texan, Tano learned the importance of faith, family, and hard work. As a county judge, Tano locked away hardened criminals and will continue to fight to support law enforcement and the American Dream. Eric Flores (TX-34): A US Army Veteran, Eric will be a champion for our veterans, fight to keep the border secure, and put a stop to migrant crime in our communities. Jim Desmond (CA-48): A Navy Veteran and commercial pilot, Jim will fight to lower costs and deliver safer communities. Brinker Harding (NE-02): An Omaha business leader, Brinker will rein in wasteful spending in Washington and work to reduce the National debt. Marty O'Donnell (NV-03): An award-winning composer for television shows, movies, and video games, Marty will fight to keep our border secure and invest in American technology. name: VoteVets
subject: Doris Miller
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY VOTEVETS, VOTEVETS
body:
Doris Miller is a hero to all Americans... but not to Pete Hegseth and Donald Trump.
#
Peter:
On December 7th, 1941, a mess attendant named Doris Miller was serving aboard the battleship West Virginia in Pearl Harbor. His job was one of just a few available to Black sailors in the segregated military. He served breakfast to the other sailors that morning, when around 0800 the West Virginia was struck by the first of seven torpedoes.
Miller reported to battlestations. The ship’s Captain, Mervyn Bennion, was wounded in the first attack, and Miller helped carry him to shelter. Because of the color of his skin, Miller was never given a chance to train on any of the ship’s weapons. Two of his shipmates trained him to operate anti-aircraft weapons on the fly, and he started firing. He fired until he ran out of ammunition, and was credited with shooting down two enemy aircraft.
The ship, struck repeatedly by armor piercing bombs and torpedoes, was leaking oil. Fire spread, smoke engulfing the conning tower. Miller then helped carry Captain Bennion out of the smoke, up to the navigation bridge. He went on to move more injured sailors out of the oil and water to the deck.
In 1942, bills were introduced in the House and Senate to award Miller the Medal of Honor, but the Secretary of the Navy recommended against it. Miller ultimately received the Navy Cross, and went back into active service in the Pacific. In 1943 he was aboard the carrier Liscome Bay when it was struck by a torpedo. The ship went down in less than a half hour, and Miller’s body was never found.
Doris Miller is a hero to all Americans... but not to Pete Hegseth and Donald Trump.
[](https://act.votevets.org/signup/Aug_VV_doris_miller_em/?source=em260821-1-360&refcode2=35491.3013755.ykzQeF&akid=35491%2E3013755%2EykzQeF)
Yeah, that’s complete bullshit. We’re not going to let it happen.
[**Peter, add your name _immediately_ and demand that the carrier CVN-81, the USS Doris Miller, NEVER be named after a draft-dodger who insults Veterans, the fallen, and their families. A disgrace who directed an attack on the US Capitol, started an illegal war, and got Americans killed. A coward who has trampled the graves of the fallen at Arlington, and wants to put them in his shadow by building a 250 foot tall arch, dedicated entirely to himself.**](https://act.votevets.org/signup/Aug_VV_doris_miller_em/?source=em260821-1-360&refcode2=35491.3013755.ykzQeF&akid=35491%2E3013755%2EykzQeF)

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39557?t=1011&refcode=email-20260821_v&akid=11220%2E5885482%2EZU0leQ ]Our Revolution logo

Peter Willis,

Big Tech billionaires are pushing their way into our neighborhoods —
erecting massive AI data centers that suck up our water, jack up our
energy bills, and bulldoze our communities for profit.

The threat is coming for ALL our communities — and people from all walks
of life are united in outrage. New headlines show the GOP could literally
lose places like Florida and Georgia over this!

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39558?source=email-20260821&t=1061&akid=11220%2E5885482%2EZU0leQ ]Headline: Could the GOP Lose Florida Over Data Centers?

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39558?source=email-20260821&t=1062&akid=11220%2E5885482%2EZU0leQ ]Headline: Georgia voters find solidarity in their opposition to data
centers

That’s where we see an opportunity — and Our Revolution is not standing
by. We’re making noise. We’re winning local bans. But Big Tech has
millions to spend and they’re not used to losing. To stop them, we need to
elect more leaders willing to fight back.

We are the only grassroots group with boots on the ground in down-ballot
races — the ones the tech giants hope you’ll ignore. These state and local
seats are the frontlines of the fight against data centers, but House and
Senate races matter too — and so our organizing team is racing to mobilize
the grassroots to elect leaders up and down the ballot who will stand up
and fight.

help us elect champions who’ll take on the data center invasion?

donation to Our Revolution will process immediately.

Across the country, communities are rising up. 71% of Americans now oppose
data centers near their homes, a seismic shift from just nine months ago.
Families from California to Ohio are waking up — organizing city by city
to stand up to corporate power and protect what’s ours.

The pressure is starting to work, with cities, towns, and states across
the country passing moratoriums to stop construction. But at the same
time, hundreds of new centers are popping up, destroying communities to
help Big Tech profit.

That’s why it’s so important that we elect a slate of leaders THIS YEAR
who have pledged to take on Big Tech and stop this takeover.

Take Patrick Nelson, running for New York State Senate, fighting for a
three-year statewide moratorium on new data centers. Or Ohio state Rep.
Tristan Rader, who worked with Our Revolution to expose how $1 BILLION of
taxpayer money was funneled to Big Tech and to demand hearings. Or Will
Lawrence, who is running for Congress in Michigan with a focus on stopping
data center expansion — and reshaping local politics while he does it.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39558?source=email-20260821&t=1060&akid=11220%2E5885482%2EZU0leQ ]Headline: The Anti-Data-Center Movement Is Reshaping Michigan Politics

We need these leaders — and dozens more — to fight for our communities.
When you chip in, you’re powering field organizers, voter outreach, and
the grassroots campaigns calling for bans and moratoriums, then turning
people out to vote.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39557?t=1054&amount=22&refcode=email-20260821nd&amounts=9%2C22%2C27%2C46%2C66&firstname=Peter%20Willis&lastname=&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&akid=11220%2E5885482%2EZU0leQ ]We can’t win this fight alone. Help us elect leaders who will stand up to
Big Tech and fight for US. Will you donate today to our Data Center
Candidate Fund and help us elect leaders fighting for people, not profits?

When we organize, we win.

Peter,
I will work with anybody. **_But I will bow to nobody._**
I didn’t come from money or prestige. As the son of an immigrant single mother, I came from hard work, community, and an unshakeable belief that _we could do better._
**[If you share that belief, would you chip in $5 to our re-election campaign today?](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260821-1.7K9MqX&refcode=em-20260821-1&t=2&akid=1796%2E1086043%2E9tnz02)**
Peter, my grandfather was run out of his home by the Klan. **But he rebuilt anyway.**
That history and resilience is why I believe every family deserves a fair shot at work, wages, and wealth — not just survival.
That’s what we’re building together: Teacher vacancies cut in half. Violent crime at historic lows. The first statewide Service Year Option in the country for every high school graduate.
My MAGA Republican opponent would undo all of it. **And I will not bow to him, or anyone who wants to take Maryland backward.**

The next 74 days are going to determine whether this is the year we take Texas back. My race against Greg Abbott has been in the single digits for months -- but now **poll after poll has this race statistically tied while major political outlets like Fox News and Cook Political Report have shifted this race in our favor.**
We have to do everything we can to build on this momentum. This is our opportunity to take back Texas from corporate billionaires hell bent on putting Texans last.
**I launched my race to be the next Governor of Texas with one goal in mind: securing the American Dream. For me that has always meant a quality education for our kids, an opportunity to make a living and afford your own home, and having access to basic necessities like affordable healthcare.**
In Abbott's Texas, millions of children go without healthcare. Teachers are pushed out of the classroom by out of touch standardized testing requirements and loss of funding. Hardworking families in rural Texas are forced to compete with data center giants for land and drinking water. And we sacrifice a huge national park like Big Bend all to score political brownie points with Washington.
Not in my Texas.
**As governor, I will fight for all Texans to have a seat at the table.** I will fight to lower costs, expand access to health care, restore funding to our neighborhood schools, and immediately place a moratorium on the construction of new data centers until the legislature puts real protections in place for Texans. No more paying the _Greg Abbott Corruption Tax_ where billionaires can skip the line and make money while we foot the bill.
I've driven to Brownsville, to Amarillo, to Galveston, and more, and every time I've heard the same thing: Texas families want a leader they can trust to fight for their best interests and not be beholden to the massive donor class that puts everyday Texans last. I am that leader.
**The one thing I really need all of us to take away is this: we can win.** Republicans have lost special elections left and right this year in historically deep red areas of Texas. For the first time in years, Texas Democrats have multiple candidates at the top of the ticket with real momentum. Abbott is out of step with his base. His approval is at an all time low and he is scared -- which he should be.
**[Texans are ready for real change. And I am ready to deliver. Will you help by chipping in $5 or whatever makes sense for you today, so that I can keep getting my message out to voters ahead of Election Day?](https://substack.com/redirect/ee2266e9-9450-43b2-9849-d6ac62c6e30f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ DONATE ->](https://substack.com/redirect/ee2266e9-9450-43b2-9849-d6ac62c6e30f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Thank you for being on my team,
Gina

subject: Communities are stopping data centers. Trump wants to get around us
body:
Communities are winning the fight for a say over data centers. Trump wants to cut us out. | |
---
Peter, Across the country, communities are standing up to Big Tech’s massive data center buildout, and we are winning.**** **In fact, just 2 days after Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro received 427 direct messages from our campaign, he publicly signed an executive order announcing significant restrictions on data center projects in what NBC News called a “notable shift” after previously encouraging the industry to build in the state.** **[](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm39NCDA5ge37cYZaUOgyTvISmSRetF2yjcfvCBKRCLHMCmNGzMHIGjG8WteKUvt-r76ASGGl5Q8jEI-mOfkOQa0yNc5FQwT-U2vxV18AXvxaTK-s1xEXoRrsY07tTYEk03VtChWU4-1vU6vs678Pf-xpmWGCbJYPjO35IVWMUPgMUHs6phNw1Q1oAleyPydEkUmc9rZ-5l8I6pkwi_XYlLc4V3ZQ1ESYReKU2Ydq7uexXrJxno3zw0kuhDauRLt4tQYQ_MmsIWeVsmTIXqQA4bIFRc-II6hmUcVYfPQZIYq5qacKIBhexUcimCJRAA7xd_IZTbcg_VweobJ03rF5JTbBFa0D9t2GzM_qhTu78USECxhgTKEhWPbc4_Ct1hMp13ks7fbQMWe0CNlrNp5DxKRPXHYlbnL6qjKDlMyhknyTY9h3ebipBw8l5X2SdNBQVxR3AcHfJbFouAKpOLBuA6qq/4td/c_Au3RBKTZO3RFPq00GAoA/h0/h001.8m4HvXq2vMsZEFBmWJzz3Lq6KcRu8h5r4GSXID70WcA)** ******OnePA members here in Pennsylvania are still organizing for the Governor to go a step further and support a statewide moratorium on hyperscale data centers, but this is a big first step.** In red states and blue states, people are demanding a say before corporations consume enormous amounts of electricity and water, raise costs, and reshape our communities for their own profit. We are building the power to make sure working families, Black communities, and the people who actually live with the consequences have a voice before corporations rush these projects through. Big Tech sees what is happening. So does the Trump administration. Local opposition is growing, projects are being challenged, and communities are proving that corporate money does not have to get the final word. **Now they want a way around us.** Trump is pushing data center development on federal lands and military bases, where Big Tech could sidestep local review, public hearings, and the community pressure that is already stopping projects across the country. [**We organized for a seat at the table. We are not going to let Trump and Big Tech find a way to shut us out. # [FTC urged to stop AI giants from shredding books for data](https://substack.com/redirect/e92edd70-1dd1-478e-b117-5c8892be0ee7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
More than a dozen civil society groups are urging the Federal Trade Commission to **[investigate dominant AI companies for buying, scanning and physically destroying books](https://substack.com/redirect/66166af0-d41c-48b0-8d50-02aacb145c16?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** as a data acquisition practice that may harm competition.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e92edd70-1dd1-478e-b117-5c8892be0ee7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Groups demand FTC probe:** Demand Progress Education Fund, Consumer Federation of America and Institute for Local Self-Reliance lead more than a dozen groups asking the FTC to examine the practice as an unfair method of competition.
* **Anthropic book destruction cited:** A January Washington Post report based on court filings said Anthropic spent millions acquiring books and removing their spines to scan pages into its Claude model.
* **Starving market of materials:** The letter argues the hoard-and-destroy approach starves rivals of critical source materials, raises competitors' costs and could permanently eliminate rare books from the market.
* **Focus on competition not training:** The groups stress they do not seek restrictions on AI model training itself but want intervention against destroying existing works that could create an insurmountable moat for incumbents.

# [New York just dethroned San Francisco as top tech talent hub](https://substack.com/redirect/e92edd70-1dd1-478e-b117-5c8892be0ee7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
New York's office market now[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/2933fd7f-f011-4a6f-b8df-91c6844c2cff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[hosts more tech workers than the San Francisco Bay Area for the first time in 13 years](https://substack.com/redirect/2933fd7f-f011-4a6f-b8df-91c6844c2cff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** of CBRE analysis, driven largely by rapid growth in AI-related roles.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e92edd70-1dd1-478e-b117-5c8892be0ee7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **New York leads overall:** New York counts 394,300 tech talent jobs, edging out the San Francisco Bay Area's 375,730, according to CBRE's report covering 75 metropolitan markets in the U.S. and Canada.
* **AI roles expand rapidly:** AI tech roles grew 45% in the past year across the U.S. and Canada, with New York and San Francisco each adding more than 20,000 AI-specific jobs since mid-2025.
* **AI drives leasing surge:** In San Francisco, AI companies made up 58% of all leasing in the first half of this year and 30% of activity totaling about 10 million square feet since 2023.
* **Office culture remains key:** AI has a more office-centric culture with workers in offices four to six days a week, fueling recovery as the sector creates more jobs than it eliminates.

# [Nvidia courts Korean AI chip startup Rebellions](https://substack.com/redirect/e92edd70-1dd1-478e-b117-5c8892be0ee7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Nvidia[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/5718f28c-7869-48d4-ba72-c18cb7a1b44c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[is in early discussions with South Korean AI chip designer Rebellions about a possible technical partnership,](https://substack.com/redirect/5718f28c-7869-48d4-ba72-c18cb7a1b44c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/5718f28c-7869-48d4-ba72-c18cb7a1b44c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)investment or acquisition after CEO Jensen Huang met the startup's co-founder this week in Santa Clara.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e92edd70-1dd1-478e-b117-5c8892be0ee7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Early discussions now underway:** Nvidia is holding preliminary talks with Rebellions that could include a technical partnership, an investment or even an acquisition, according to people familiar with the matter.
* **Huang meets Rebellions CEO:** Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang met Rebellions co-founder and CEO Sunghyun Park at the company's Santa Clara headquarters this week to discuss a potential tie-up.
* **Startup raises $850 million:** Bundang-based Rebellions has raised roughly $850 million from investors including SK Hynix, Samsung Ventures and Arm and was most recently valued at around $2.3 billion.
* **Focuses on inference chips:** The company founded in 2020 specializes in neural processing units for data centers optimized for AI inference, the higher-volume workload required to operate AI services at scale.

# [Nvidia's valuation now hinges on one open-source AI shift](https://substack.com/redirect/e92edd70-1dd1-478e-b117-5c8892be0ee7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
HSBC analyst Frank Lee says **[Nvidia's next major stock re-rating will come from positioning](https://substack.com/redirect/52360d23-b860-4634-9f7f-4a7f8309d8d9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** as the world's largest contributor to open-source AI rather than from earnings or product roadmap alone.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e92edd70-1dd1-478e-b117-5c8892be0ee7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Expectations run hot into earnings:** Nvidia reports results August 26 with the market positioned for strong numbers after the stock outperformed the S&P 500 by five percentage points over the past month.
* **Open-source models gain traction:** Aggregate open-source models now represent the second most popular category by token generation and small language models are preferred for agentic AI and on-device applications.
* **TAM expansion potential:** Boosting small language models lowers barriers for enterprise inference and expands Nvidia's addressable market beyond frontier labs to millions of developers and sovereign nations.
* **Recent capital partnerships:** Nvidia partnered with Apollo, BlackRock and others to deploy $500 billion in private capital for AI data centers and offered up to $105 billion credit support for an 8-gigawatt Ohio campus.

# [Bitcoin rockets 23% in one week as optimism floods back](https://substack.com/redirect/e92edd70-1dd1-478e-b117-5c8892be0ee7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Bitcoin was on track for a **[weekly gain of around 23% Friday after rising above $77,000,](https://substack.com/redirect/8ef4c11d-02be-4a10-8e5c-525ccbff1ce2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/8ef4c11d-02be-4a10-8e5c-525ccbff1ce2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)driven by falling Treasury yields, a short squeeze and renewed hopes for the Clarity Act.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e92edd70-1dd1-478e-b117-5c8892be0ee7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Price and weekly performance:** Bitcoin last traded near $77,000, up from about $62,800 at the week's start, putting it on pace for roughly a 23% weekly advance amid broader crypto gains.
* **Yields and short squeeze:** The rally started Wednesday as Treasury yields fell sharply after intervention, then amplified by a massive short squeeze that liquidated roughly $2.7 billion in crypto short positions.
* **Clarity Act catalyst hopes:** Investor sentiment improved Thursday on a last-ditch White House and industry push to pass the Clarity Act, viewed as key to ending the crypto winter that began last fall.
* **Still below prior highs:** Despite the rebound bitcoin remains well below its 2026 high of $94,820 from mid-January and the all-time high of $126,198 hit on October 6 last year.

# [660 million barrels secured: U.S. forces move on the Strait of Hormuz](https://substack.com/redirect/e92edd70-1dd1-478e-b117-5c8892be0ee7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
U.S. Central Command has aided passage of **[more than 660 million barrels of crude oil through the Strait of Hormuz](https://substack.com/redirect/deea277c-e4fa-4e39-bc29-a5e629796911?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** since early May, assisting about 1,300 commercial vessels amid Iranian threats and contested control.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e92edd70-1dd1-478e-b117-5c8892be0ee7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Assistance volume since May:** Central Command helped more than 660 million barrels of crude oil and about 1,300 commercial vessels sail through the Strait of Hormuz since early May this year.
* **Recent three-week flow:** Military statements indicate at least 160 million barrels or more than 7 million barrels per day transited the strait over the past three weeks alone.
* **Far below pre-war levels:** Shipments remain well under the roughly 20 million barrels per day of crude oil and products that passed through Hormuz before the conflict began.
* **Contested lanes and claims:** Iran says the strait is closed until U.S. obligations under the June 17 interim peace deal are met while President Trump insists it stays open under American control.

# [Apollo confirms major data breach as financial hacking wave explodes](https://substack.com/redirect/e92edd70-1dd1-478e-b117-5c8892be0ee7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Apollo Global Management[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/da7369d0-66ba-487d-b102-b85fd6c32932?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[confirmed hackers stole names, birth dates, addresses and Social Security numbers](https://substack.com/redirect/da7369d0-66ba-487d-b102-b85fd6c32932?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** from its cloud systems via social engineering between July 6 and July 10 amid a broader campaign targeting private equity firms.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e92edd70-1dd1-478e-b117-5c8892be0ee7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Hackers gained cloud access:** Between July 6 and July 10, attackers used social engineering to breach Apollo Global Management's cloud environment and steal sensitive personal information, according to a California attorney general filing.
* **Stolen data includes identifiers:** The breach compromised names, birth dates, contact details such as home addresses, and Social Security numbers from the private equity firm managing $938 billion in assets.
* **Part of extortion campaign:** Security researchers at Google previously warned of hackers known as Falcon, Helix, Pink and Redact targeting financial giants with fake IT support calls to obtain passwords and codes.
* **Ransoms and employee scale:** Similar attacks have yielded ransoms as high as $750,000 while Apollo employs around 5,000 people; the firm has not confirmed if a ransom was paid in this case.

# [American brands are getting crushed by Chinese rivals at home](https://substack.com/redirect/e92edd70-1dd1-478e-b117-5c8892be0ee7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
American consumer brands including Nike and Starbucks are losing influence in China as geopolitical tensions, domestic competition and cultural disconnects **[reshape a once lucrative market for U.S. companies.](https://substack.com/redirect/6fe3dc47-a02d-4d47-8280-42382b509d4f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e92edd70-1dd1-478e-b117-5c8892be0ee7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Nike China sales plunge:** Nike has seen its China business shrink 30% since 2021, with annual revenue hitting its lowest level in eight years as shoppers turn to domestic brands.
* **Starbucks faces fierce rivals:** Starbucks confronts intense competition from Luckin Coffee, which operates more than three times the number of stores in China and sells drinks at steep discounts.
* **Some brands still thrive:** Lululemon expects about 20% China growth this year while Ralph Lauren posted 40% growth in its most recent quarter by staying locally relevant.
* **Gap exits local control:** Gap sold its China business to Baozun for $40 million after struggling to connect with consumers, and the buyer has since refined strategy successfully.

# [Trump admin taps Matt Zames for Social Security advisory role](https://substack.com/redirect/e92edd70-1dd1-478e-b117-5c8892be0ee7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Former JPMorgan Chase executive Matt Zames **[is joining the Trump administration](https://substack.com/redirect/0f6b850a-fb9a-4746-94d0-27fc23c8cab7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in an unpaid advisory role at the Social Security Administration to help modernize the agency, starting Monday at Baltimore headquarters.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e92edd70-1dd1-478e-b117-5c8892be0ee7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Unpaid role begins Monday:** Zames starts an unpaid advisory position Monday at Social Security Administration headquarters in Baltimore where an office placard bearing his name has already been installed.
* **Helping former colleague:** He will assist former JPMorgan colleague Frank Bisignano, who became Social Security Commissioner last year, on modernization of the agency's decades-old technology systems.
* **Career background details:** Zames rose at JPMorgan after the London Whale cleanup, served as chief operating officer for about five years, then led at Cerberus before starting his own firm.
* **Special employee limits:** As a special government employee Zames can hold the position for 130 days though that period may stretch because he will not work full-time.

AI roles expand rapidly: AI tech roles grew 45% in the past year across the U.S. and Canada, with New York and San Francisco each adding more than 20,000 AI-specific jobs since mid-2025. AI drives leasing surge: In San Francisco, AI companies made up 58% of all leasing in the first half of this year and 30% of activity totaling about 10 million square feet since 2023. Startup raises $850 million: Bundang-based Rebellions has raised roughly $850 million from investors including SK Hynix, Samsung Ventures and Arm and was most recently valued at around $2.3 billion. Yields and short squeeze: The rally started Wednesday as Treasury yields fell sharply after intervention, then amplified by a massive short squeeze that liquidated roughly $2.7 billion in crypto short positions. Clarity Act catalyst hopes: Investor sentiment improved Thursday on a last-ditch White House and industry push to pass the Clarity Act, viewed as key to ending the crypto winter that began last fall. Peter, **[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137675115/641561283/169718829?contactdata=IJN/r3cTbEIgOyYXr0WFjhNUP++CA+NkzPSokURp+smnfDSch1yXT+t0i80I20/k+q1mWTDJ2WhLK1mQjioqFWHTqj+2D4vMdYztWdQQtT0kpaYxKD9u/6EpiQ1AqsO5HbbJ0pGVaXLtUnl44x3/djeyw1kneN8YK+/I++tOAAhMEFVD/5IOQYtBggHnLi5c&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDMyMDUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNDczYTBlMzQtOGI5ZC1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAwZDNhMTFmYTMwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=3Zum-gidc7E1Crrdq4PgXsASkZP7otfhuUP2yGzkJ2M=&emci=3f19da65-829d-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=473a0e34-8b9d-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=9848080)** Nolan Wells would be 19 this week. He should be celebrating with his family and looking forward to his future. Instead, his family is still fighting for answers about how their 18-year-old son and brother disappeared on July 4 and was found dead two days later. And Nolan’s family is not alone. Across America, Black families and other families of color have been left with unanswered questions after loved ones who have died under suspicious or unexplained circumstances. Each case has its own facts. But the pattern of families being forced to beg for urgency, transparency, and accountability cannot be ignored. Authorities owe these families more than quick conclusions and closed doors. They owe them the truth.

clean_body: Unexplained deaths demand federal scrutiny and accountability.| | | | Peter, Nolan Wells would be 19 this week. He should be celebrating with his family and looking forward to his future. Instead, his family is still fighting for answers about how their 18-year-old son and brother disappeared on July 4 and was found dead two days later. And Nolan’s family is not alone. Across America, Black families and other families of color have been left with unanswered questions after loved ones who have died under suspicious or unexplained circumstances. Each case has its own facts. But the pattern of families being forced to beg for urgency, transparency, and accountability cannot be ignored. Authorities owe these families more than quick conclusions and closed doors. They owe them the truth. As I told Don Lemon, the Department of Justice must investigate Nolan Wells’s death and the broader pattern of recent unexplained deaths of people of color—and hold state and local authorities accountable wherever the evidence reveals failures, misconduct, or civil rights violations. And when we take back the House, Congress must investigate these cases and make this a national issue. No family should have to become its own investigator. No family should have to fight this hard for the truth. Thank you for your activism and all that you do. In solidarity, Ro | | | | | | | Wait! One more thing– Ro doesn't accept a cent from lobbyists or PACs, meaning our work is completely funded by grassroots supporters like you. By donating just $3 today, you’re helping us create a country that works for everyone, not just those at the top. That means a renewed investment in American manufacturing, Medicare for All, student debt relief, and a green future. If you want to support our people-powered campaign as we continue to fight for progress in Washington, please consider making a donation of $3 or more today. They’ll do whatever it takes to protect their bottom lines — and the politicians who keep putting corporate profits ahead of the people they’re supposed to serve. I say, enough is enough. The candidates we’re electing are offering something different. They look at communities where children are growing up with asthma because of the air they breathe. Families worried about what’s in their water. Neighbors facing rare cancers and toxic pollution while corporations rake in record profits. **And instead of accepting that as the way things have to be, they’re running to change it.** That’s why $22.09 matters so much to me. subject: New NC Polling Alert
body:
How quickly things can change
|
# [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1132&source=&t=1&akid=2928%2E124072%2EdIsx2X)
| | | |
---
Folks,

Just after I reached out _this morning_ to talk to you about not being able to trust the polling lead we’ve had in this race, we got word about a brand-new poll here in North Carolina, and it’s not looking good:
Following the millions of dollars the GOP has been pouring into attack ads against me, **a brand-new poll out today shows Michael Whatley and I are statistically tied.** If that’s all you need to hear today, please use this link to chip in and stop them from taking the lead: **[_https:/actblue.com/donate_](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1132&amount=5&t=8&akid=2928%2E124072%2EdIsx2X)**
North Carolina hasn’t sent a Democrat to the U.S. Senate since 2008 – and Republicans want it to stay that way. They know that if we fail to flip this seat, we’ll lose our chance at taking back the U.S. Senate majority.
This new poll only confirms what we’ve known all along: this is going to be an extremely close race. And I’m going to need all the help I can get.
I’ve been a top target for national Republicans all cycle. So far, GOP super PACs are pouring nearly $100 million into this race so far to try and defeat me.
I’ve spent much of my life fighting for North Carolinians, but alone I can’t out-organize all the GOP’s dark money. Unlike Whatley, who relies on special interests and dark money to win, our campaign depends on grassroots supporters like you.
**[_Will you chip in $5 to help me fight back and win?_](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1132&amount=5&t=9&akid=2928%2E124072%2EdIsx2X)**

body:
An issue a day

| |
---
| | _With just eighteen days until the primary, I am using each day to discuss an issue I have highlighted on the campaign trail. For Day 18, I am highlighting the need to pass Medicare for All so that good healthcare isn’t tied to your age, your job, or how much money you have._
* * *
Dear David, When I announced my support for Medicare for All, I wasn’t just following the crowd. **[In fact, I was the first candidate in this race to publicly support providing everyone health insurance through Medicare.](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/y4znCUkPHjvtajNWLSUzEg~~/AAUS1hA~/y5gfIkxrLlAlXE3_JHuBuapiA0GdEso4CJ6-U4varA2jrm7TPq4e97NxZKhICP9b6V9w20IXSy18P_46mYDqAGQLBDLKdrzbYtmYO_VWnwymqx5wNp00Mc9LyhrZEAoazindPOdlbB8YZMoyroUJ4vr3c0n1VmplCdFork4jPhLEm_s6qVL9KmFSzAwplnbp)** It wasn’t a hard decision for me at all. Medicare for All is a broadly popular policy proposal, and it’s also just the right thing to do. I’ve talked to too many people in this district who have had to choose between filling a prescription or buying groceries, who have put off going to the doctor because they were terrified of what the bill would look like, and too many who are one medical emergency away from financial ruin. **[Healthcare should be a right for _everyone_ , not a privilege reserved for people who can afford it. If you’re ready to join me and fight to make this a reality, please pitch in today.](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/0Vl1VnSIxySW6yZT4riDXQ~~/AAUS1hA~/ObMpxgXXpxtsNL5ozUA4Ls1gWiJZ-fnMhwPHVV1MSkLy-KUhdDKK2d2oxSEuUSCwDJtKfugZnNs2IdHXpq0kPTG-EMM1P0TPCTB4VIyyVJqNybBvIxvx_VqfG71X6NFeJdsiHvlhQzlkWrUPpQ8FrxAQJBH0QLhZMYCLmLnM8cBz0Ck1h4tWegdxwrwqP_T6Ouztk0kiufCnFgj7Q4tnTbus7HtuRvIM5FbkQPQtXchN0fNucqEBRQ_Mxcj_NJkYyu9VhQSVCrwAwzy_mM42jg~~)** | | [DONATE](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/0Vl1VnSIxySW6yZT4riDXQ~~/AAUS1hA~/ObMpxgXXpxtsNL5ozUA4Ls1gWiJZ-fnMhwPHVV1MSkLy-KUhdDKK2d2oxSEuUSCwDJtKfugZnNs2IdHXpq0kPTG-EMM1P0TPCTB4VIyyVJqNybBvIxvx_VqfG71X6NFeJdsiHvlhQzlkWrUPpQ8FrxAQJBH0QLhZMYCLmLnM8cBz0Ck1h4tWegdxwrwqP_T6Ouztk0kiufCnFgj7Q4tnTbus7HtuRvIM5FbkQPQtXchN0fNucqEBRQ_Mxcj_NJkYyu9VhQSVCrwAwzy_mM42jg~~)
---
In New Hampshire, we know all too well about rising property taxes. Residents are being crushed by them, and renters are also seeing this burden reflected in their rent, which is rising faster than their income can keep up with.
Not only does Medicare for All ensure that people have access to high-quality health insurance and make sure that people don’t have to pay extraordinarily high insurance premiums, **but it also would lower property taxes across our district.**
There are three costs driving increases in public school budgets (and as a result, your property taxes): special education, transportation, and **health insurance.**
Medicare for All would help lower your property taxes by reducing the gigantic health insurance premiums that school districts and municipalities pay to insurance companies to cover their municipal employees.
I have served on the budget committee, and I have pored over every line looking for ways to save property taxpayers a dime. **Taking health insurance premiums out of the budget would help us lower property taxes.**
**[People deserve a leader who’s honest about the scale of the problem and bold enough to back a solution that fixes it. I support Medicare for All, and I will do everything in my power to get it through Congress. If you’re with me, I’d be grateful for your support today:](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/0Vl1VnSIxySW6yZT4riDXQ~~/AAUS1hA~/ObMpxgXXpxtsNL5ozUA4Ls1gWiJZ-fnMhwPHVV1MSkLy-KUhdDKK2d2oxSEuUSCwDJtKfugZnNs2IdHXpq0kPTG-EMM1P0TPCTB4VIyyVJqNybBvIxvx_VqfG71X6NFeJdsiHvlhQzlkWrUPpQ8FrxAQJBH0QLhZMYCLmLnM8cBz0Ck1h4tWegdxwrwqP_T6Ouztk0kiufCnFgj7Q4tnTbus7HtuRvIM5FbkQPQtXchN0fNucqEBRQ_Mxcj_NJkYyu9VhQSVCrwAwzy_mM42jg~~)**

clean_body: An issue a day | | | | With just eighteen days until the primary, I am using each day to discuss an issue I have highlighted on the campaign trail. For Day 18, I am highlighting the need to pass Medicare for All so that good healthcare isn’t tied to your age, your job, or how much money you have. Dear David, When I announced my support for Medicare for All, I wasn’t just following the crowd. It wasn’t a hard decision for me at all. Medicare for All is a broadly popular policy proposal, and it’s also just the right thing to do. I’ve talked to too many people in this district who have had to choose between filling a prescription or buying groceries, who have put off going to the doctor because they were terrified of what the bill would look like, and too many who are one medical emergency away from financial ruin. ~~ | | ~~ In New Hampshire, we know all too well about rising property taxes. Residents are being crushed by them, and renters are also seeing this burden reflected in their rent, which is rising faster than their income can keep up with. Not only does Medicare for All ensure that people have access to high-quality health insurance and make sure that people don’t have to pay extraordinarily high insurance premiums, but it also would lower property taxes across our district. There are three costs driving increases in public school budgets (and as a result, your property taxes): special education, transportation, and health insurance. Medicare for All would help lower your property taxes by reducing the gigantic health insurance premiums that school districts and municipalities pay to insurance companies to cover their municipal employees. I have served on the budget committee, and I have pored over every line looking for ways to save property taxpayers a dime. * * *
Parents are living in fear of their kids having fewer rights than the last generation of special-needs kids. A frightening memo from the Justice Department recently argued that states do not have to provide in-home or community-based care to people with disabilities. **Without the mandate to integrate, kids with disabilities will not be educated like their peers with no disabilities.****** Bright young people who are blind will not be offered resources to study or opportunities that they should be entitled to. It is frankly cruel and reminiscent of a time when the deaf, mute, and blind were deemed _dumb_. **Without the federal government requiring that states help disabled children integrate into their schools, this has the momentum to force a generation of young people into darkness.****** We must fight for our young people and elect leaders who will write the laws that protect them. clean_body: | | | Schools may no longer be required to integrate special-needs kids. Parents are living in fear of their kids having fewer rights than the last generation of special-needs kids. A frightening memo from the Justice Department recently argued that states do not have to provide in-home or community-based care to people with disabilities. Without the mandate to integrate, kids with disabilities will not be educated like their peers with no disabilities.**** Bright young people who are blind will not be offered resources to study or opportunities that they should be entitled to. It is frankly cruel and reminiscent of a time when the deaf, mute, and blind were deemed dumb. Without the federal government requiring that states help disabled children integrate into their schools, this has the momentum to force a generation of young people into darkness.**** We must fight for our young people and elect leaders who will write the laws that protect them. The disabled community just doesn’t have major political power like the tobacco or gun lobby – YET. name: Angela Alsobrooks
subject: MAGA’s next target
body:
Our democracy shouldn't be decided by whichever party is willing to cheat hardest | | | I want to tell you what I learned chairing Maryland's redistricting commission — because it's the reason I'm asking for your help today. We held public meetings across this state. Hundreds of Marylanders testified. And underneath so many of the comments was the same conviction: **Our democracy should not be decided by whichever party is willing to cheat hardest.** But that's exactly the game Donald Trump is running. His party looked at their record — the costs, the corruption, the chaos — and concluded they can't win a fair fight at the ballot box. So they stopped fighting fair. Texas, Missouri, North Carolina, Florida: rigged maps, drawn mid-decade, designed to decide who controls Congress before voters get a say. And every rigged seat in a red state cancels out a vote cast right here in Maryland. **Question 3 is Maryland's answer.** This amendment aligns our redistricting rules with states across the country, giving Maryland voters the power to respond to MAGA's rigged maps with our own. It's on your ballot this November — and it's the last opportunity we have anywhere in America to fight back directly against MAGA map-rigging in 2026. **Which is why I'm asking you, right now, to[chip name: Deb Haaland
subject: I'm angry
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY DEB FOR NEW MEXICO**
body:
| | | [](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/134?t=1&akid=11914%2E400544%2E8uTN37)
---
Friend, like so many New Mexicans, I relied on Planned Parenthood, Medicaid, SNAP, and WIC to fill the gaps when I was raising my child as a single mother living paycheck to paycheck. I know how important it is to have access to reliable healthcare and healthy food you can put on the table, and how much these programs mean to a family when they need help to make ends meet.
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15433?refcode=jtk1249-fr-nd&t=2&akid=11914%2E400544%2E8uTN37)
**That’s why learning that my Republican opponent said he would put New Mexicans’ reproductive freedom at risk made me angry.** _My opponent even said he would work with extremist Texas Governor Greg Abbott to take away reproductive healthcare options from people who need them, putting lives at risk._
**This should concern every New Mexican who believes decisions about our bodies and our healthcare should be made by us, not politicians.[_And with so much at stake, I need your help: Will you chip in $5 or whatever you can before midnight to help me fight back?_](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15440?refcode=jtk1249-fr-nd&t=3&akid=11914%2E400544%2E8uTN37)**

---
After the Supreme Court overturned _Roe v. Wade_ , states like Texas passed extreme abortion bans that criminalized healthcare providers. _New Mexico chose a different path._

New Mexico became a place people can rely on for reproductive healthcare, and we protected the providers who deliver that care.

_But that progress is at risk._
My Republican opponent has made clear that he would welcome the same extremist agenda as Greg Abbott and Donald Trump. He would work to flip the New Mexico Legislature by electing anti-choice Republicans who could vote to roll back our reproductive freedoms.

**I won’t let that happen.**
As governor, I will fight to keep New Mexico a leader in reproductive healthcare. I will protect the providers who care for New Mexicans and people who come here seeking healthcare. And I will defend every New Mexican’s right to make their own decisions about their body, their family, and their future.
I’ve never been afraid of a tough fight. My family taught me to be fierce, and my career has given me the opportunity to put that lesson into practice, but I need your help: **[_Will you chip in $5 today to help us win this election and protect access to reproductive healthcare in New Mexico?_](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15440?refcode=jtk1249-fr-nd&t=8&akid=11914%2E400544%2E8uTN37)**

#

**The fight isn’t over.**
As you may have heard, we ended the campaign with a good amount of money in the bank. We saved the money because we were running this campaign to win in November – to flip this seat – and we knew that if we had spent it all in the primary our chances of doing that would be slim to none.
Obviously, that first part didn’t work out as we had hoped.

---
Friend, Growing up in a family with two parents who immigrated to the U.S., I learned Spanish and English roughly at the same time. My mom and dad both pushed me to learn and master English, but Spanish came more easily to me as a young kid. In elementary school, I struggled to learn because English just didn't stick. My mom, who was working as a night shift nurse, would come home, sleep for a bit while I was at school, and then wake up when I got back to **work with me for three to four hours every day for years** to make sure I learned to read, write, and speak English. My mom made all the difference in my life. Our community welcomed us. And kids like me got a chance to learn, grow, and pursue our dreams.
---
| [ ](https://clicksp.urrutia4nh.net/f/a/78uLH2NKcg4gVNeUY-4zAQ~~/AAPPABA~/59bAzZsrnRiHt_Qm1RRNvwZtJrLvT2bDtlKeAU9-Cv9pr1gvTcgTreMbUjJA_F-xbVSkTSrLc8bWiQvaLWJ2B8sXfUvFPTmQgG_OJkUMu_uEk3yF8b5psERDsPNOUYS5BmonMCmG8kL_aIlnK8h-8CRgu66bnCo2ekJtHebPcAs~)

clean_body: | | ~ | Friend, Growing up in a family with two parents who immigrated to the U.S., I learned Spanish and English roughly at the same time. My mom and dad both pushed me to learn and master English, but Spanish came more easily to me as a young kid. In elementary school, I struggled to learn because English just didn't stick. My mom, who was working as a night shift nurse, would come home, sleep for a bit while I was at school, and then wake up when I got back to work with me for three to four hours every day for years to make sure I learned to read, write, and speak English. My mom made all the difference in my life. Our community welcomed us. And kids like me got a chance to learn, grow, and pursue our dreams. | ~ We were able to make a home, to work hard, and to get a fair shake. But that is sadly no longer a reality for so many in our country, whether the kid of immigrants or a fifth-generation American. I think about my story, my parents' story, and the stories of so many of the people I meet every day on the campaign trail. The America I believe in is one that helps every kid get a fair shot. That 's why I'm in this fight. I'm a 1st generation American. I fought for human rights as a lawyer. I served my country as a captain in the National Guard. Now I'm running for Congress -- to take on a rigged system and build something better. name: Darline Graham
subject: President Trump knows what's at stake
body:
Tonight, I want to tell President Trump you're with us. |
---

Tonight I will join President Trump on stage - but before I do, I need to know if you're with me, Peter.

| Friday, August 21, 2026| GOP Map Survives Court Test
---|---
5-minute read · 4 stories
Lead Story · The 2026 MapMISSOURI JUDGE UPHOLDS GOP CONGRESSIONAL MAP, BLOCKS REFERENDUM BIDWhat's Happening
* Cole County Circuit Judge **Daniel Green** ruled that Missouri's constitutional referendum provisions do not apply to congressional redistricting enacted by the General Assembly.
* The decision keeps the state's new Republican-drawn U.S. House map in place for the November election.
* Green sided with Republican Secretary of State **Denny Hoskins** , who had rejected a veto-referendum petition as a violation of the Missouri Constitution.

The Situation
* The group People Not Politicians said it gathered **more than 300,000 signatures** to put the map before voters.
* Gov. Mike Kehoe signed the map last September after President Trump urged GOP-led states to redraw boundaries; it splits Kansas City among three districts and puts Democratic Rep. Emanuel Cleaver's seat in play.
* Plaintiff Richard von Glahn appealed Wednesday evening, and the case is widely expected to reach the Missouri Supreme Court — so this is not the final word.

The PerspectiveRead the ruling for what it actually says: the judge did not declare this map fair or wise, he decided who holds the pen. Missouri's constitution assigns congressional redistricting to the legislature, and a signature drive cannot rewrite that assignment after the fact. Conservatives who spent a decade arguing that elected legislatures — not commissions, courts, or petition campaigns — carry the redistricting power should be consistent enough to accept the same logic when Democrats win a map somewhere else. And with an appeal already filed, anyone treating November's lines as settled is getting ahead of the record.[Read the full story at Washington Examiner](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.SfPhhFqVdCCzAqIAosiI_F0KAElx4yVoiF03sTMUTyXVppiSKgyDOfmQE1iA2Q6feP26i8skzhG01HhpOZ0-7LGl1yILJyjmZhYSg4JlhnDqSoieh6tq0cf2dEw9-rFfQPaur5EVqs6vH99PeFLMKbdurloQfYjzCD8YFb12_F1nOQg5hNlMksIUwsLryO5Uq5VlcdZiSngfwFJbIZ6r0aMIu390GVZOjrXzArrjBt6DprziLpdJcQ-o9YvkBaz8uYzxAOKGj-JaIgUaJ6Ak5nzjPevsJW1h6ldL_qWrolf28Fw_IAoi4oVGDaYvrHU2AEIuWZnooub68sK214SYD7jZPAzQMUFcOmDUa-76Q0NB-XolcKvdOVz_y5ezSvZTpPkm-VgA12DDnX0zEoprww/4td/s02KSihTT4Wy4B9gmAfQJQ/h5/h001.5SDQFSbIHMnH1l6Qx0k9P2Iwb6BlhWrJwUmrm6DcNYo)

JusticeFBI SEIZES SWALWELL'S DEVICES AS MISCONDUCT INVESTIGATION ESCALATESWhat's Happening
* The FBI seized former Rep. Eric Swalwell's electronic devices at San Francisco International Airport on **Saturday night** , two sources familiar with the incident told Fox News Digital.
* His Washington, D.C., home was searched the following day, a source said.
* The seized devices included at least one cell phone. Swalwell was **not arrested or detained**.

The Situation
* The activity is tied to an investigation into sexual misconduct allegations that surfaced during Swalwell's California gubernatorial bid.
* He resigned his House seat in April, after the allegations were reported in detail.
* **No charges have been filed** , and an investigation is not a finding of guilt. Fox News Digital reported that it reached out to Swalwell's attorney; the report is developing.

The PerspectiveThe principle worth defending here is the boring one: the same rules for everybody. For years the complaint from the right was that the well-connected got the benefit of the doubt while ordinary people got the full weight of federal process. If a search warrant is the appropriate step in a case like this, it is appropriate regardless of the party letter after the subject's name. That principle has a second edge, and it applies today: a seized phone is evidence-gathering, not a verdict. The women who came forward deserve a real investigation. Swalwell deserves the presumption of innocence. Both of those can be true at once, and conservatives lose the argument the moment they abandon the second one for a political scalp.[Read the full story at Fox News](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.SfPhhFqVdCCzAqIAosiI_NRx3TmKyUjNZ_2a-If6mreHFSHW_ofj753TZdCB4NYn4HF1bt6Rv_3REjhW-B0Ayo8ipbpo8q0bt0tlpYqkUUrB-7bsNm3OY-uLVNN5UKDnP2fsqEWgDApBD9y0kRPdXZHjM_Vl-PbHcuKIxgkGCD87rV7yI5qup4T2it6CQwny4L21huR7QudyzfQgj5OrqCHm2QGKyW9-r3jHFfi0QDEUqmUfNbxyexE0IHnpmh2ojGUS4Sdw0onpYF6wyYBqoYpQQ5OLw-OCfKMGP5QjA4zQmwTCaR6a41NNQEu8qNjNOM4sfnALD3urA7SJoQTbU1kO0LIcQP0pKq8WQBSRciatp49czzPRW_R6kTjasT7bhdU7qDMq2vptU_s-Dwo4oQ/4td/s02KSihTT4Wy4B9gmAfQJQ/h6/h001.mb5pUA0nm3iCF7NOUkmpzAGr_aVOeYLMzRuBrM2zn6w)

The EconomyCOST-OF-LIVING ANXIETY IS DRIVING UNDECIDED VOTERS IN TWO SENATE BATTLEGROUNDSWhat's Happening
* New focus groups of undecided voters in **Iowa and Georgia** found economic anxiety to be the dominant concern heading into November.
* The dozen participants included six independents, five Republicans and one Democrat; nine backed Trump in the last presidential election and three backed Kamala Harris.
* All but three said they feel **more anxious about the economy now** than when Trump returned to office, and eight said he is not focused enough on it.

The Situation
* Participants cited the cost of healthcare, gas, food and utilities, with some describing delayed major purchases or selling possessions to cover bills.
* Rich Thau of Engagious, which ran the groups alongside Sago and Syracuse University, said economic anxiety is the animating midterm issue — "not Iran, not immigration."
* Important caveat: focus groups are qualitative and are **not a representative sample**. A dozen voters can show you a mood, not a margin.

The PerspectiveTwelve voters in two states do not decide a Senate majority, but the signal in this one is hard to wave off, because it is coming from people who already voted Republican and are still waiting to feel the benefit. Courtroom wins on maps and pressure campaigns abroad are real accomplishments, and neither shows up in a grocery cart. If the closing argument this fall is anything other than prices, Republicans will be talking about a scoreboard voters cannot see. The party that best explains how it will lower the monthly bill wins these two states.[Read the full story at NBC News](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.SfPhhFqVdCCzAqIAosiI_Hww93iPI4LJrShhMJMeWsBwwLRkiqL8TVbHKcIylW_-etZ_afeBRejRdXXJD4gt-iPCMDdXFWDFtODCk3pmO7iguLlRLFxgH9hn9yYaADhIyfV2tLAgA8yYVUHu1aBVgx3HAtoXs7o0iJZCo7HFzUXpCwtVljY_VDbj3Kp3KC0oR4_cxdNV3GpUUB62oQS2TAE0VoNc6JplqxKX5NDxx3vC1V-2evyOzR6w4GJzTQW7JgnyTNglyh8USl5sKVrB1sJxpJyH_Ahi5qWB3Txx-CS2KJ9C552ETEZHcthll0Fl_apMRDNGq5od_F28afb9-fgejlvcT17jJuTebG9z2bbxL328fK6VNvjkUTYnr_e2bDcHBJIXDYQWWjzLmXogxA/4td/s02KSihTT4Wy4B9gmAfQJQ/h7/h001.mdy8FDMW-V2SygGMuRX3-dt7gEMSk6w-Zy8M9WT0ZT0)

ImmigrationFIRST REMOVAL FLIGHT LANDS UNDER LIBERIA DEPORTATION AGREEMENTWhat's Happening
* The United States carried out its first deportation Thursday under an agreement for Liberia to accept up to **1,200 people who are not Liberian nationals**.
* Twenty deportees arrived at Roberts International Airport outside Monrovia.
* Liberian officials said the full group will arrive over 12 months and will include Africans as well as nationals from North America, South America and the Caribbean.

The Situation
* Per Liberian Information Minister Jerolinmek Piah and Justice Minister Natu Oswald Tweh, arrivals may seek asylum in Liberia or leave the country when they choose.
* Monrovia says it will receive U.S. support to strengthen its migration system and that the arrangement was not a quid pro quo — characterizations that come from the Liberian government and have not been independently verified.
* The administration has reached similar third-country agreements with at least 35 countries, and more than **23,000 people** have been removed to 26 countries under them.

The PerspectiveThird-country agreements exist to close a loophole that made a mockery of immigration law for decades: a foreign government could simply refuse to take its own nationals back, and a final removal order would quietly convert into permanent residence. An order a country cannot enforce is not a law, it is a suggestion. That said, enforcing the law well is part of enforcing it at all — where people are sent, whether the receiving country can actually absorb them, and how they are treated after landing are legitimate questions, and congressional oversight of these deals is a feature, not an obstacle.[Read the full story at NBC News](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.SfPhhFqVdCCzAqIAosiI_CxFUquvFkw68OM0iDID0yCS586KyA9dDlc76MjxR3LupLc0l0NSkx_hcFo3GTx45ikSmw0oiGoDdYvPuRR1UOHH5AhX4AY8A9Pg9tvJjUshbstqnjIQHUfJPlMm68TAW-xkut3VIuC397G90R9J1ColhF_vuhd8-SGVtJGs-9jSLspLAN6KMgWsrAiOf_ke0BJ7jipUp6afrPGFRa8OHainjWcoUZql3MmWb6Hk2AfRIrLEj2mqGQ5LAXwctknnKPW3KK5R63IXv6IAdFVSTBiG496cLFa8l9uV7gJd02rNu8ZjYx-rxhLvKJycKZ5M6NIv7oTWJ-n_fZsVIPxRyRpWscGz7ldr5Muf39xhCEQkb6zXVOfH-MXt8cxTF0B8ZA/4td/s02KSihTT4Wy4B9gmAfQJQ/h8/h001.9hhKSaUEN-Uekq6xJ4vsEwJ-kg2D-dGStXzfbG6eC-8)
| ⚡ The Bottom LineRepublicans had a good day in a Missouri courtroom, and a courtroom is not a kitchen table. The map that survived, the warrant that was served, the flight that landed in Monrovia — each is a win for the proposition that written law means what it says and applies to everyone equally. But a dozen undecided voters in Iowa and Georgia just reminded us that none of it lands with people still doing math on the drive to the grocery store. Institutions and prices are both on the ballot, and only one of them shows up in the monthly budget. That's just the truth.

If the closing argument this fall is anything other than prices, Republicans will be talking about a scoreboard voters cannot see. The party that best explains how it will lower the monthly bill wins these two states. ImmigrationFIRST REMOVAL FLIGHT LANDS UNDER LIBERIA DEPORTATION AGREEMENTWhat's Happening The United States carried out its first deportation Thursday under an agreement for Liberia to accept up to 1,200 people who are not Liberian nationals. Twenty deportees arrived at Roberts International Airport outside Monrovia. Liberian officials said the full group will arrive over 12 months and will include Africans as well as nationals from North America, South America and the Caribbean. The Situation Per Liberian Information Minister Jerolinmek Piah and Justice Minister Natu Oswald Tweh, arrivals may seek asylum in Liberia or leave the country when they choose. Monrovia says it will receive U.S. support to strengthen its migration system and that the arrangement was not a quid pro quo — characterizations that come from the Liberian government and have not been independently verified. The administration has reached similar third-country agreements with at least 35 countries, and more than 23,000 people have been removed to 26 countries under them. The PerspectiveThird-country agreements exist to close a loophole that made a mockery of immigration law for decades: a foreign government could simply refuse to take its own nationals back, and a final removal order would quietly convert into permanent residence. An order a country cannot enforce is not a law, it is a suggestion. That said, enforcing the law well is part of enforcing it at all — where people are sent, whether the receiving country can actually absorb them, and how they are treated after landing are legitimate questions, and congressional oversight of these deals is a feature, not an obstacle. | ⚡ The Bottom LineRepublicans had a good day in a Missouri courtroom, and a courtroom is not a kitchen table. The map that survived, the warrant that was served, the flight that landed in Monrovia — each is a win for the proposition that written law means what it says and applies to everyone equally. But a dozen undecided voters in Iowa and Georgia just reminded us that none of it lands with people still doing math on the drive to the grocery store. Institutions and prices are both on the ballot, and only one of them shows up in the monthly budget. That's just the truth. "The truth isn't conservative or liberal. It's just the truth."Just The Truth 6547 N Academy Blvd #2436 | Colorado Springs, CO 80918 | | | | Update your email preferences or unsubscribe (C) 2026 Just The Truth 228 Park Ave S, #29976, New York, New York 10003, United States |

## Photo Booth Pictures Lead Twins to Birth Mom
Marielle and Mireille Landry were identical twins adopted at three months old in a closed adoption in Nova Scotia. That meant no contact with their birth parents until they turned 18. They were 12 when a leftover strip of [photo booth pictures](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyskD1uhDAQRk8DnZEZm58tXKSh27QpkcHjtRPDIDOLtbePNmdI_33vSe_rPt9tTHF_fNoNjX_4mT3NO5YzITPm2R508mqz85m2gPbC3T3XH0czSOiFHAW0s105XjhrWzvjEQFVjaYdxkFpGADqYG6olRrsugxey0W3unV9B526Obkqb_s6mjdPjtCClB20zfC-jkrqBTrsACst0UWm3HxT3DmgTy-6MDcrbXUygfk4K_VRwVTBVEppnkehzOH1HlQwHbuwjg5GJ7jE_RQbIoslZg5iIw6YxWZTEkcgJrEQcahgqrNxR4kpxbMfKi0fm43pT8n_UOsy8BsAAP__tMiCMg) changed everything. name: True the Vote
subject: Round 1: Democracy Docket Got It Wrong
body:
Truth, prayer, and action.
| | August 21, 2026 | [**Read Online**](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/o8up29nr7ksqh6049rnsvhqp04onzcohde5z6/48hvhehmxpwl8gixh7/aHR0cHM6Ly9ja2FyY2hpdmUuY29tL2IvcWR1OGg3aDRsOHdydmF6d25ubXc3dThubTk2cXhmNGhrb3Z4OQ==) | |
---
| Hi Friend — We are under attack. This is one of several emails we’ll be sending over the coming days because ... we have had enough. Buckle up. Round 1. Please read to the end. Democracy Docket recently published a piece portraying True the Vote as part of an outside network supposedly shaping the Trump administration’s election policy. Here is the [article](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/o8up29nr7ksqh6049rnsvhqp04onzcohde5z6/wnh2hghq0km768t7hx/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZGVtb2NyYWN5ZG9ja2V0LmNvbS9uZXdzLWFsZXJ0cy90aGUtZWxlY3Rpb24tZGVuaWVycy1pbmZsdWVuY2luZy10cnVtcHMtYW50aS12b3RpbmctcG9saWN5LWZyb20tb3V0c2lkZS10aGUtd2hpdGUtaG91c2Uv): | [](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/o8up29nr7ksqh6049rnsvhqp04onzcohde5z6/wnh2hghq0km768t7hx/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZGVtb2NyYWN5ZG9ja2V0LmNvbS9uZXdzLWFsZXJ0cy90aGUtZWxlY3Rpb24tZGVuaWVycy1pbmZsdWVuY2luZy10cnVtcHMtYW50aS12b3RpbmctcG9saWN5LWZyb20tb3V0c2lkZS10aGUtd2hpdGUtaG91c2Uv)_Link:_[_https://www.democracydocket.com/news-alerts/the-election-deniers-influencing-trumps-anti-voting-policy-from-outside-the-white-house/_](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/o8up29nr7ksqh6049rnsvhqp04onzcohde5z6/wnh2hghq0km768t7hx/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZGVtb2NyYWN5ZG9ja2V0LmNvbS9uZXdzLWFsZXJ0cy90aGUtZWxlY3Rpb24tZGVuaWVycy1pbmZsdWVuY2luZy10cnVtcHMtYW50aS12b3RpbmctcG9saWN5LWZyb20tb3V0c2lkZS10aGUtd2hpdGUtaG91c2Uv)
---
There is a problem with that story.
One of the central facts it reports about me is simply false.
The article states that I attended a meeting in Washington with Cleta Mitchell and other election-integrity advocates ahead of President Trump’s remarks on elections.
I was not there.
Not “I don’t remember being there.” Not a disagreement over how the meeting should be characterized.
I was 100% not there. True the Vote did not participate in that meeting.
That matters because Democracy Docket then uses my supposed attendance as part of the foundation for its broader claim that True the Vote is an influential force “shaping” administration policy.
Remove the false premise, and that conclusion becomes considerably harder to support.
And that is important because Democracy Docket is what we call a “canary in the coal mine”. Their goal is to establish a narrative that the mockingbirds will faithfully repeat.
True the Vote is not an arm of this administration — or any administration.
We are an independent organization that works with American citizens. Voters. All of them, irrespective of party.
For sixteen years, our focus has remained remarkably consistent: citizens should be able to understand how their elections work, participate meaningfully in the process, examine public records, raise legitimate questions, and expect election systems worthy of public confidence.
When an administration takes meaningful steps toward those goals, we applaud it.
We applaud the efforts by the Trump Administration and we understand just how difficult it is to achieve meaningful reform in this environment.
There is an extraordinarily well-funded ecosystem of lawyers, NGOs, political operatives, and media outlets prepared to challenge almost every serious attempt to improve election transparency or accountability — silenced before the proposal can even be fairly considered.
And there is some relevant history you deserve to know.
Democracy Docket was founded by Marc Elias. His law firm, Elias Law Group, represents Fair Fight in years-long litigation against True the Vote.
We won that case at the district-court level. The litigation continues on appeal.
Democracy Docket’s own [case page](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/o8up29nr7ksqh6049rnsvhqp04onzcohde5z6/reh8hohm63kdzkt2h6/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZGVtb2NyYWN5ZG9ja2V0LmNvbS9jYXNlcy9nZW9yZ2lhLXZvdGVyLWludGltaWRhdGlvbi1zdWl0Lw==) is here:
[](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/o8up29nr7ksqh6049rnsvhqp04onzcohde5z6/reh8hohm63kdzkt2h6/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZGVtb2NyYWN5ZG9ja2V0LmNvbS9jYXNlcy9nZW9yZ2lhLXZvdGVyLWludGltaWRhdGlvbi1zdWl0Lw==)_Link:_[_https://www.democracydocket.com/cases/georgia-voter-intimidation-suit/_](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/o8up29nr7ksqh6049rnsvhqp04onzcohde5z6/reh8hohm63kdzkt2h6/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZGVtb2NyYWN5ZG9ja2V0LmNvbS9jYXNlcy9nZW9yZ2lhLXZvdGVyLWludGltaWRhdGlvbi1zdWl0Lw==)
---
Democracy Docket says its newsroom operates independently of Elias Law Group. But when an outlet founded by the lawyer whose firm represents our legal adversary publishes an article portraying us as dangerous “election deniers,” readers are entitled to understand the history surrounding that coverage.
They are also entitled to expect the basic facts to be right. In this instance, they weren’t. And it’s far from the first time this has happened.
Then there is Gregg Phillips.
Democracy Docket could not resist inserting a sneering aside that Gregg once claimed he had “teleported into a Waffle House,” complete with a parenthetical “don’t ask.”
It has nothing to do with election policy.
Nothing to do with the White House. Nothing to do with the premise of the article. It is there to discredit him.
But what they leave out is the human context.
Gregg’s comment was made on my personal podcast. I unwittingly created this hurt for him by asking him to allow me to chronicle his battle against cancer.
I’m writing the following with his permission.
Gregg has been fighting prostate cancer since 2019, which in 2023 progressed to stage-four metastatic bone cancer. In 2024, he had been given a devastating prognosis. He had been through aggressive radiation. It didn’t work. The next option was chemo, but he was forewarned, in his case there was no cure. What sustained him, then and now, was his faith. All glory to God.
In 2025, he embarked on an unbelievably tough alternative protocol.
Thousands of people were following his battle, asking how he was doing and praying for him. So we made the decision to document the journey.
All of it.
The treatments. The fear. The hope. The setbacks. The things that worked. The things that didn’t. And, yes, the supernatural experiences Gregg described during one of the most physically vulnerable periods of his life.
The conversation Democracy Docket chose to mock came during the very beginning of an intensive treatment protocol, while Gregg was heavily medicated and simply speaking openly about experiences he could not explain.
Even the word “teleportation” was not Gregg’s characterization, it was mine. I’d been with him through the valley and then, as now, I believe in the power of miracles. God’s hand was all over Gregg and never for a second did I believe we should be shy about sharing what was happening.
We showed Gregg’s cancer journey the way it actually happened — unfiltered — because that was the promise we had made to the thousands of people following along.
Reducing one moment from that journey to a cheap punch line tells readers considerably more about the people who chose to include it than it does about Gregg.
And at the time these attacks intensified, Gregg was serving as a federal employee (as he still is, which is another factually inaccurate datapoint) and was constrained in his ability to publicly defend himself.
So we did.
Here is what [we wrote](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/o8up29nr7ksqh6049rnsvhqp04onzcohde5z6/08hwh9h2l9nervulh5/aHR0cHM6Ly90cnVldGhldm90ZS5vcmcvbmV3cy9jaGluYS1zYXZlLWFtZXJpY2EtaW4tdGhlLXNlbmF0ZS1hbmQtdGVsZXBvcnRhdGlvbi1vaC1teQ==) at the time:
[](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/o8up29nr7ksqh6049rnsvhqp04onzcohde5z6/08hwh9h2l9nervulh5/aHR0cHM6Ly90cnVldGhldm90ZS5vcmcvbmV3cy9jaGluYS1zYXZlLWFtZXJpY2EtaW4tdGhlLXNlbmF0ZS1hbmQtdGVsZXBvcnRhdGlvbi1vaC1teQ==)_Link to newsletter:_[_https://truethevote.org/news/china-save-america-in-the-senate-and-teleportation-oh-my_](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/o8up29nr7ksqh6049rnsvhqp04onzcohde5z6/08hwh9h2l9nervulh5/aHR0cHM6Ly90cnVldGhldm90ZS5vcmcvbmV3cy9jaGluYS1zYXZlLWFtZXJpY2EtaW4tdGhlLXNlbmF0ZS1hbmQtdGVsZXBvcnRhdGlvbi1vaC1teQ==)
---
None of this means True the Vote expects immunity from criticism. Quite the opposite.
Challenge our research. Question our conclusions. Ask hard questions about our methodology. We have spent years working in an arena where disagreement is inevitable.
But criticism is different from caricature.
And advocacy masquerading as settled fact becomes especially problematic when the underlying reporting contains factual errors.
True the Vote does not work for Donald Trump. We do not work for the Republican Party. We do not work for Washington. We work with American citizens.
When government does the right thing, we will say so. When government fails, we will say so.
When powerful organizations use litigation, money, political influence, or media narratives to prevent citizens from asking legitimate questions about their elections, we will continue to stand our ground.
And when someone publishes something about us that simply isn’t true, we are going to correct the record.
We have spent a long time absorbing attacks.
We are fighting back.
Not with personal smears or manufactured narratives. With facts. With records. With evidence. And with the American citizens who have stood beside us from the beginning.
The Irish-philosopher Edmund Burke is often cited as having said, “The only thing necessary for the triumph of evil is for good men to do nothing.” Rise up, friend. Don’t do nothing. It’s time to fight.
Keep the faith. Never quit. Ephesians 6 FTW!
Ever onward —
---
P.S. — Marc Elias and Democracy Docket: this is a direct request to correct the record.
Your article states as fact that I attended the White House meeting you describe.
I did not. I was not there. True the Vote did not participate in that meeting.
You then use my supposed attendance as evidence for the much broader assertion that True the Vote is helping shape administration policy. That premise is false.
So I am calling on Democracy Docket to retract the false statement, correct the article, and clearly disclose the correction to your readers.
If you have evidence that I was present, publish it. If you do not, retract it.
You are free to disagree with us. You are free to criticize our work. You are not entitled to invent our attendance at meetings we did not attend and then use that fiction to support a predetermined narrative.
Marc, your law firm has spent years litigating against True the Vote. Democracy Docket has now published a demonstrably false statement about me. This is an opportunity to show your readers that, whatever our differences, facts still matter.
Correct it.
And while you are reviewing the piece, I hope you will reconsider the gratuitous attempt to discredit Gregg Phillips by mocking an intensely vulnerable moment from his documented battle with metastatic cancer — a detail that had absolutely nothing to do with the subject of your article.
You may disagree with Gregg. You may dislike him. But turning a man’s battle with cancer into a punch line was beneath the subject, beneath the article, and frankly, beneath you.
If you didn’t know when you wrote it, you know now.
If you knew and still wrote it, may God have mercy on your soul.

[**Please Help Us If You Can**](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/o8up29nr7ksqh6049rnsvhqp04onzcohde5z6/8ghqhohor2wdndfkh9/aHR0cHM6Ly90cnVldGhldm90ZS5vcmcvZG9uYXRl)
---

|
### **Make Sure Our Emails Always Reach You**
UPDATE: We continue to get "Hellos" and they absolutely make our day. 😊 If you've followed the steps below, no need to do it again. If you missed it.... here's what this is all about. Sending email to our entire list has become increasingly difficult. Our detractors have made a practice of filing complaints about our weekly messages, and those complaints train the filters — which means frictionless delivery is now nearly impossible. And we expect it to get harder, not easier. **The most reliable fix is on your end: please whitelist our name.** It takes less than a minute, and it works in every email program, old or new. Here's how to do it:
1. Open your email program and find a message from True the Vote — check your Spam, Junk, or Promotions folder if you don't see one in your inbox.
2. If it's in Spam or Junk, click **Not Spam** (or **Not Junk**), then move the message to your inbox.
3. Open one of our emails and add the sender address — [**catherinee@truethevote.org**](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/o8up29nr7ksqh6049rnsvhqp04onzcohde5z6/vqh3hrhowvm0rrtghl/bWFpbHRvOmNhdGhlcmluZWVAdHJ1ZXRoZXZvdGUub3Jn)**** — to your contacts or address book. In most programs you can right-click the sender's name and choose **Add to Contacts.**
4. To seal the deal, reply to this email with a quick "hello" — even one word. Nothing signals "this sender is welcome" more strongly than a reply.

That's it. This same four-step habit works for True the Vote or any sender you don't want to miss — your bank, your doctor, your church. Thank you for taking a moment to keep our line open. We'll keep doing our part with our email provider, and together we'll stay connected. |
