Remove the false premise, and that conclusion becomes considerably harder to support. And that is important because Democracy Docket is what we call a “canary in the coal mine”. Their goal is to establish a narrative that the mockingbirds will faithfully repeat. True the Vote is not an arm of this administration — or any administration. We are an independent organization that works with American citizens. Voters. All of them, irrespective of party. For sixteen years, our focus has remained remarkably consistent: citizens should be able to understand how their elections work, participate meaningfully in the process, examine public records, raise legitimate questions, and expect election systems worthy of public confidence. When an administration takes meaningful steps toward those goals, we applaud it. We applaud the efforts by the Trump Administration and we understand just how difficult it is to achieve meaningful reform in this environment. There is an extraordinarily well-funded ecosystem of lawyers, NGOs, political operatives, and media outlets prepared to challenge almost every serious attempt to improve election transparency or accountability — silenced before the proposal can even be fairly considered. And there is some relevant history you deserve to know. Democracy Docket was founded by Marc Elias. His law firm, Elias Law Group, represents Fair Fight in years-long litigation against True the Vote. We won that case at the district-court level. The litigation continues on appeal. Democracy Docket’s own == is here: == Democracy Docket says its newsroom operates independently of Elias Law Group. But when an outlet founded by the lawyer whose firm represents our legal adversary publishes an article portraying us as dangerous “election deniers,” readers are entitled to understand the history surrounding that coverage. They are also entitled to expect the basic facts to be right. In this instance, they weren’t. And it’s far from the first time this has happened. Then there is Gregg Phillips. Democracy Docket could not resist inserting a sneering aside that Gregg once claimed he had “teleported into a Waffle House,” complete with a parenthetical “don’t ask.” It has nothing to do with election policy. Nothing to do with the White House. Nothing to do with the premise of the article. It is there to discredit him. But what they leave out is the human context. Gregg’s comment was made on my personal podcast. I unwittingly created this hurt for him by asking him to allow me to chronicle his battle against cancer. I’m writing the following with his permission. Gregg has been fighting prostate cancer since 2019, which in 2023 progressed to stage-four metastatic bone cancer. In 2024, he had been given a devastating prognosis. He had been through aggressive radiation. It didn’t work. The next option was chemo, but he was forewarned, in his case there was no cure. What sustained him, then and now, was his faith. All glory to God. In 2025, he embarked on an unbelievably tough alternative protocol. Thousands of people were following his battle, asking how he was doing and praying for him. So we made the decision to document the journey. All of it. The treatments. The fear. The hope. The setbacks. The things that worked. The things that didn’t. And, yes, the supernatural experiences Gregg described during one of the most physically vulnerable periods of his life. The conversation Democracy Docket chose to mock came during the very beginning of an intensive treatment protocol, while Gregg was heavily medicated and simply speaking openly about experiences he could not explain. Even the word “teleportation” was not Gregg’s characterization, it was mine. I’d been with him through the valley and then, as now, I believe in the power of miracles. God’s hand was all over Gregg and never for a second did I believe we should be shy about sharing what was happening. We showed Gregg’s cancer journey the way it actually happened — unfiltered — because that was the promise we had made to the thousands of people following along. Reducing one moment from that journey to a cheap punch line tells readers considerably more about the people who chose to include it than it does about Gregg. And at the time these attacks intensified, Gregg was serving as a federal employee (as he still is, which is another factually inaccurate datapoint) and was constrained in his ability to publicly defend himself. So we did. Here is what == at the time: to newsletter:== None of this means True the Vote expects immunity from criticism. Quite the opposite. Challenge our research. Question our conclusions. Ask hard questions about our methodology. We have spent years working in an arena where disagreement is inevitable. But criticism is different from caricature. And advocacy masquerading as settled fact becomes especially problematic when the underlying reporting contains factual errors. True the Vote does not work for Donald Trump. We do not work for the Republican Party. We do not work for Washington. We work with American citizens. When government does the right thing, we will say so. When government fails, we will say so. When powerful organizations use litigation, money, political influence, or media narratives to prevent citizens from asking legitimate questions about their elections, we will continue to stand our ground. And when someone publishes something about us that simply isn’t true, we are going to correct the record. We have spent a long time absorbing attacks. We are fighting back. Not with personal smears or manufactured narratives. With facts. With records. With evidence. And with the American citizens who have stood beside us from the beginning. The Irish-philosopher Edmund Burke is often cited as having said, “The only thing necessary for the triumph of evil is for good men to do nothing.” Rise up, friend. Don’t do nothing. It’s time to fight. Keep the faith. Never quit. Ephesians 6 FTW! Ever onward — P.S. — Marc Elias and Democracy Docket: this is a direct request to correct the record. Your article states as fact that I attended the White House meeting you describe. I did not. I was not there. True the Vote did not participate in that meeting. You then use my supposed attendance as evidence for the much broader assertion that True the Vote is helping shape administration policy. That premise is false. So I am calling on Democracy Docket to retract the false statement, correct the article, and clearly disclose the correction to your readers. If you have evidence that I was present, publish it. If you do not, retract it. You are free to disagree with us. You are free to criticize our work. You are not entitled to invent our attendance at meetings we did not attend and then use that fiction to support a predetermined narrative. Marc, your law firm has spent years litigating against True the Vote. Democracy Docket has now published a demonstrably false statement about me. This is an opportunity to show your readers that, whatever our differences, facts still matter. Correct it. And while you are reviewing the piece, I hope you will reconsider the gratuitous attempt to discredit Gregg Phillips by mocking an intensely vulnerable moment from his documented battle with metastatic cancer — a detail that had absolutely nothing to do with the subject of your article. You may disagree with Gregg. You may dislike him. But turning a man’s battle with cancer into a punch line was beneath the subject, beneath the article, and frankly, beneath you. If you didn’t know when you wrote it, you know now. If you knew and still wrote it, may God have mercy on your soul. | Make Sure Our Emails Always Reach You UPDATE: We continue to get "Hellos" and they absolutely make our day. 😊 If you've followed the steps below, no need to do it again. If you missed it.... here's what this is all about. Sending email to our entire list has become increasingly difficult. Our detractors have made a practice of filing complaints about our weekly messages, and those complaints train the filters — which means frictionless delivery is now nearly impossible. And we expect it to get harder, not easier. The most reliable fix is on your end: please whitelist our name. It takes less than a minute, and it works in every email program, old or new. Here's how to do it: 1. Open your email program and find a message from True the Vote — check your Spam, Junk, or Promotions folder if you don't see one in your inbox. 2. If it's in Spam or Junk, click Not Spam (or Not Junk), then move the message to your inbox. 3. Open one of our emails and add the sender address — ** — to your contacts or address book. In most programs you can right-click the sender's name and choose Add to Contacts.** 4. To seal the deal, reply to this email with a quick "hello" — even one word. Nothing signals "this sender is welcome" more strongly than a reply. That's it. This same four-step habit works for True the Vote or any sender you don't want to miss — your bank, your doctor, your church. Thank you for taking a moment to keep our line open. We'll keep doing our part with our email provider, and together we'll stay connected. | ---|---|--- | | == Update your or unsubscribe © 2026 True the Vote 3120 Southwest Frwy Ste 101, PMB 19128, Houston, Texas 77098-4520

Dear Friend, With Election Day getting closer, we're building the volunteer organization that will carry this campaign through the final stretch -- and there are plenty of ways to be part of it. It starts tomorrow morning in Washington with the kickoff of our Washington Area Community Action Team, with more Town Halls and opportunities to get involved coming up across the district. Whether you want to help in your own community, meet Alan, ask him a question, or introduce someone new to the campaign, we hope you'll join us at an upcoming event.
### **Tomorrow: Washington Area Volunteer Meeting**
**Saturday, August 22 | 11:30 AM - 1:00 PM**
**The Center on Strawberry**
59 East Strawberry Ave, Washington, PA 15301 Tomorrow morning, we're kicking off the **Washington Area Bradstock Community Action Team**. This is an opportunity to learn how you can help build support for Alan in your own community -- whether that's talking with friends and neighbors, helping spread the word about the campaign, volunteering at events, or finding other ways to get involved. You don't need to be an experienced campaign volunteer. If you support Alan and want to help us build the organization we need to win, we'd love to have you join us. Whether you want to help in your own community, meet Alan, ask him a question, or introduce someone new to the campaign, we hope you'll join us at an upcoming event. Tomorrow: Washington Area Volunteer Meeting Saturday, August 22 | 11:30 AM - 1:00 PM The Center on Strawberry 59 East Strawberry Ave, Washington, PA 15301 Tomorrow morning, we're kicking off the Washington Area Bradstock Community Action Team. This is an opportunity to learn how you can help build support for Alan in your own community -- whether that's talking with friends and neighbors, helping spread the word about the campaign, volunteering at events, or finding other ways to get involved. You don't need to be an experienced campaign volunteer. If you support Alan and want to help us build the organization we need to win, we'd love to have you join us. ~ Alan's Town Hall SeriesContinues Alan believes that running for Congress means showing up, listening, answering questions, and being accessible to the people you hope to represent. That's why we've been holding Town Halls throughout the district -- open to everyone, regardless of political party. We now have six upcoming Town Halls scheduled across the district: Tuesday, August 25 - Monongahela 6:00 - 8:00 PM Monongahela American Legion 1938 Rte 2023, Monongahela ~ Tuesday, September 1 - Somerset 6:00 - 8:00 PM Somerset Borough Public Safety Community Room 340 W Union St, Somerset ~ Monday, September 14 - Carmichaels 6:00 - 8:00 PM American Legion Post 400 205 E George St, Carmichaels ~ Thursday, September 17 - Peters Township 7:00 - 9:00 PM St. David's Episcopal Church 905 East McMurray Road, Venetia ~ Thursday, September 24 - Uniontown 6:00 - 8:00 PM Venue 67 67 Connellsville St, Uniontown ~ Monday, September 28 - Washington 6:00 - 8:00 PM American Legion Post 175 168 Park Ave, Washington ~ At every Town Hall, Alan will talk about why he's running, the issues facing our communities, and his priorities for Congress -- and then open the floor to questions. Bring your questions. Bring a friend or neighbor. And if you know someone who hasn't met Alan yet, invite them to come hear from him directly. Can't make one of these events? We're continuing to add Town Halls, volunteer opportunities, canvasses, and other events throughout the district. For a complete list of all of our Town Halls and volunteer oppurtunities, please visit ~ Thank you for being part of this campaign. Every conversation, every volunteer, and every person who shows up helps us build the grassroots organization we need to win. We hope to see you soon! Phillip Whoriskey Field Director Bradstock for Congress 703-869-4480 ~~ P.S. Grassroots campaigns are powered by volunteers and supporters like you. If you'd also like to help us continue growing our organizing operation across the district, contributions of any amount make a real difference. ➡️ ~~ | ~~ "Facebook" "Instagram" mailto:info@bradstockforcongress.com "Email" ~ "Bluesky" "X" ~ "YouTube" Bradstock for Congress P.O. She never had the luxury of a career path or a safety net. She just kept going, because that's what it took. That's the America I come from. Not a talking point, my actual childhood. And I'll be honest: it's infuriating to watch politicians in Washington talk about working families like we're an abstraction, while they vote for policies that make it harder for everyday people to catch a break. Rising costs. Corporations and billionaires posting record profits while paying next to nothing in taxes. A minimum wage that hasn't kept up with the reality of housing and healthcare costs in years. America can do better than this. We must do better than this.

# **[Dalio smells blood in the water and loads Gold and Bitcoin](https://substack.com/redirect/25da9f58-cf6d-487f-bbdd-1c24ebcfb399?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Ray Dalio just looked at Scott Bessent's debt buyback and called it the flashing red light. Government is spending 40% more than it takes in. July deficit hit $432 billion. Debt service would run roughly $11 trillion against annual revenue if this were a real company. Crisis window: one to five years, his guess three. Dump the bonds. Put 10-15% in gold and a bit of bitcoin.
* **Winners?** Gold and bitcoin holders who move first. Capital that stays underweight Treasuries before the forced adjustment hits.
* **Losers?** Bondholders still treating U.S. debt as risk-free. Everyday savers who eat the inflation or tax haircut when the music stops.
* **Next?** Longer yields keep grinding higher. More foreign dumping of U.S. paper. Either real spending cuts and tax hikes land or the trauma arrives on schedule.

This is late-cycle arithmetic, pure and simple. You cannot outgrow or inflate away this mountain without pain. Dalio's three-prong fix, cut spending, raise revenue, ease rates carefully, sounds clean until Washington touches it. Position in the hard assets or get steamrolled. The ones who prepare who print. The ones who hope get the bag of IOUs.

# **[Apple swings the axe at Siri and Vision Pro to feed the real AI machine](https://substack.com/redirect/25da9f58-cf6d-487f-bbdd-1c24ebcfb399?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Apple just cut more than 200 jobs, roughly 100 from Vision Pro gaming and immersive video, another 100 from Siri and software AI teams. This is not panic. It is triage. New AI-powered Siri needs different skills. Vision Pro usage data showed gaming and fancy video were dead ends. Resources are shifting to future devices that actually move the needle.
* **Winners?** Apple shareholders and the remaining AI/hardware talent who get the new roles. Anyone who bets on focused execution over headcount.
* **Losers?** The cut workers and anyone still dreaming Vision Pro becomes a mass-market gaming platform. Soft software teams that could not ship.
* **Next?** Cleaner AI Siri rollout. Thinner support for underperforming Vision initiatives. More efficiency moves as the handoff approaches.

This lines up with the earlier call that AI hardware is the only future that matters. Cutting dead weight while doubling down on what prints is pure profit discipline. The market rewards results, not nostalgia. Watch the new Siri, if it lands, this bloodletting looks like genius.

# **[John Ternus inherits the $32 million-an-hour throne](https://substack.com/redirect/25da9f58-cf6d-487f-bbdd-1c24ebcfb399?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
John Ternus takes the CEO chair September 1. The number he has to beat is $32 million, that is the average hourly market-cap creation under Tim Cook as Apple went from roughly $350 billion to $4.5 trillion. Revenue nearly quadrupled to over $400 billion. Hardware engineer replacing the operations king. The bar is absurdly high.
* **Winners?** Ternus if he protects the profit machine and restores product surprise. Long-term holders who keep compounding at this scale.
* **Losers?** Anyone expecting overnight fireworks. Short-term traders if the transition creates even a small hiccup around the holiday launches.
* **Next?** Smooth handoff. Cook stays close on policy. Ternus pushes hardware-led AI devices. The stock will judge him on the next category, not the past.

Cook turned Apple into the most profitable machine on earth. Ternus has to keep the cash flowing and deliver the technological magic markets still crave. $32 million an hour is the measuring stick. Miss it and the market reminds him daily. Hit it and he joins the pantheon. No pressure John.

# **[Micron CEO confirms the memory famine and the printer is just warming up](https://substack.com/redirect/25da9f58-cf6d-487f-bbdd-1c24ebcfb399?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Sanjay Mehrotra just told CNBC the quiet part loud: data-center customers want about 50% more memory than Micron can even commit. AI is eating DRAM and HBM alive. Revenue already up nearly 167% year-over-year. Stock jumped almost 4%. This is the exact **[RAMageddon](https://substack.com/redirect/f4fa0cbf-dd15-4125-9a6b-737dfac15eee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** I flagged when Wall Street crowned Micron the next Nvidia.
* **Winners?** Micron shareholders and anyone long high-bandwidth memory. The pick-and-shovel names that own the bottleneck print while demand stays inelastic.
* **Losers?** Hyperscalers and device makers forced to pay up or ration capacity. Weaker semiconductor names that cannot deliver advanced nodes.
* **Next?** More capacity announcements, higher ASPs, and the stock grinding higher on structural shortage through 2027. Supply does not catch demand overnight.

Exactly as predicted in **["Wall Street crowns Micron the next Nvidia."](https://substack.com/redirect/f4fa0cbf-dd15-4125-9a6b-737dfac15eee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Memory is the new oil. When the CEO admits he cannot fill the orders, you do not sell, you load the truck harder. This shortage has legs. Let the weak hands finance the upside.

body:
| | | Peter, 25,000. That’s the number of donations a 91-year-old woman in assisted living was manipulated into giving to Democratic causes through spam emails. And she isn’t the only one. This week, a Stanford political science professor released new reporting about the consulting companies and PACs across the political left — including some of the highest-ranking Democrats and committees — **taking advantage of well-meaning supporters and vulnerable seniors through fundraising emails filled with cheap tricks**.1 These emails tempt you with massive donation matches that never existed. They scream in all-caps about urgent deadlines they pulled out of thin air. They fool you into opening them with subject lines about job interviews and flight confirmations. If you’ve fallen for any of these tactics, Peter, you’re not alone. Scam PACs have raised over $1.4 billion since 2017, a shocking percentage of which (64% in some cases) is spent solely on raising _even more money_. **At the Working Families Party, we’re committed to building our movement with honesty and respect, spending what we raise on work that truly matters to our communities.[If that’s the kind of organization you want to see succeed, we would be grateful for any contribution that you’re able to make today.](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqvlwhslwHzsYo7bshL1ic1bfv_rqEDumUkUFVYwSCxDQSuVCKKXf16KTIi8PqLG9-zX3X-Uh5BL3_ozj9mGfEKrnvqO5Ujqye2BLdyvXlGpadEGUjz4hMpfWinx6oejoxgU_VtgDDhXNri0axMTpG6FKnPk2Cc1NhljBH5qZVLwlJKvcRKIAP0hxNO7ZICHG8LzvjEyOfmT-j1zf0I_gAJ-QlDId7Rf0AHjjppGw8y0qXjFiJg4owqP0tnVrA3UNz2FU9YbL_QlsO4ObpxH2w_xREdej355rBv-2MeHCaXw5_hNBYYz5cFOPC4BQv6uo2O1rjIN5iKhIyeTUFJOBEOY/4td/PlSTA6bVRaao3J0Bw3U4qQ/h0/h001.OEK3OOIghSwlDMJjdeNCORRfB2UyK9VzCl3Q_7xdqKo)** **[Make a donation to the Working Families Party](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqvlwhslwHzsYo7bshL1ic1bfv_rqEDumUkUFVYwSCxDQSuVCKKXf16KTIi8PqLG9-zX3X-Uh5BL3_ozj9mGfEKr2bV5eDuvHH-MyB4a5nO3vUdmqBqZuxDOswvJnXzN-F85yLzqKiq4naOkIQ242s6lxb7Q5KnoJ0CIFUyVjG_DHveWwUNF9hirZIExt4QhjKU2xZAia3Fxcy9Bl2C0t_R4npvbe4CZ1oU-C4UyuxCuHHH_Xhvtv-_m6PfMIONalSZbRUEHMZH_nz3eOhStEA5pPIIkJnayZts1EvQ4TSoYTcr9DVAdxlSlrHJ0bCV6cl5HkaOJH5OhG-WvfaSBTk52/4td/PlSTA6bVRaao3J0Bw3U4qQ/h1/h001.b98fGa8LOwrlg5lUECyoEGbQDq0OZGjHEb_T1smsJ1s)** This is a crisis, Peter. But instead of standing up to the political scammers abusing its users, Gmail is instead making it easier for spam emails to reach your inbox, per new reporting from the New York Times.2 **We’re going to be honest with you, Peter. We’re pissed off.** We believe that candidates and organizations cannot claim to fight for the working class when they abuse and exploit the same people they claim to represent. We believe that we owe it to you, and to anyone who takes the time to read our emails, to treat you with respect and dignity. And most of all, we believe that our mission is worth asking you to fight for — without resorting to scare tactics or lies. **When we ask you to donate to the Working Families Party, it’s because we know our organizing works and that by electing more WFP Champions to office, we will continue to change working people’s lives for the better.** We’re building a government of bold leaders who fight for the people over the powerful, winning 19 competitive congressional primaries so far this year, along with scores of down-ballot races. Your donations aren’t a trick. They’re an investment in the future and the party we’re building together. clean_body: | | | Peter, 25,000. That’s the number of donations a 91-year-old woman in assisted living was manipulated into giving to Democratic causes through spam emails. And she isn’t the only one. This week, a Stanford political science professor released new reporting about the consulting companies and PACs across the political left — including some of the highest-ranking Democrats and committees — taking advantage of well-meaning supporters and vulnerable seniors through fundraising emails filled with cheap tricks.1 These emails tempt you with massive donation matches that never existed. They scream in all-caps about urgent deadlines they pulled out of thin air. They fool you into opening them with subject lines about job interviews and flight confirmations. If you’ve fallen for any of these tactics, Peter, you’re not alone. Scam PACs have raised over $1.4 billion since 2017, a shocking percentage of which (64% in some cases) is spent solely on raising even more money. At the Working Families Party, we’re committed to building our movement with honesty and respect, spending what we raise on work that truly matters to our communities. This is a crisis, Peter. But instead of standing up to the political scammers abusing its users, Gmail is instead making it easier for spam emails to reach your inbox, per new reporting from the New York Times.2 We’re going to be honest with you, Peter. We’re pissed off. We believe that candidates and organizations cannot claim to fight for the working class when they abuse and exploit the same people they claim to represent. We believe that we owe it to you, and to anyone who takes the time to read our emails, to treat you with respect and dignity. And most of all, we believe that our mission is worth asking you to fight for — without resorting to scare tactics or lies. When we ask you to donate to the Working Families Party, it’s because we know our organizing works and that by electing more WFP Champions to office, we will continue to change working people’s lives for the better. We’re building a government of bold leaders who fight for the people over the powerful, winning 19 competitive congressional primaries so far this year, along with scores of down-ballot races. Your donations aren’t a trick. They’re an investment in the future and the party we’re building together. And the spam emails hitting millions of inboxes nationwide are hurting all of us. So we’ve got two requests for you. First, talk to any vulnerable seniors in your life and warn them about these tactics and how to spot them. Second, vote with your wallet: Do not reward these tactics with a single cent more, and, if you can, focus your support on the organizations that are living their values. If you would like to choose to no tricks, no gimmicks, no lies — thank you. Your support means the world to us, and is the reason we’re able to keep doing this work to build a political party by and for the multi-racial working class. If not — then thank you for reading this far. We’re so honored that you’re a part of our movement. body:
Running where independence is truly required...

| | | [ ](www.forwardparty.com)
---
### Peter —
This week’s Fast Forward is building on the foundation we emphasized last week with the pursuits for ballot access, the expansion to 41 states, and the lasting infrastructure that will go beyond one election cycle. This week, we want to show you who that foundation is for. In recent days, Forward Party endorsed three candidates in Ohio, New York, and Montana, whose regions could not be more different, and whose candidacies say the same thing: **there are good people everywhere who are done waiting for the two parties to fix things, and they are doing something about it.** **We would like to spotlight those candidates and the work they stand on.** |
## **Tracey Tackett**
Independent Candidate - Ohio's 4th Congressional District
---
Tracey Tackett has been doing the essential work of local government in Springfield, Ohio for years. As Assistant Mayor, she represents the city on boards and commissions covering economic development, transportation, neighborhood engagement, historic preservation, and community relations. This is the kind of work that determines whether a city functions, businesses open, or even if neighborhoods stay together.
She has also served in leadership roles with the Epilepsy Foundation of Ohio, the Glen Helen Association, Habitat for Humanity, the Greater Springfield Chamber of Commerce, and the American Cancer Society.
Her campaign is built on the conviction that OH-04 deserves a representative who brings people together rather than using the district as a vehicle for partisan warfare. She is running as an independent not because she couldn't choose a party but because she has decided that the party framework itself is the problem.
## **Alissa Ellman**
Independent Candidate - New York's 24th Congressional District
---
Alissa Ellman joined the military before she was old enough to vote. She served at Bagram Airfield in Afghanistan, came home, and then spent years teaching underprivileged students before helping fellow veterans navigate the Department of Veterans Affairs to obtain the benefits they earned. She was doing that VA work when the Department of Government Efficiency eliminated her position.
That loss activated her. She began hosting town halls and listening sessions across New York's 24th District and then launched a campaign for Congress that won the Democratic primary in June. She is now in the general election, and Forward Party is standing with her.
Her platform covers affordability, healthcare access, childcare, infrastructure, responsive constituent services, and election reforms including ranked-choice voting. But what defines her campaign more than any specific issue is the operating principle underneath all of them: **listen first, govern pragmatically, represent everyone in the district, not just the people who share your political affiliation.** That is a Forward Party principle as much as it is a campaign message. It is why we are endorsing her even as a Democratic nominee, because Forward has always said that good representation matters more than party label.
## **Dr. Michael Eisenhauer**
Independent Candidate - Montana's 2nd Congressional District
---
Dr. Michael Eisenhauer spent nearly 25 years in the United States Army as a physician and medical corps officer, serving in leadership positions around the world before deploying to Iraq as Deputy Forces Surgeon and Chief of Clinical Operations for Multi-National Forces–Iraq. He earned the Bronze Star for that service. When he retired from active duty, he came home to Montana and kept working, traveling to rural communities across the state to provide specialized cardiac care to patients who otherwise had no access to it.
He is running for Montana's 2nd Congressional District as an independent because he believes the two-party system has stopped delivering for Montanans. Congress has dismal approval ratings, young Montanans are losing faith in the American Dream, and the people sent to Washington to fix these things keep prioritizing their party over their constituents. His platform focuses on affordability, healthcare, veterans' issues, and reducing the partisan gridlock that has made Congress functionally useless on the issues Montana actually cares about. As an independent, he answers only to the people of Montana. That is the job as he sees it.
### **What These Endorsements Say**
It is easy to make an argument for a better political system. Forward Party makes that argument every day. What is harder, and what matters more, is backing that argument with real candidates in real races, in places where real voters are being asked to make a choice this November.
Ohio, New York, and Montana are all very different but connected in wanting to revive faith in our democracy.
These are Forward Party's megaphones. They speak in their own voices, from their own experience, to their own communities. That is the point. A movement that only produces candidates who sound like the party is not a movement. Forward Party is something different: **a home for the kind of people who want to serve their communities and understand the needs of those communities better than any party leaders could.**
**As we get closer to November 3, Forward Party will continue endorsing candidates who meet our standard, wherever they are, whatever their background, ensuring more and better choices are on the ballot.**
##### _Please forward this to your friends, family, and coworkers. It helps us introduce them to Forward and to what we are building. Also consider inviting them to one of our upcoming events listed below. We'd love to meet them._

clean_body: Running where independence is truly required... | | | www.forwardparty.com Peter — This week’s Fast Forward is building on the foundation we emphasized last week with the pursuits for ballot access, the expansion to 41 states, and the lasting infrastructure that will go beyond one election cycle. This week, we want to show you who that foundation is for. In recent days, Forward Party endorsed three candidates in Ohio, New York, and Montana, whose regions could not be more different, and whose candidacies say the same thing: there are good people everywhere who are done waiting for the two parties to fix things, and they are doing something about it. We would like to spotlight those candidates and the work they stand on. | Tracey Tackett Independent Candidate - Ohio's 4th Congressional District Tracey Tackett has been doing the essential work of local government in Springfield, Ohio for years. As Assistant Mayor, she represents the city on boards and commissions covering economic development, transportation, neighborhood engagement, historic preservation, and community relations. This is the kind of work that determines whether a city functions, businesses open, or even if neighborhoods stay together. She has also served in leadership roles with the Epilepsy Foundation of Ohio, the Glen Helen Association, Habitat for Humanity, the Greater Springfield Chamber of Commerce, and the American Cancer Society. Her campaign is built on the conviction that OH-04 deserves a representative who brings people together rather than using the district as a vehicle for partisan warfare. She is running as an independent not because she couldn't choose a party but because she has decided that the party framework itself is the problem. Alissa Ellman Independent Candidate - New York's 24th Congressional District Alissa Ellman joined the military before she was old enough to vote. She served at Bagram Airfield in Afghanistan, came home, and then spent years teaching underprivileged students before helping fellow veterans navigate the Department of Veterans Affairs to obtain the benefits they earned. She was doing that VA work when the Department of Government Efficiency eliminated her position. That loss activated her. She began hosting town halls and listening sessions across New York's 24th District and then launched a campaign for Congress that won the Democratic primary in June. She is now in the general election, and Forward Party is standing with her. Her platform covers affordability, healthcare access, childcare, infrastructure, responsive constituent services, and election reforms including ranked-choice voting. But what defines her campaign more than any specific issue is the operating principle underneath all of them: listen first, govern pragmatically, represent everyone in the district, not just the people who share your political affiliation. That is a Forward Party principle as much as it is a campaign message. It is why we are endorsing her even as a Democratic nominee, because Forward has always said that good representation matters more than party label. Dr. Michael Eisenhauer Independent Candidate - Montana's 2nd Congressional District Dr. Michael Eisenhauer spent nearly 25 years in the United States Army as a physician and medical corps officer, serving in leadership positions around the world before deploying to Iraq as Deputy Forces Surgeon and Chief of Clinical Operations for Multi-National Forces–Iraq. He earned the Bronze Star for that service. When he retired from active duty, he came home to Montana and kept working, traveling to rural communities across the state to provide specialized cardiac care to patients who otherwise had no access to it. He is running for Montana's 2nd Congressional District as an independent because he believes the two-party system has stopped delivering for Montanans. Congress has dismal approval ratings, young Montanans are losing faith in the American Dream, and the people sent to Washington to fix these things keep prioritizing their party over their constituents. His platform focuses on affordability, healthcare, veterans' issues, and reducing the partisan gridlock that has made Congress functionally useless on the issues Montana actually cares about. As an independent, he answers only to the people of Montana. That is the job as he sees it. What These Endorsements Say It is easy to make an argument for a better political system. Forward Party makes that argument every day. What is harder, and what matters more, is backing that argument with real candidates in real races, in places where real voters are being asked to make a choice this November. Ohio, New York, and Montana are all very different but connected in wanting to revive faith in our democracy. These are Forward Party's megaphones. They speak in their own voices, from their own experience, to their own communities. That is the point. A movement that only produces candidates who sound like the party is not a movement. Forward Party is something different: a home for the kind of people who want to serve their communities and understand the needs of those communities better than any party leaders could. As we get closer to November 3, Forward Party will continue endorsing candidates who meet our standard, wherever they are, whatever their background, ensuring more and better choices are on the ballot. body:
# [](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/3095?t=1&akid=5613%2E35263%2EDBqwzn)
Peter,
When I first ran for office, I didn’t set out to break barriers. I ran because I wanted to fight hard for Wisconsin families.
Very quickly, I learned that **no obstacle is too big when the fight is worth it.**
That's how I became Wisconsin's first woman ever elected to Congress. And when I won my Senate seat, I became the first openly LGBTQ+ Senator in U.S. history.
[](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/6050?c0=em-ms-tb-20260821-barriers.uDTH6G&amount=5&refcode=&t=2&akid=5613%2E35263%2EDBqwzn)
I’m proud of those firsts. But the barrier I care most about breaking is the one that keeps working families locked out of a fair shot.
I’ve worked across party lines to strengthen economic security for Wisconsinites — investing in our state’s job readiness, expanding access to quality health care, and protecting retirement security.
**There is _so_ much more we can accomplish together, and breaking down barriers so more people can join the fight is exactly how we’re going to do it.**
I didn't get here alone, and we won't keep this progress alone either.

_As a mother who 's passionate about youth sports, I felt the urge to intervene._I didn't go for the publicity... I went to stand up for something I'm passionate about and am prepared to staunchly defend.When I first launched this campaign for U.S. Senate in Minnesota, _I knew I would have to prepare myself and my family for the pain and vitriol that would be slung my way._**But, never in my wildest dreams would I imagine something so basic to be the cause of such heated debate. Biology isn 't complicated. Women are born with a specific set of chromosomes. So are men. They're different.

**That's why we have women's divisions in sports, so women can compete on a fair playing field.

And every roster is finite. Every team excludes someone. That's not bigotry, that's how sports work.

Women's sports should belong to women.Fellow American, if you can agree with me on that, then I have a feeling we'll be aligned on plenty of other things.Unfortunately, my far-Left candidate is not the same. She supports biological men in girls' sports, taxpayer-funded surgeries, and largely prefers lunacy over common sense.[If you want a candidate who’s looking to restore common sense to our communities, Fellow American, then I’m graciously asking you to become a supporter of this movement. **PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Happy Friday!
Here's a summary of today's top stories:
**🏔️ Here in Colorado...** A Denver audit found the $149 million 16th Street project ballooned to $175.6 million via an [$18 million change order that bypassed City Council,](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) with $1.03 million in penalties waived. Colorado cities are taking a[ ](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)[scattershot approach to data centers](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), with Denver pausing new development until 2027. GOP nominee [Victor Marx called for more water storage](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) to prepare for drought. Xcel won a $157 million rate hike, [adding about $5/month to bills](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Denver's Chamber president warned rising [socialist influence could clash with business realities](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Hunting groups threatened to [sue over a new furbearer bag](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) limit passed without real public comment. And a Do No Harm report found the state's I Matter program spent nearly [$5 million on youth-targeted ads](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) telling minors 12 and older they can get free counseling without parental consent.
**🗣️ Commentary Spotlight...** Cory Gaines criticized a CSU study backing the furbearer bag limit, arguing its [self-selected survey ignored the rural-urban divide](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) and its wording was designed to steer respondents toward stricter answers.
This is your Mountain Minute for Friday, August 21, 2026.
– Team RMV

**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[Colorado funded ads telling kids they can get therapy without parental consent](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
A child in Colorado can sign up for state-funded therapy at age 12 without a parent knowing. That is not a loophole. It is how the program is built.
The program is called I Matter.
It offers up to six free counseling sessions to any young person 18 or under, or up to 21 for those receiving special-education services, and is delivered mostly by telehealth.
According to a report released this month by the medical advocacy group Do No Harm, the state funded a youth-targeted advertising push built around one message. Youth 12 and older don’t need a parent to sign off.
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|

**[A change order, not an amendment: How Denver moved $18 million past City Council](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
_A city audit reveals how Denver's signature downtown project ballooned by $18 million without ever facing a council vote, exposing a loophole officials decline to close._
* **A budget gap that skipped oversight:** Denver's 16th Street Improvement Project grew from a $149 million council-approved budget to $175.6 million after crews hit an unmapped brick sewer, but because the resulting $18 million settlement was structured as a "change order" rather than a formal contract "amendment," it never required City Council approval under the city's own rules.
* **A loophole city officials defend:** Denver Auditor Timothy O'Brien found no mechanism exists to convert a large change order into a council-reviewed amendment, warning that without one, "construction projects can continue circumventing City Council review" — yet the Department of Transportation & Infrastructure disagreed with the fix, insisting it followed proper legal guidance.
* **Missed deadlines and unenforced penalties:** Only one of the project's 14 blocks finished on time, and the city chose not to collect roughly $1.03 million in contractually available penalties for missed deadlines, while auditors also found the department couldn't produce records showing why the contractor was competitively selected in the first place.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**

Republican Wetland Destruction Exacerbated Massive Floods After 22+ years of one-party Republican control, Indiana’s wetlands network is smaller than ever before, and has lost considerable acreage in the past ten years alone. As our state experiences more and more historic flooding and weather events, the need for these natural water collection reservoirs will only grow. This month’s floods reminded Indiana of the danger of paving over wetlands that protect property and lives from stormwaters. In 2021, Republicans targeted isolated wetlands and allowed them to be developed with little-to-no state oversight. In 2024, the Republican supermajority went even further by eliminating protections for a much larger number of wetlands, and limiting what local governments can do to protect them. These irresponsible policies exacerbatedthe catastrophic flooding Indiana is currently experiencing. It’s time to elect new leadership and more Democratic state legislators who understand the value and importance of our state’s wetlands. Ford is a strong, competitive candidate that could flip this seat in November. It’s time to end Victoria Spartz’s time in Congress, and the dysfunction she promotes in Washington. J.D. |
Peter,
North Carolina GOP state supreme court nominee Sarah Stevens has been named as an attendee at a fundraiser hosted by a man named Harvey West, a MAGA operative and convicted child sex offender.
According to reporting by the Asheville Watchdog, when Harvey West was a 28-year-old police officer, he was arrested and charged with the statutory rape of three girls, two aged 14 and one aged 16.
West pled guilty to 16 lesser charges of "taking indecent liberties with a child" and served six years in prison.
In 2018 after North Carolina began partisan elections for judges, West founded his annual "North Carolina Judicial Picnic" that has drawn many of the state's most prominent Republicans to his home for a fundraiser, including GOP US Senate nominee Michael Whatley -- and GOP State Supreme Court nominee Sarah Stevens.
---
| [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001z_Fw1U0nf8v_m9aYJAJzozAPdaWNmBXN3M95SS7ojqWcVztKCkSX9P-KdzmY2-OIyWlFoQFjrZzQEVmV5CVc6TmVC7fSVaYfvQY3hu8P9FAt1-mIJym4c7nBb4tvLVuluSVDg4Pm8a_4HjaykzXbnRQ_F9_LpFrt0XFqU56rxB23g2vzel9iK9qIhqY2uuLOtQklf_PbMUpD6DJEgV7ist4tF-dirDoMuwuzaZmiQMQ=&c=hnPfDFkFSxRcXJ739t6QVGeIoYCljgn34Er2kjQTduDc_x5dLHmw2g==&ch=tiKsnfNYQqEtsCxtUu0_pUlNErtp_-JBR7DlkXgLV6sS7-HTArUrgg==)
---
Even fellow conservatives have publicly condemned GOP candidates' participation in West's fundraisers. One Republican activist said: "Sarah Stevens, I guarantee you, today is regretting that she attended that picnic...It's going to cost her her election. She will lose to Anita Earls."
People who have made mistakes and served their time certainly deserve second chances. But associating with sex offenders, particularly those implicated in serious and disturbing crimes involving children as young as 14, calls into question the judgment of candidates for public office -- ESPECIALLY a candidate running to serve on the state's highest court.
Sarah Stevens is not fit to rule on the NC Supreme Court. We have to rally and throw everything we've got into re-electing and retaining Justice Anita Earls, a woman of integrity and principles who has already proven herself to be a fair and competent judge.
As a bonus, if Justice Earls wins and retains her seat this year then three GOP justices will be on the ballot in 2028, giving Democrats a golden opportunity to flip control of this court entirely in a single election. But we have to win in November first.
[Someone who associates with convicted child sex offenders has no place serving on the bench. clean_body: Someone who associates with convicted child sex offenders has no place serving on the bench. | | | | | == | Peter, North Carolina GOP state supreme court nominee Sarah Stevens has been named as an attendee at a fundraiser hosted by a man named Harvey West, a MAGA operative and convicted child sex offender. According to reporting by the Asheville Watchdog, when Harvey West was a 28-year-old police officer, he was arrested and charged with the statutory rape of three girls, two aged 14 and one aged 16. West pled guilty to 16 lesser charges of "taking indecent liberties with a child" and served six years in prison. In 2018 after North Carolina began partisan elections for judges, West founded his annual "North Carolina Judicial Picnic" that has drawn many of the state's most prominent Republicans to his home for a fundraiser, including GOP US Senate nominee Michael Whatley -- and GOP State Supreme Court nominee Sarah Stevens. | == Even fellow conservatives have publicly condemned GOP candidates' participation in West's fundraisers. One Republican activist said: "Sarah Stevens, I guarantee you, today is regretting that she attended that picnic...It's going to cost her her election. She will lose to Anita Earls." People who have made mistakes and served their time certainly deserve second chances. But associating with sex offenders, particularly those implicated in serious and disturbing crimes involving children as young as 14, calls into question the judgment of candidates for public office -- ESPECIALLY a candidate running to serve on the state's highest court. Sarah Stevens is not fit to rule on the NC Supreme Court. We have to rally and throw everything we've got into re-electing and retaining Justice Anita Earls, a woman of integrity and principles who has already proven herself to be a fair and competent judge. As a bonus, if Justice Earls wins and retains her seat this year then three GOP justices will be on the ballot in 2028, giving Democrats a golden opportunity to flip control of this court entirely in a single election. | | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | | | | Your Kids Could Owe More in 2026 Than You Think! The discussion contrasted the resistance to data centers with Maine's embrace of wind and solar projects, arguing that green-energy subsidies have raised costs while rewarding politically connected interests. Nuclear power, natural gas access and data centers could offer a more serious path to lower electricity prices, new investment and long-term economic growth.

| | | | Fellow Conservative, If you haven’t heard about “See You at the Library Day” on Fox News or Newsmax or your other favorite news sources, **[please let me tell you why it’s so critical.](http://links.justandfreegop.com/u/click?_t=8ca5ef3d31cc43bcb1fbe6968d953911&_m=ffac037d07be4773b60c6fe05ff1357c&_e=Jed56gT-vtySLVll-L6f1RsljRzavHI3upg8qathUlUIunwA3BitL8QJg9hTAUQq7Su07IrHp4_-_zTrRY9iYXAYZzPoY26uJKkeQh9-FG00HCvTvASVfdr9wG-IwHyUf2rDWiqxXlRnqd98Kz6enQEUPSOLCKrxely5tg0m36F3hK25YG-vWgpumIulS-p7vtGAYHSipTsHdohQK3EdpLWDmFlr6Es7ghXcHpZgL8xTGA0Tx42HJZ9V3YJkgMXRfgwlMQUMLw5Mt_CGCzJnHL_Ird6hFUKh_BE07rJXJTqNXee10acRhnXQyad21Y-XAPX5-IPyDOptqKlCfhHCcEGGvtH3MsmqpFqPU58LcLlGuaN1HHM0pMkdhXuNnvcPipS3mfOzzpQ7ZSIEB-pyyPpY8Swld3ofeLS9wutOS0hw38RCSFE9wGfle8beqsa1xhojyhm2nCKjEwOA4zNmTSoBcyjTajIwfZT1vjCbpc7CPFH6aUha6MQhYj2C4xs6JFnGt4UX0XsW29RzQNM4HzqrDi8Y6QZVL2y7T49jP7SkOHDsdwGTHINU6u6FD7xbPmhX8QODusP514Heb4Y2ZQv7-5i_7vZQ0pBsCp664oyhxf8CE5tcvOenXLQr5u9IRrQEZTw2PJea3e-0S7xqst5cDH7mPKMWpp46MiJ-G1-Sfnw_duUb8UZYTV-Aewjv)** Back when you were growing up, you may remember lazy Saturdays at the library with a kind but stern librarian.She would fill your mind with classics like _Pat the Bunny_ and _The Little Engine That Could_. And eventually you got old enough to roam by yourself and discover adventures like the _Three Musketeers_ , _Treasure Island_ and _Charlotte’s Web_.**But today, all that has changed.** Instead of filling children with wholesome stories, the president of the American Library Association (ALA) says libraries should be used to address ‘systemic racism’ and elevate ‘BIPOC and GLBTQR+ writers and voices.’ Radical librarians call _Adventures of Huckleberry Finn_ and _To Kill a Mockingbird_ “racist.” They’ve stripped Laura Ingalls Wilder’s name from a prestigious book award because of her “problematic’ _Little House_ series.And they bring in men wearing full makeup, dresses, and high heels for “Drag Queen Story Hours” where books like these are read to children of all ages... _A is for Activist._ An ABC board book for “families who want their kids to grow up in a space that is unapologetic about activism, environmental justice, civil rights, LGBTQ rights, and everything else that activists believe in and fight for.” _Woke Baby._ “For all the littlest progressives, waking up to seize a new day of justice and activism. Woke babies raise their fists in the air. Woke babies cry out for justice. Woke babies grow up to change the world.” _Prince and Knight._ The “premier queer-friendly fairy tale” about a prince who marries a knight instead of a princess. And _The Hips on the Drag Queens Go Swish, Swish, Swish._ A “family-friendly celebration of drag” that encourages children to “work it.”I wish I could tell you this was only happening in places like New York City and San Francisco...but that’s just not true.

Or maybe you’ve noticed the “Teen Zone” which is really meant to be a “parent-free” zone.The “Teen Zone” is filled with books like: _Rick_ about a cross-dressing Grandpa, _Melissa_ filled with graphic nudity, and _Darkstalker_ featuring gory violence and domestic abuse.**But here’s what’s really alarming.** We can’t just sit back and say, “Well, I’ll just make sure my family doesn’t go to “Drag Queen Story Hour” and we won’t check out those inappropriate books.”That may be good for your family -- for now.**But meanwhile, the ALA uses our taxpayer-funded libraries to lure in millions of _other_ children who grow up to be the very activists who are destroying our country and conservative values!** _**[I hope you see why I need your help today.](http://links.justandfreegop.com/u/click?_t=8ca5ef3d31cc43bcb1fbe6968d953911&_m=ffac037d07be4773b60c6fe05ff1357c&_e=Jed56gT-vtySLVll-L6f1RsljRzavHI3upg8qathUlUIunwA3BitL8QJg9hTAUQq7Su07IrHp4_-_zTrRY9iYXAYZzPoY26uJKkeQh9-FG00HCvTvASVfdr9wG-IwHyUf2rDWiqxXlRnqd98Kz6enQEUPSOLCKrxely5tg0m36F3hK25YG-vWgpumIulS-p7vtGAYHSipTsHdohQK3EdpLWDmFlr6Es7ghXcHpZgL8zb7VDd205T9ZXhXOsKrpNqSizijeWLTkP1Y-TW77htWTAWiepU4_eWItnoVgtWa_jZRKPHTzSVWUiabfFqPA_xhTcANAoGcAcQV0hcX-Ihdg-V9E-J3t_T3qSLRrisLyV6dgsR_A-MfZ3MLWmSCsMW-n7j4q2nglM4AvFkxK64GyxO3OWn5uXs1K2PFeVUIFDvHz9BPkm-a8zWPH8IZ4U1Zkg3yfQwihnbJ-7qAwEnY4S1rRd3ZOiX2OPEIJH2sjQ65WGxUWa_xoZFUS_i4_WQqwr2Vl13zYpyIj7qfKwKyzU-JcInbhpnFL9foR9pZ7IE3bgwGFHbXrAJmrzsn9qA1vddWdd63-djUrIw8YZ7PuQA0jJsiPT5hwRaj2n6jJbZHrs7i9gQNEmBmHGthRZecMElyutTn6odkVK3SkRENUVx4mOGaMvU1sKFqx3yGjs4YXXMf5InVyaydz0GyrPU) **_My name is Kirk Cameron. Maybe you recognize me from the 1980’s family sitcom “Growing Pains” or from my work in inspirational movies like “Fireproof” and “Left Behind.”I know firsthand how dangerous it is to be indoctrinated by leftist values. Pride almost took me down as a young actor in Hollywood.But the gospel saved me. I love being an actor, but what’s far more important is being a husband, dad, grandad, and a Christian.When I saw what book publishers and libraries were doing to indoctrinate children with anti-God, anti-family, anti-America messages, I knew I had a duty to take action.So, I wrote a little book called “As You Grow” to teach children how to grow in wisdom through the fruit of the spirit.**Then I decided to go one step further and counter those awful “Drag Queen Story Hours” with _conservative Story Hours_ filled with the classic books you and I grew up with, plus new wholesome books like mine that captivate children with lessons in bravery, honesty, kindness, and patriotism.**And boy, the ALA and radical librarians didn’t like that one bit. >> Over 50 libraries rejected my request to host our Story Hour.>> The ALA helped local libraries scheme ways to keep me out including booking all the event rooms for themselves. >> Social media blew up with attacks: I was compared to a Nazi (that’s original), my publisher was accused of trying to “confuse and demoralize children,” supporters were described as “bored moms/busybodies who need something to feel good about,” and on and on.I can’t even print most things these radicals said because it’s so vile. But here’s the greatest part...From there, parents and grandparents started asking how they could host “Story Hours” of their own.And that’s how the nationwide “See You at the Library” movement was born.Last year, committed conservatives just like you booked event rooms at 201 libraries in 46 states. clean_body: We can't surrender our librariesAnd The Hips on the Drag Queens Go Swish, Swish, Swish. | | | | Fellow Conservative, If you haven’t heard about “See You at the Library Day” on Fox News or Newsmax or your other favorite news sources, Back when you were growing up, you may remember lazy Saturdays at the library with a kind but stern librarian.She would fill your mind with classics like Pat the Bunny and The Little Engine That Could. And eventually you got old enough to roam by yourself and discover adventures like the Three Musketeers , Treasure Island and Charlotte’s Web.But today, all that has changed. Instead of filling children with wholesome stories, the president of the American Library Association (ALA) says libraries should be used to address ‘systemic racism’ and elevate ‘BIPOC and GLBTQR+ writers and voices.’ Radical librarians call Adventures of Huckleberry Finn and To Kill a Mockingbird “racist.” They’ve stripped Laura Ingalls Wilder’s name from a prestigious book award because of her “problematic’ Little House series.And they bring in men wearing full makeup, dresses, and high heels for “Drag Queen Story Hours” where books like these are read to children of all ages... A is for Activist. An ABC board book for “families who want their kids to grow up in a space that is unapologetic about activism, environmental justice, civil rights, LGBTQ rights, and everything else that activists believe in and fight for.” Woke Baby. “For all the littlest progressives, waking up to seize a new day of justice and activism. Woke babies raise their fists in the air. Woke babies cry out for justice. Woke babies grow up to change the world.” Prince and Knight. The “premier queer-friendly fairy tale” about a prince who marries a knight instead of a princess. And The Hips on the Drag Queens Go Swish, Swish, Swish. A “family-friendly celebration of drag” that encourages children to “work it.”I wish I could tell you this was only happening in places like New York City and San Francisco...but that’s just not true. THIS IS A MAN leading “Drag Queen Story Hour” For decades, the ultra-liberal Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation and George Soros’ Open Society have spent millions radicalizing the ALA. And as a result, a new generation of pink-haired, activist librarians have made it their mission to fill library shelves with anti-American, LGBTQ-friendly, and explicitly sexual content. Maybe you’ve noticed all the displays at your own library celebrating Pride Month or elevating ‘the environment’ to a type of religion. Or maybe you’ve noticed the “Teen Zone” which is really meant to be a “parent-free” zone.The “Teen Zone” is filled with books like: Rick about a cross-dressing Grandpa, Melissa filled with graphic nudity, and Darkstalker featuring gory violence and domestic abuse.But here’s what’s really alarming. We can’t just sit back and say, “Well, I’ll just make sure my family doesn’t go to “Drag Queen Story Hour” and we won’t check out those inappropriate books.”That may be good for your family -- for now.But meanwhile, the ALA uses our taxpayer-funded libraries to lure in millions of other children who grow up to be the very activists who are destroying our country and conservative values! My name is Kirk Cameron. Maybe you recognize me from the 1980’s family sitcom “Growing Pains” or from my work in inspirational movies like “Fireproof” and “Left Behind.”I know firsthand how dangerous it is to be indoctrinated by leftist values. Pride almost took me down as a young actor in Hollywood.But the gospel saved me. I love being an actor, but what’s far more important is being a husband, dad, grandad, and a Christian.When I saw what book publishers and libraries were doing to indoctrinate children with anti-God, anti-family, anti-America messages, I knew I had a duty to take action.So, I wrote a little book called “As You Grow” to teach children how to grow in wisdom through the fruit of the spirit.Then I decided to go one step further and counter those awful “Drag Queen Story Hours” with conservative Story Hours filled with the classic books you and I grew up with, plus new wholesome books like mine that captivate children with lessons in bravery, honesty, kindness, and patriotism.And boy, the ALA and radical librarians didn’t like that one bit. >> Over 50 libraries rejected my request to host our Story Hour.>> The ALA helped local libraries scheme ways to keep me out including booking all the event rooms for themselves. >> Social media blew up with attacks: I was compared to a Nazi (that’s original), my publisher was accused of trying to “confuse and demoralize children,” supporters were described as “bored moms/busybodies who need something to feel good about,” and on and on.I can’t even print most things these radicals said because it’s so vile. In the end I got two libraries to reverse course by reminding them that their censorship violated the Constitution of the United States.And thousands of parents and grandparents brought their little ones to those “Story Hours” where we pledged allegiance to the flag, sang “God Bless America”, and read wholesome and Godly books. It was incredible. But here’s the greatest part...From there, parents and grandparents started asking how they could host “Story Hours” of their own.And that’s how the nationwide “See You at the Library” movement was born.Last year, committed conservatives just like you booked event rooms at 201 libraries in 46 states. On the same day, across America hundreds of “Story Hours”filled children’s hearts with goodness, gratitude, and God.Conservative parents, grandparents, and patriots stood together for a very simple mission -- to reject the Left’s radical ideas and reclaim childhood innocence in America’s libraries. The exact date will soon be announced. And before then, I need you! The response from parents, grandparents, and patriots who want to host “Story Hours” has been overwhelming.That’s a very good thing.But it’s going to be a big undertaking and expensive to give these volunteers the resources they need to hold “Story Hours” for 250,000 children. BRAVE for Good was started by BRAVE Books -- the small Christian publisher of my book “As You Grow” –- because so many patriots were asking how they could help “See You at the Library Day” with a tax-deductible gift.Your sponsorship gift helps send a ‘Story Hour Kit’ to every parent, grandparent, and patriot who’s organizing a “See You at the Library” event. The kit includes everything they need to bring your conservative values back into our public libraries: instructions for booking their library space and running their Story Hour, small American flags for little ones, fun stickers, wholesome books, Bible memory verse cards, and other specialty items. Your sponsorship gift is the only way we can fund our “Story Hours” for 250,000 children to counter the radical leftists who’ve taken control of our libraries. We don’t have the millions behind us like the giant taxpayer-funded ALA. Singlehandedly, you’ll be reaching 50 children with our wholesome, Godly, and patriotic message. Thank you! God Bless You and God Bless America,Kirk Cameron | | | 100 I-45 N 260Conroe, TX 77301

It’s official – the path back to national sanity runs through our district, Virginia's Fighting Fifth!

**That’s right, the DCCC has just elevated our race to the coveted Red to Blue status, given to the highest tier of pick-up opportunities needed to reclaim a Democratic majority.**

This has been a huge week of momentum, starting with a new poll that shows our months of barnstorming the district have paid off.

**[If you love this momentum as much as I do, don’t bother reading the rest of this email. Just click here to split a donation between my campaign and Tim Kaine's Common Ground PAC so we can reach the voters who will do the rest. Let’s leave nothing on the table to ensure we reclaim this seat for the people of the Fighting Fifth.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137686893/641593087/1139833646?refcode=260821em_tp&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDQvMS84ODkyNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5ZTEzZGRhNi1hYjlkLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=GPhscqw1Bnkr8n4Uqo-9njHn9I142vEBTuUr-LuirqY=)** **

Mike Lawler has faced Democratic politicians before, Peter. But he’s never faced someone like me. He and I are about the same age. We both grew up in the Hudson Valley. And for the last twenty years, while he’s been a political operative finding every way possible to profit off of democracy, I’ve been leading America’s sons and daughters in defense of it. I went to West Point after 9/11. That’s why I’m running for Congress. body:
The next couple months will be an all-out sprint — and these are races that could get overlooked
| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137687339/641594351/-3547583?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjRhZGI0NmJmLWFkOWQtZjExMS05YjMzLTAwMGQzYTExZmEzMCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=UUkxRgISMHwGvKaYPHc14SvRBgS_HXAhwY37ngC8utU=&emci=e0698a48-9d9d-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=4adb46bf-ad9d-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=8431045)

Peter, This Tuesday will mark exactly 10 weeks until Election Day. We’ll have just 10 weeks left to help power our Democracy Defenders to victory — in over a dozen states across the country. Just 10 weeks left to elect leaders who can counter or overturn Republican gerrymanders, shut down anti-voter legislation, stop future MAGA map manipulation ahead of 2028, and achieve or protect fair-minded state supreme court majorities that can ensure a level playing field. **We’re fighting in the most critical state-level races — which run the risk of getting overlooked in an election cycle dominated by D.C.
